# GB-64: Benchwork State Persistence, Bulk Operations & Playwright E2E Quality Gate

> **Status:** Ready  
> **Target Scope:** `benchwork` (`benchwork-core`, `benchwork-cli`, `benchwork/web`)  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs`, `.ts`, and `.tsx` files.  
> 2. Zero-loss reload persistence: page refresh never resets active tabs, sub-view modes, or filter state.  
> 3. Atomic bulk mutations: batch task archiving must atomically update stores and broadcast live DAG updates.  
> 4. Full browser E2E test verification via Playwright in `benchwork/web`.  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

Benchwork currently suffers from three major usability and reliability issues:
1. **Viewport & Sub-View State Loss on Refresh:**
   * Navigating to Kanban or List view and refreshing the browser resets the view back to Panel 2 CAD DAG View.
   * Active filters (e.g. status, repo, kind) and sidebar width are wiped on reload.
2. **Lack of Bulk Archiving:**
   * Archiving only exists as a single-task button inside the task inspection drawer; cleaning up dozens of completed tasks requires dozens of manual drawer interactions.
3. **No Automated End-to-End Browser Testing:**
   * `benchwork/web` lacks test coverage for UI interactions, SSE streaming chat, and state restoration, making regressions easy to introduce.

---

## 2. Architecture & File Layout

```text
benchwork/crates/
├── benchwork-cli/src/daemon/
│   └── routes_dag.rs         # POST /api/v1/dag/bulk-archive endpoint (<230 LOC)
└── benchwork-core/src/
    └── dag_service.rs        # Bulk archive routing to member stores (<240 LOC)

benchwork/web/
├── playwright.config.ts      # Playwright test harness configuration (<80 LOC)
├── e2e/
│   ├── persistence.spec.ts   # Reload and URL hash persistence tests (<160 LOC)
│   ├── benji_chat.spec.ts    # Streaming chat & context injection tests (<180 LOC)
│   └── bulk_archive.spec.ts  # Multi-select and bulk archiving tests (<150 LOC)
└── src/
    ├── hooks/
    │   ├── usePersistentState.ts # LocalStorage + URL hash sync hook (<120 LOC)
    │   └── useBulkSelection.ts   # Multi-select ID tracking hook (<110 LOC)
    └── components/
        └── dag/
            ├── BulkActionBar.tsx     # Floating multi-action toolbar (<160 LOC)
            ├── TaskTableView.tsx     # List view with checkboxes (<230 LOC)
            └── KanbanBoardView.tsx   # Kanban view with checkboxes (<240 LOC)
```

---

## 3. Subtasks & Breakdown

* **GB-65 (Feature, P1):** LocalStorage and URL hash persistence for panel navigation, sub-view modes, and sidebar state.
* **GB-66 (Feature, P1):** Bulk task multi-select and batch archiving in DagBoard list and kanban views.
* **GB-67 (Feature, P1):** Automated Playwright E2E test suite in benchwork/web.

---

## 4. Execution Plan & Verification Gates

### Step 1: Subtask GB-65 (State Persistence)
* Implement `usePersistentState` hook synchronizing `localStorage` with `window.location.hash`.
* Bind active tab (`#docs`, `#dag`, `#xray`, `#hub`), sub-view (`#dag/dag`, `#dag/kanban`, `#dag/list`), filters, and Benji layout.
* *Verification Gate:* Manual browser reload & unit test

# GB-66: Bulk Task Multi-Select and Batch Archiving in DagBoard

> **Status:** Ready  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-64`  
> **Target Scope:** `benchwork` (`benchwork-core`, `benchwork-cli`, `benchwork/web`)  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs`, `.ts`, and `.tsx` files.  
> 2. Atomic multi-repo archive dispatch: batch archiving must resolve governing store per ticket (`ws.resolve_governing_store_name`).  
> 3. Zero orphaned UI state: bulk selection clears automatically after successful execution.  
> 4. Immediate WebSocket broadcast: live DAG updates notify all connected clients instantly.  

---

## 1. Overview & Objectives

In production workflows, managing hundreds of tasks requires bulk operations. Currently, tasks must be opened one-by-one in the drawer to archive them.

GB-66 accomplishes:
1. Adds `POST /api/v1/dag/bulk-archive` to `benchwork-cli` and `benchwork-core`.
2. Implements a multi-select state manager in `benchwork/web` (`useBulkSelection`).
3. Adds row checkboxes and "Select All" to `TaskTableView` (List view).
4. Adds card selection checkboxes and column-level select controls to `KanbanBoardView`.
5. Renders a fixed floating `BulkActionBar` showing selection count, "Archive Selected", and "Clear Selection" buttons.

---

## 2. API Contract & Data Types

```rust
// POST /api/v1/dag/bulk-archive
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BulkArchiveRequest {
    pub task_ids: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BulkArchiveResponse {
    pub archived_count: usize,
    pub errors: Vec<String>,
}
```

---

## 3. Verification Steps

1. Navigate to List view; select 3 tasks using checkboxes.
2. Verify `BulkActionBar` appears displaying "3 tasks selected".
3. Click "Archive Selected"; verify tasks disappear from active list and appear when "Include Archived" is toggled.
4. Verify `POST /api/v1/dag/bulk-archive` executes cleanly in daemon logs.
5. Run `cargo test -p benchwork-cli --lib daemon::routes_dag::tests`.

> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic safety: no `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` in production library paths (`thiserror`).  
> 3. Clean terminal hygiene: child processes (`git`, `cargo`) never dump raw stdout/stderr directly to console handles; output is captured, structured, and only surfaced on failure or `--verbose`.  
> 4. Decoupled domain engine: `outfeed-core` defines a lightweight `ProgressReporter` trait / observer so CLI rendering (`indicatif`) does not leak into library/MCP consumers.  
> 5. Non-TTY resilience: dynamic spinners gracefully degrade to clean milestone lines when not on an interactive TTY, and are completely suppressed in `--json` and `-q`.  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

Currently, when executing batch commands across the meta-harness such as `outfeed push --all` or `outfeed install --all`, child processes (`git push`, `cargo install`) run directly via `.status()`, inheriting stdout and stderr from the parent terminal.

This causes raw subprocess messages (such as 20 consecutive un-prefixed lines of `Everything up-to-date`) to stream into the terminal with no repository indication, before outfeed suddenly dumps its completion emojis at the very end:
```text
➜  neurosymbolic-suite git:(main) outfeed push --all
Everything up-to-date
Everything up-to-date
... (20 lines) ...
🚀 miter: pushed branch 'main' and tag 'v0.1.0-beta.1' to origin
🚀 storypole: pushed branch 'main' and tag 'v0.1.0-beta.2' to origin
```

Furthermore, outfeed lacks unified verbosity controls (`-v`, `-vv`, `-q`), making it impossible to quiet down progress during automation or inspect child command details without hacking debug prints.

`GB-68` resolves this across all multi-repo commands (`push`, `install`, `release`, `clean`, `publish`):
1. **Dynamic Progress & Spinners**: Uses `indicatif` (v0.18, matching `miter`) with `MultiProgress` and dynamic per-repo spinners (`⠋`) transitioning into clean colored status icons (`✔`, `✖`, `⊘`).
2. **Subprocess Capturing**: Standardizes child process execution to buffer stdout and stderr. On success in normal mode, the terminal remains clean. On error, or with `-v` (verbose), the buffered output is printed indented and prefixed with the repo name (e.g. `  [miter] Everything up-to-date`).
3. **Standard Verbosity Flags**:
   - Default: clean interactive spinners, warning-level logs.
   - `-v, --verbose` (counted): `-v` enables info logs + repo-prefixed child output; `-vv` enables debug tracing.
   - `-q, --quiet`: suppresses all non-essential output, spinners, and progress bars; emits only errors.
   - `--json`: machine-readable output with progress bars automatically hidden.
4. **TTY / CI Auto-Detection**: Detects `is_terminal()`; renders dynamic spinners on interactive terminals, linear milestone lines in non-TTY/CI, and hides spinners entirely in quiet/JSON modes.

---

## 2. Resolved Architectural Decisions (from /grill-me)

| Decision ID | Question | Chosen Option | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2f8dd71d` | Visual progress style and engine | `indicatif MultiProgress / Spinners` | Dynamic spinners for active repos showing current action, settling into clean status lines; aligns with `indicatif 0.18` already in workspace (`miter`). |
| `95d45ab7` | Subprocess stdout/stderr handling | `Capture by default; display on error or verbose` | Keeps terminal clean during normal execution; displays full diagnostics indented by repo on failure or `-v`. |
| `d51a03c0` | CLI verbosity flag convention | `Multi-level -v/-vv count + -q/--quiet` | Standard Rust CLI pattern (`-q` quiet, default clean spinners, `-v` verbose with child output, `-vv` debug tracing). |
| `5ba1a0b9` | Non-interactive / CI / pipes behavior | `Auto-detect TTY: dynamic on TTY, linear on non-TTY, hidden in quiet/json` | Prevents ANSI redraw corruption in CI logs or pipes while retaining interactive richness on real terminals. |
| `86aa8bf2` | Rollout scope across subcommands | `Full suite rollout (push, install, release, clean, publish)` | Delivers consistent developer experience across all multi-repo operations. |
| `23502b4c` | Terminal iconography & styling aesthetic | `Modern CLI styling (⠋, ✔, ✖, ⊘)` | Clean, subtle modern CLI aesthetic matching modern developer tools like cargo, gh, and docker. |

---

## 3. Architecture & File Layout

```text
outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/
├── progress.rs        # ProgressReporter trait, NoopProgress, and RepoProgressEvent (<150 LOC)
├── cmd.rs             # Subprocess runner capturing stdout/stderr into CommandOutput (<150 LOC)
├── push.rs            # Updated push_repo/push_all to use runner and ProgressReporter (<200 LOC)
├── install.rs         # Updated install_repo/install_all to use runner and reporter (<200 LOC)
├── publish.rs         # Updated publish_repo to use runner and reporter (<200 LOC)
├── clean.rs           # Updated clean_workspace to report progress (<200 LOC)
└── lib.rs             # Re-exports progress types and CommandOutput

outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli/src/
├── args/
│   └── mod.rs         # Add global -v/--verbose (count) and -q/--quiet flags (<150 LOC)
├── progress/
│   ├── mod.rs         # Progress factory returning appropriate reporter based on TTY/flags (<100 LOC)
│   ├── multi.rs       # indicatif MultiProgress reporter for interactive terminals (<200 LOC)
│   └── text.rs        # Plain milestone-line reporter for non-TTY/CI (<120 LOC)
├── commands/
│   ├── push.rs        # Wire progress reporter and verbosity (<120 LOC)
│   ├── install.rs     # Wire progress reporter and verbosity (<120 LOC)
│   ├── clean.rs       # Wire progress reporter and verbosity (<120 LOC)
│   ├── publish.rs     # Wire progress reporter and verbosity (<120 LOC)
│   └── release.rs     # Wire progress reporter and verbosity (<150 LOC)
└── main.rs            # Initialize tracing-subscriber dynamically from verbosity flags (<100 LOC)
```

---

## 4. Execution Steps & Verification Gates

1. **Step 1: Core Progress Observer & Subprocess Runner (`outfeed-core`)**
   - Define `ProgressReporter` trait and event models in `outfeed-core/src/progress.rs`.
   - Implement `run_command` in `outfeed-core/src/cmd.rs` capturing stdout/stderr into `CommandOutput`.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo check -p outfeed-core` and unit tests in `crates/outfeed-core/tests`.

2. **Step 2: Core Subcommand Adaptation (`outfeed-core`)**
   - Update `push.rs`, `install.rs`, `publish.rs`, and `clean.rs` to execute via `cmd.rs` and notify `ProgressReporter`.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.

3. **Step 3: CLI Progress Reporter & Verbosity Setup (`outfeed-cli`)**
   - Add `indicatif = "0.18"` to `outfeed-cli/Cargo.toml`.
   - Implement interactive `MultiProgress` and non-TTY fallback in `outfeed-cli/src/progress/`.
   - Add `-v` / `-vv` (count) and `-q` (flag) to `outfeed-cli/src/args/mod.rs` and configure `tracing-subscriber`.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo check -p outfeed-cli`.

4. **Step 4: CLI Subcommands Wiring (`outfeed-cli`)**
   - Wire reporter into `push`, `install`, `publish`, `clean`, and `release` CLI handlers.
   - Print repo-prefixed child output when `-v` is active or on error.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo clippy -p outfeed-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p outfeed-cli`.

5. **Step 5: End-to-End Suite Dogfooding & Binary Update**
   - Install binary into `~/.cargo/bin` via `cargo install --path outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli --force`.
   - Verify `outfeed push --all` (and `--dry-run`), testing interactive TTY, piped non-TTY, `-v`, and `-q`.
   - *Verification Gate:* Full Tier 3 workspace checks and Storypole verification receipt.

plan.summary: Enforce main branch, porcelain tree checks, and clean Storypole release commit
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-70: Enforce main branch, porcelain tree checks, and clean Storypole release commit

> **Status:** InProgress  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic safety: no `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` in production library paths (`thiserror`).  
> 3. Releases MUST occur strictly on branch `main` with a clean working tree across both target repo and meta-harness root.  
> 4. `outfeed apply` MUST NOT leave a dirty `.storypole/ledger.jsonl`: the release ticket must be created and certified before the release commit is made.  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Root Cause

1. **Branch Enforcement Gap**:
   `OutfeedError::InvalidBranch(String)` was defined in `error.rs`, but `assert_main_branch` was never implemented or invoked in `plan_release` and `apply_release`. Furthermore, when targeting a member repository within a meta-harness, only the child directory was inspected, ignoring the parent workspace's active branch.

2. **Dirty Ledger on Release**:
   `apply_release` performed git commit and tag *before* creating and certifying the Storypole release ticket. As a result, the release ticket appended to `.storypole/ledger.jsonl` was uncommitted, leaving the working tree dirty immediately after release.

---

## 2. Implementation Steps

1. **Step 1: Implement `assert_main_branch` in `outfeed-core::git`**
   - Check `get_current_branch(repo_dir)? == "main"`.
   - Traverse upward to detect any enclosing parent Git repository (the meta-harness workspace root) and ensure it is also on `main` and has a clean working tree.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo check -p outfeed-core`.

2. **Step 2: Enforce checks in `plan_release` and `apply_release`**
   - Call `assert_main_branch(repo_dir)?` at the entry of both `plan_release` and `apply_release`.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.

3. **Step 3: Reorder Storypole Ticket Creation before Release Commit**
   - In `apply_release`, create and certify the Storypole release ticket *before* calling `create_release_commit_and_tag`.
   - `git add -A` within `create_release_commit_and_tag` will stage the updated `.storypole/ledger.jsonl` into the atomic release commit.
   - *Verification Gate:* `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.

4. **Step 4: Dogfooding & Binary Update**
   - Test `outfeed apply` and ensure working tree remains 100% clean (`git status` is empty).
   - Recompile and reinstall binary into `~/.cargo/bin`.

plan.design_markdown:
# GB-72: Add --all Suite-Wide Orchestration Flag to outfeed release

> **Status:** InProgress  
> **Parent Epic:** Release Delivery Infrastructure  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic error handling with strongly typed errors via `thiserror`.  
> 3. Clean fallback when individual repo is omitted (`default_value = "."`).  
> 4. Deterministic topological iteration order across the 10 suite tools.  

---

## 1. Overview & Objectives

`outfeed release` orchestrates the complete SemVer release pipeline (`plan` -> `apply` -> `install` -> `push` -> `publish`). While other subcommands (`install --all`, `status --all`, `push --all`) support suite-wide execution across all 10 repositories, `outfeed release` required a specific `<REPO>` argument and lacked an `--all` option.

`GB-72` adds:
1. `outfeed release --all`: Iterates through all 10 suite repositories (`SUITE_TOOLS`) in dependency order.
2. For each repository with unreleased commits, executes the full release pipeline; clean repositories are skipped.
3. Respects all flags (`--dry-run`, `--skip-install`, `--skip-push`, `--skip-publish`, `--json`).
4. Makes `<REPO>` optional (`default_value = "."`), allowing `outfeed release` within a repository directory or `outfeed release <REPO>` from root.

---

## 2. Implementation Steps

1. In `outfeed-core`:
   * Add `release_all(workspace_root: &Path, opts: &ReleaseOpts) -> Result<Vec<ReleaseSummary>, OutfeedError>` in `crates/outfeed-core/src/release.rs`.
   * Export `release_all` in `crates/outfeed-core/src/lib.rs`.
2. In `outfeed-cli`:
   * Update `ReleaseArgs` in `crates/outfeed-cli/src/args/release.rs` to add `#[arg(long)] pub all: bool` and make `repo` default to `"."`.
   * Update `handle_release` in `crates/outfeed-cli/src/commands/release.rs` to handle `args.all`.
   * Add unit/CLI test in `crates/outfeed-cli/tests/` or `crates/outfeed-core/tests/`.
3. Verification:
   * Tier 2 checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` in `outfeed`.
   * Test `outfeed release --all --dry-run` dogfooding.

plan.summary: GB-74: Implement outfeed clone and bootstrap commands for suite-wide and selective repo setup
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-74: Implement outfeed clone and bootstrap commands for suite-wide and selective repo setup

> **Status:** Ready  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic error handling with strongly typed errors via `thiserror`.  
> 3. Standalone independence: does not require submodules or complex gitdir pointers.  
> 4. Idempotent execution: existing repositories are detected, inspected, and skipped cleanly.  

---

## 1. Overview & Objectives

As the `gaugeblock` meta-harness evolves into the primary developer and contributor entrypoint (`gaugeblock/gaugeblock`), developers and agents need a first-class, reliable mechanism to clone and initialize member repositories.

Following the design directive to eliminate ad-hoc shell scripts and consolidate developer workflow under `outfeed`:
1. `outfeed clone` clones all 10 suite repositories (`--all`) or a specific subset of named tools (`outfeed clone miter storypole`).
2. Supports `--locked` to read `suite.lock` and checkout the pinned git tag or commit SHA for each cloned tool.
3. Supports protocol selection via `--protocol <ssh|https>` (default: `ssh`).
4. Supports `--install` to automatically build and install binaries to `~/.cargo/bin` upon clone completion.
5. Supports `--sync-mcp` to update Antigravity / Cline `mcp_config.json` after installation.
6. Integrates with `outfeed`'s progress reporting (`indicatif` spinners in interactive TTY, clean milestones in non-TTY).

---

## 2. CLI Interface & Flags

```bash
# Clone entire suite
outfeed clone --all

# Clone specific tools
outfeed clone miter storypole dado

# Clone entire suite pinned to exact suite.lock commits
outfeed clone --all --locked

# Clone via HTTPS instead of SSH
outfeed clone --all --protocol https

# Clone and immediately install binaries to PATH + sync Antigravity MCP
outfeed clone --all --install --sync-mcp

# Dry-run preview
outfeed clone --all --dry-run
```

---

## 3. Architecture & Module Design

### 3.1. `crates/outfeed-core/src/clone.rs` (<250 LOC)
* Types:
  - `CloneOpts`: `all: bool`, `locked: bool`, `protocol: GitProtocol`, `dry_run: bool`, `install: bool`, `sync_mcp: bool`.
  - `GitProtocol`: `Ssh`, `Https`.
  - `CloneSummary`: `repo: String`, `target_dir: PathBuf`, `status: CloneStatus` (Cloned, SkippedExisting, PinnedCommit).
* Functions:
  - `clone_repo(workspace_root: &Path, tool: &SuiteTool, opts: &CloneOpts, reporter: &dyn ProgressReporter) -> Result<CloneSummary, OutfeedError>`
  - `clone_suite(workspace_root: &Path, targets: &[&str], opts: &CloneOpts, reporter: &dyn ProgressReporter) -> Result<Vec<CloneSummary>, OutfeedError>`

### 3.2. `crates/outfeed-cli/src/args/clone.rs` (<120 LOC)
* Clap argument parser for `CloneArgs`.

### 3.3. `crates/outfeed-cli/src/commands/clone.rs` (<150 LOC)
* Command handler wiring `clone_suite`, spinner reporter, and optional post-clone install.

---

## 4. Verification Gates

1. **Tier 1:** `cargo check -p outfeed-core` and `cargo check -p outfeed-cli`.
2. **Tier 2:** `cargo clippy -p outfeed-core -p outfeed-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.
3. **Dogfooding:** Execute `outfeed clone --dry-run --all` in a scratch directory to verify clone URL generation and skipped repo detection.

plan.summary: GB-75: Implement outfeed sync to audit and align local checkouts with remotes or suite.lock
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-75: Implement outfeed sync to audit and align local checkouts with remotes or suite.lock

> **Status:** Ready  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic error handling with strongly typed errors via `thiserror`.  
> 3. Safe git execution: never overwrites uncommitted work or dirty working trees without explicit confirmation.  
> 4. Clean tabular and JSON reporting for human developers and Benchwork.  

---

## 1. Overview & Objectives

In a multi-repository workspace, developers and agents switch branches, make local changes, or need to align with newly landed releases. `outfeed sync` provides a unified multi-repo synchronization and alignment tool:

1. **Drift & Status Audit:** Inspects all 10 repositories, reporting current branch, dirty working tree status, unpushed commits, and distance from upstream `origin/main`.
2. **Upstream Synchronization (`--all`):** Fast-forward pulls latest upstream changes across all clean member repositories.
3. **Reproducible Alignment (`--locked`):** Checks out the exact commit SHAs pinned in `suite.lock`.
4. **Safety Invariants:** Refuses to pull or checkout if a repository has uncommitted changes (`git status --porcelain` check), reporting warnings clearly.

---

## 2. CLI Interface & Flags

```bash
# Audit status of all repositories without modifying anything
outfeed sync --status

# Pull latest upstream main across all clean repositories
outfeed sync --all

# Sync specific repositories
outfeed sync miter storypole

# Align all repositories to exact commits pinned in suite.lock
outfeed sync --all --locked

# Machine-readable output for Benchwork integration
outfeed sync --all --json
```

---

## 3. Architecture & Module Design

### 3.1. `crates/outfeed-core/src/sync.rs` (<250 LOC)
* Types:
  - `SyncOpts`: `all: bool`, `locked: bool`, `status_only: bool`, `dry_run: bool`.
  - `RepoSyncStatus`: `repo: String`, `branch: String`, `head_sha: String`, `dirty: bool`, `unpushed_count: usize`, `divergence: BranchDivergence`.
* Functions:
  - `audit_repo_sync(repo_dir: &Path) -> Result<RepoSyncStatus, OutfeedError>`
  - `sync_repo(repo_dir: &Path, opts: &SyncOpts, reporter: &dyn ProgressReporter) -> Result<RepoSyncStatus, OutfeedError>`
  - `sync_suite(workspace_root: &Path, targets: &[&str], opts: &SyncOpts, reporter: &dyn ProgressReporter) -> Result<Vec<RepoSyncStatus>, OutfeedError>`

### 3.2. `crates/outfeed-cli/src/args/sync.rs` (<100 LOC)
* Clap argument parser for `SyncArgs`.

### 3.3. `crates/outfeed-cli/src/commands/sync.rs` (<150 LOC)
* Handler rendering formatted status tables or JSON output.

---

## 4. Verification Gates

1. **Tier 1:** `cargo check -p outfeed-core` and `cargo check -p outfeed-cli`.
2. **Tier 2:** `cargo clippy -p outfeed-core -p outfeed-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.
3. **Dogfooding:** Execute `outfeed sync --status` across the active workspace and verify table formatting and dirty tree warnings.

plan.summary: GB-73: Orchestrate meta-harness suite release and suite.lock generation in outfeed
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-73: Orchestrate meta-harness suite release and suite.lock generation in outfeed

> **Status:** Ready  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic error handling with strongly typed errors via `thiserror`.  
> 3. Enforces clean porcelain tree checks before release tagging.  
> 4. Deterministic snapshot reproducibility via `suite.lock`.  

---

## 1. Overview & Objectives

While `outfeed release --all` (GB-72) iterates across the 10 member repositories to plan, apply, install, push, and publish individual crates, the meta-harness itself (`gaugeblock/gaugeblock`) requires an overarching release coordinator:

`outfeed release suite` (or `outfeed release --suite`):
1. Runs pre-flight verification across the workspace.
2. Gathers the latest verified tags, versions, and commit SHAs across all 10 member repositories.
3. Generates the canonical `suite.lock` manifest.
4. Verifies/updates root `CHANGELOG.md` with suite milestone highlights.
5. Commits `suite.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md` to `main`.
6. Creates the annotated git tag `suite-v<version>` (e.g., `suite-v0.1.0-beta.2`).
7. Pushes the release commit and tag to `origin` (`gaugeblock/gaugeblock`).
8. Generates a GitHub Release with changelog release notes.

---

## 2. CLI Interface & Flags

```bash
# Preview suite release without side effects
outfeed release suite --dry-run

# Run full suite release with explicit target version
outfeed release suite --version 0.1.0-beta.3

# Run suite release skipping push
outfeed release suite --skip-push
```

---

## 3. Architecture & Verification Gates

1. Core module: `crates/outfeed-core/src/suite_release.rs` (<250 LOC).
2. Manifest generation: writes TOML formatted `suite.lock` at workspace root.
3. Tier 2 gate: `cargo clippy -p outfeed-core -p outfeed-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p outfeed-core`.
4. Dogfooding: `outfeed release suite --dry-run`.

# GB-76: Refactor scripts/bootstrap.sh and Suite Setup Scripts to Wrap Outfeed Clone and Install

## Objective
Provide an idempotent, ergonomic entrypoint `scripts/bootstrap.sh` for new and existing developer environments in the `gaugeblock` meta-harness. The script bootstraps the seed `outfeed` CLI binary, and delegates repository cloning, dependency resolution, suite binary installation, and MCP server configuration directly to `outfeed clone` and `outfeed install`.

## Architecture & Invariants
1. **Submodule-Free Workspace (`suite.lock`):**
   - In accordance with the inherited architecture decision, member repositories are cloned as independent checkouts.
   - Pinned tags or commits defined in `suite.lock` can be automatically applied via `--locked`.
2. **Deterministic Seed Bootstrap:**
   - If `outfeed` is not already installed on `PATH`, `bootstrap.sh` verifies `cargo` and compiles `outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli` into `~/.cargo/bin`.
3. **Delegation to Dogfood CLI:**
   - Workflows delegate to `outfeed clone --all --install --sync-mcp` and `outfeed sync`.
   - Supports flag forwarding: `--protocol <ssh|https>`, `--locked`, `--no-install`, `--no-sync-mcp`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.

## Execution Plan
1. Create `scripts/bootstrap.sh` with robust error handling (`set -euo pipefail`), prerequisite checks, outfeed compilation fallback, and option parsing.
2. Ensure `scripts/bootstrap.sh` has executable permissions (`chmod +x`).
3. Refactor `scripts/install-suite.sh` to leverage `outfeed install --all` and `outfeed` built-in MCP sync capabilities.
4. Dogfood `scripts/bootstrap.sh --help` and dry-run execution.
5. Verify clean execution across workspace and finalize Storypole verification receipt.

# GB-77: Enhance Outfeed Release with Progress Reporting, --no-llm Flag, and Resilient Error Handling

## Objective
Provide real-time progress visibility during `outfeed release` and `outfeed release --all`, add a `--no-llm` / `--deterministic` flag across release commands for instant offline operation, and handle remote LLM synthesis timeouts and errors gracefully without hanging or spamming raw router traces.

## Problem Statement
When running `outfeed release --all`:
1. It silently evaluated repos until reaching `benchwork`, where Sawhorse attempted to call a failing remote LLM endpoint (`api.cline.bot` returned 500).
2. The user was left with no indication of which repository was being operated on or what phase was executing.
3. The process took over 20 seconds of retries and logged raw router `WARN` traces without application context.
4. There was no CLI flag to disable LLM synthesis and generate deterministic changelogs offline.

## Architecture & Invariants
1. **Progress Observability:**
   - `release_repo` and `release_all` accept `&dyn ProgressReporter`.
   - Each repository emits start, update (planning, synthesizing, committing, installing, pushing), and completion status (`Skipped` for clean checkouts, `Success` for released versions).
2. **Deterministic / Offline Execution:**
   - `ReleaseOpts`, `PlanOpts` include `no_llm: bool`.
   - `--no-llm` (alias `--deterministic`) flag available on `outfeed plan`, `outfeed apply`, and `outfeed release`.
   - When enabled, changelog generation directly invokes `format_release_section` without loading or querying Sawhorse.
3. **Resilient Synthesis Fallback:**
   - Wrap `call_sawhorse` in a 10-second timeout.
   - Catch errors and log a clean informative message before immediately returning the deterministic changelog.
4. **Code Quality Invariants:**
   - Hard 250 LOC file limit across all Rust source files.
   - Tier 2 clippy and unit test verification.

## Execution Steps
1. Update `outfeed-core::model` and `engine` to accept `no_llm: bool`.
2. Update `outfeed-core::synthesis` with 10s timeout and graceful fallback.
3. Update `outfeed-core::release` with `ProgressReporter` integration.
4. Update `outfeed-cli` args and command handlers (`plan`, `apply`, `release`) to wire `--no-llm` / `--deterministic` and progress reporting.
5. Add unit and integration tests verifying progress reporting and `--no-llm` behavior.
6. Tier 2 verification, install binary to `~/.cargo/bin`, dogfood, and commit.

# GB-78: Capture Cargo Test Verification Output, Fix Misleading Step Labels, and Add --no-verify to Outfeed Release

## Problem
1. **Compilation/Test Output Leaking:** In `apply_release`, `cargo test --workspace` was invoked using `.status()`, which connected directly to stdout/stderr. Thousands of compiler and test output lines streamed to the terminal while `indicatif` progress spinners were ticking, corrupting cursor positions, duplicating progress bars, and scrambling the terminal UI.
2. **Misleading Step Information:** `release_repo` prematurely emitted `committing and tagging v...` before invoking `apply_release`. Inside `apply_release`, long-running test suites executed for minutes while the UI misleadingly claimed it was committing and tagging.
3. **Missing `--no-verify` Flag:** `outfeed apply` supported `--no-verify`, but `outfeed release` did not expose `--no-verify` or allow skipping the verification test suite.

## Solution
1. Use `run_captured(&mut test_cmd)` for `cargo test --workspace` in `engine.rs` so stdout/stderr are cleanly captured in memory.
2. Implement `apply_release_with_progress` taking `&dyn ProgressReporter` and reporting discrete, accurate phases:
   - `updating manifests & changelog...`
   - `synchronizing Cargo.lock...`
   - `running verification tests (cargo test)...`
   - `certifying release in Storypole...`
   - `committing and tagging v{target_version}...`
3. Add `--no-verify` to `ReleaseArgs` and `no_verify: bool` in `ReleaseOpts`.
4. Ensure all files remain strictly under 250 LOC and Tier 2/Tier 3 gates pass.

# GB-80: Enrich Sawhorse Provider Observability and Expand Synthesis Token Headroom for Reasoning Models

## Problem
1. **Empty Response Content from Reasoning Models:**
   `cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash` is a reasoning model. During inference, reasoning models emit an extensive thinking trace (`reasoning_tokens`) before outputting Markdown `content`. In empirical tests on changelog synthesis, the model used 1,950 reasoning tokens. Because `outfeed-core::synthesis` hardcoded `max_tokens = 1024`, the token limit was exhausted mid-thought, leaving `message.content` empty (`""`). The Cline API gateway rejected the empty completion with HTTP 500 `{"error":"empty response content","success":false}`.
2. **Zero Visibility into Sent Requests & Errors:**
   `sawhorse-core` lacked structured logging of model names, prompt sizes, and token limits. On HTTP errors, `Http` error messages omitted the target model and request parameters, leaving operators blind to what request payload was dispatched or why the provider failed.
3. **Timeout Insufficient for Thought Chains:**
   `outfeed-core` had a 10s synthesis timeout, which is insufficient for reasoning models that take 12-18s to finish complex thought chains.

## Solution
1. **Enrich `sawhorse-core` Observability & Error Diagnostics:**
   - In `OpenAiCompatProvider::complete` and `complete_stream`, emit structured `tracing::debug!` logs capturing `model`, `url`, `prompt_len`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`.
   - On HTTP errors, format the error to include the model name and `max_tokens`, and append an actionable diagnostic hint if `"empty response content"` is encountered.
2. **Expand `outfeed-core` Token Headroom & Timeout:**
   - Increase `req.max_tokens` from 1024 to 4096 in `outfeed-core::synthesis`.
   - Increase LLM synthesis timeout from 10s to 30s.
   - Add structured `tracing::debug!` logs before dispatching synthesis requests.
3. **Verification:**
   - Pass Tier 2 verification in `sawhorse` and `outfeed`.
   - Test live changelog synthesis with `outfeed release --all --dry-run` to confirm successful LLM synthesis without timeouts or empty response failures.

# GB-81: Add Reasoning Effort Controls and Capture Reasoning Traces in sawhorse-core

## Problem
1. **Inefficient Reasoning in Routine Utility Tasks:**
   For formatted utility prompts such as changelog synthesis in `outfeed`, frontier reasoning models (like `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) execute a 1,500–2,000 token thinking trace to produce simple Markdown bullets. This imposes 15–25s latency and high token consumption for deterministic output.
2. **Discarded High-Value Training Data:**
   `sawhorse-core::providers::openai_compat::payload::extract_chat_response` parses only `choices[0].message.content` and discards `choices[0].message.reasoning` / `reasoning_details`. In neurosymbolic architectures where outputs are compiler-verified, captured reasoning traces represent ground-truth process-supervised data for local SLM distillation.

## Solution
1. **Add `ReasoningEffort` to `sawhorse-core::types`:**
   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum ReasoningEffort {
       None,
       Low,
       Medium,
       High,
   }
   ```
2. **Expose in `InferenceRequest`:**
   Add `pub reasoning_effort: Option<ReasoningEffort>` to `InferenceRequest`.
3. **Dialect-Specific Payload Mapping:**
   In `openai_compat::payload::build_payload`:
   - Map `ReasoningEffort` to OpenAI standard `reasoning_effort`.
   - For models requiring `/no-think` or `thinking: { type: "disabled" }`, serialize appropriately based on dialect.
4. **Preserve Reasoning Traces in `InferenceResponse`:**
   Extend `InferenceResponse` with:
   - `pub reasoning_trace: Option<String>`
   - `pub reasoning_tokens: Option<u32>`
5. **Update `extract_chat_response`:**
   Extract `body["choices"][0]["message"]["reasoning"]` or `body["data"]["choices"][0]["message"]["reasoning"]` into `InferenceResponse::reasoning_trace`.

## Step Breakdown
- Step 1: Add `ReasoningEffort` enum and update `InferenceRequest` and `InferenceResponse` in `sawhorse-core::types` (Gate: `cargo check -p sawhorse-core`)
- Step 2: Update `build_payload` and `extract_chat_response` in `sawhorse-core::providers::openai_compat::payload` (Gate: `cargo test -p sawhorse-core`)
- Step 3: Run Tier 2 verification across `sawhorse` workspace (Gate: `cargo clippy -p sawhorse-core && cargo nextest run -p sawhorse-core`)

# GB-82: Implement Check -> Plan -> Execute 3-Phase Suite Release Pipeline in outfeed-core

## Problem
1. **Blind Sequential Execution:**
   `outfeed release --all` sequentially iterates through repos without an upfront plan, giving the operator zero visibility into which repos will be bumped, their target versions, or which are clean.
2. **Late Failures on Dirty Repos:**
   If repository 8 has uncommitted changes or is on a feature branch, the release pipeline executes for minutes on repositories 1–7 before crashing on repository 8, leaving the workspace in a half-released, dirty state.
3. **No Upfront Confirmation Gate:**
   Operators have no opportunity to inspect proposed versions or abort before irreversible tag creations, installations, and pushes occur.

## Solution
1. **Phase 1: Pre-flight Check (`check_suite_preflight`):**
   - Concurrently audit all 10 repositories (`main` branch check, clean working tree, remote tracking sync).
   - Strict Fail-Fast: Abort upfront with a diagnostic status table if any repository fails.
2. **Phase 2: Suite Release Plan (`plan_suite_releases`):**
   - Concurrently analyze git commits and Storypole tasks across all member repos using `futures::future::join_all`.
   - Calculate semver bumps and render the upfront **Compact Summary Table**:
     `REPOSITORY | CURRENT | TARGET | ACTION | COMMITS | TASKS`.
   - Auto-Exit Clean: If 0 repos need releases, print status and exit code 0.
3. **Phase 3: Topological Execution (`execute_suite_releases`):**
   - Execute releases strictly in topological dependency order.
   - Enforce concurrency control (`jobs = 1` by default for CPU/RAM safety on laptops).
   - Use captured verification and granular step progress.

## Step Breakdown
- Step 1: Implement `check_suite_preflight` in `outfeed-core::suite_check` (Gate: `cargo check -p outfeed-core`)
- Step 2: Implement `plan_suite_releases` and `format_suite_plan_table` in `outfeed-core::suite_plan` (Gate: `cargo check -p outfeed-core`)
- Step 3: Implement `execute_suite_releases` and refactor `release_all` in `outfeed-core::release` (Gate: `cargo test -p outfeed-core`)
- Step 4: Tier 2 verification in `outfeed-core` (Gate: `cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`)

# GB-83: Add --yes Flag and Concurrency Controls to outfeed release CLI

## Problem
1. **Interactive Prompt Bypass for Automated Environments:**
   With the introduction of the confirmation gate in the 3-phase release pipeline, automated CI scripts and agent harness runs need a non-interactive bypass flag (`--yes` / `-y`).
2. **Missing Workstation Concurrency Control:**
   Power users and high-core workstations should be able to specify concurrency levels via `--jobs` / `-j` when executing releases, while defaulting safely to sequential execution (`jobs = 1`) on resource-constrained laptops.

## Solution
1. **Update `ReleaseArgs` in `outfeed-cli`:**
   - Add `#[arg(short = 'y', long = "yes", help = "Automatically confirm release plan without prompting")] pub yes: bool`.
   - Add `#[arg(short = 'j', long = "jobs", default_value = "1", help = "Maximum concurrent release jobs (default: 1)")] pub jobs: usize`.
2. **Wire Confirmation Gate in CLI Handler:**
   - In `outfeed-cli::commands::release`:
     - Render the Plan Table.
     - If `--dry-run`: run simulated execution automatically.
     - If zero releases: print status and return Ok(()).
     - If not `--yes` and not `--json`: prompt `Proceed with release? [y/N]` using `dialoguer` or `std::io::stdin`.
     - Dispatch to `execute_suite_releases` passing `jobs`.

## Step Breakdown
- Step 1: Add `--yes` and `--jobs` flags to `ReleaseArgs` in `outfeed-cli` (Gate: `cargo check -p outfeed-cli`)
- Step 2: Implement confirmation prompt and wire CLI to 3-phase pipeline (Gate: `cargo test -p outfeed-cli`)
- Step 3: Run Tier 2 verification and dogfood `outfeed release --all --dry-run` (Gate: `cargo nextest run --workspace`)

plan.design_markdown:
# GB-84: Support DeepSeek and Cline Thinking Suppression Payload Formats and /no-think Directive

## Context & Root Cause
When calling `cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash` via `sawhorse-core` during changelog synthesis, the upstream gateway rejected requests with HTTP 500:
`{"error":"empty response content","success":false} (model: 'cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash', max_tokens: 4096)`.
Even with `max_tokens: 4096`, the model consumed all tokens inside `<think>...</think>` without generating completion content.

OpenAI-compatible endpoints use top-level `reasoning_effort` (`low`, `medium`, `high`). However:
1. DeepSeek and Cline/OpenRouter gateways default reasoning models to high thinking effort unless explicitly disabled via gateway-specific payload structures:
   - `"thinking": { "type": "disabled" }`
   - `"reasoning": { "effort": "none" }`
2. DeepSeek's instruction parser also supports an explicit instruction directive `/no-think` in the prompt to immediately suppress reasoning trace generation.
3. Because `build_payload` only emitted top-level `"reasoning_effort": "none"`, the gateway ignored it and ran with full default thinking mode.

## Implementation Steps
1. In `sawhorse/crates/sawhorse-core/src/providers/openai_compat/payload.rs`:
   - Map `ReasoningEffort::None` to:
     - `"reasoning_effort": "none"`
     - `"thinking": { "type": "disabled" }`
     - `"reasoning": { "effort": "none" }`
   - Map `ReasoningEffort::Low`, `Medium`, `High` to corresponding `"thinking": { "type": "enabled" }` and `"reasoning": { "effort": "<level>" }`.
2. In `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/synthesis.rs`:
   - Prefix the changelog synthesis prompt with `/no-think\n` when `ReasoningEffort::None` is dispatched.
3. Validate with unit tests and ensure file size remains under 250 LOC.

plan.summary: GB-85: Immediate Header Presentation, Live Progress Spinners, and Fast Deterministic Suite Release Planning
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-85: Immediate Header Presentation, Live Progress Spinners, and Fast Deterministic Suite Release Planning

## Context & Root Cause
When running `outfeed release --all`:
1. Phase 1 ran pre-flight silently without any stdout or progress spinner.
2. Phase 2 (`plan_suite_releases`) called `plan_release` with remote LLM changelog synthesis enabled for every single non-clean repository before printing anything to stdout.
3. For 8 member repositories, this executed 8 sequential remote LLM queries (taking 2.5 minutes) with zero terminal output, making the CLI appear completely frozen.
4. The upfront suite summary table only requires:
   - Current version (from Git tag or Cargo.toml)
   - Unreleased commit counts (from Git rev-parse / log)
   - SemVer bump calculation (from Conventional Commit prefixes)
   - Target version (from SemVer bump)
   - Referenced Storypole tickets (from commit messages)
   All of these operations are 100% deterministic local AST/Git operations that take under 50 milliseconds across the entire workspace.
5. In Phase 3 (`execute_suite_plan` / `release_repo`):
   - In dry-run mode, LLM synthesis was called despite notes never being applied or committed.
   - Initial progress reporting did not clearly label the active changelog evaluation phase.

## Implementation Steps
1. In `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/suite_plan.rs`:
   - Enforce fast deterministic commit evaluation (`no_llm: true`) inside `plan_suite_releases` so Phase 2 finishes in <50ms without network overhead.
2. In `outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli/src/commands/release.rs`:
   - Print the suite release header banner immediately upon invocation.
   - Start live spinner progress on `"suite"` for pre-flight validation.
   - Update spinner progress for suite plan compilation.
   - Complete spinner and render the compact summary table instantly.
   - Wire interactive confirmation prompt `Proceed with release? [y/N]: ` (bypassed with `--yes`, `--dry-run`, or `--json`).
3. In `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/release.rs`:
   - In `release_repo`, bypass remote LLM calls if `opts.dry_run` is set (`let no_llm = opts.no_llm || opts.dry_run;`).
4. Validate with Tier 1 and Tier 2 tests; ensure all files remain <= 250 LOC.

# GB-86: Suite-Wide 9-Document Architecture Rollout & Standardized READMEs

## Vision & Architecture Overview
This epic aligns documentation across the entire `gaugeblock` ecosystem with the canonical 9-document architecture defined in GB-18 and enforced by `chalkline docs check`.

1. **Member README Standardization:**
   Every member repository README will follow a strict 9-section architecture:
   - Header with badges (Version, License: Apache-2.0, Suite: gaugeblock, CI/Docs)
   - Woodworking Metaphor & Elevator Pitch
   - Architecture & Mental Model (ASCII flowcharts / diagrams)
   - Core Capabilities & Features
   - Crate Structure & Responsibilities
   - CLI Quickstart & Command Cheatsheet
   - Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool Reference
   - Verification & Development Invariants (file limits, Tier 1–3 checks)
   - License & Ecosystem Links

2. **AST-Grounded 9-Doc Scaffolding:**
   Dogfood `chalkline docs scaffold` to establish the required 6-document tier in every member repo:
   - `README.md`
   - `CONTRIBUTING.md`
   - `ARCHITECTURE.md`
   - `SPEC.md`
   - `CHANGELOG.md`
   - `AGENTS.md`
   (while `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and `ROADMAP.md` remain housed at the meta-harness root).

3. **Drift Resolution & Verification:**
   - Resolve `CHANGELOG.md` unreleased markers (`## [Unreleased]`).
   - Audit every repository with `chalkline docs check` as a mandatory Tier 3 completion gate (0 missing, 0 drifted).

## Work Breakdown & Child Tasks
- **GB-87:** Core Foundations (`miter`, `storypole`, `sawhorse`)
- **GB-88:** Synthesis Stack (`chalkline`, `dado`, `batten`, `joiner`)
- **GB-89:** Delivery & UI (`benchwork`, `outfeed`, `rabbet`)

# GB-92: Roll back modified Cargo.lock when Tier 4 verification fails during outfeed release

## Context & Root Cause
In `outfeed-core` (`crates/outfeed-core/src/engine.rs`), Step 2 runs `cargo check --workspace` which synchronizes `Cargo.lock` to the newly bumped version.
If Step 3 (Tier 4 verification `cargo test --workspace`) fails:
`outfeed` calls `rollback_manifest_diffs(repo_dir, &plan.manifest_diffs)` which restores `Cargo.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
However, `Cargo.lock` is not rolled back. This leaves `Cargo.lock` dirty in the working tree, blocking all subsequent release attempts with `Working tree is dirty: M Cargo.lock`.

## Implementation Steps
1. In `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/engine.rs`:
   - When rolling back manifest diffs after a failed verification, also revert `Cargo.lock` if it exists in the repository root (e.g. via `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` or restoring its original state).
2. Add a helper function or integrate into rollback logic to ensure working tree cleanliness on aborted release.
3. Verify with unit tests in `outfeed-core`.
4. Commit atomically: `fix(outfeed-core): roll back Cargo.lock on release verification failure`.

# GB-96: Embed static web assets within benchwork-cli crate directory for crates.io packaging

## Context & Root Cause
In `benchwork-cli` (`crates/benchwork-cli/src/daemon/assets.rs:15`), `rust-embed` was configured with:
`#[folder = "../../web/dist"]`
When running `cargo publish` or `cargo package`, Cargo isolates the packaged crate into `target/package/benchwork-cli-<version>/` and verifies compilation. Because Cargo excludes files outside the package root from the crate tarball, `../../web/dist` evaluated to `target/web/dist` (which does not exist), failing publication with:
`error: #[derive(RustEmbed)] folder '.../target/package/benchwork-cli-0.1.0-beta.5/../../web/dist' does not exist.`

## Implementation Steps
1. Create `crates/benchwork-cli/dist` directory and populate it with web assets from `web/dist`.
2. Update `benchwork/web/package.json` build script to ensure `dist/` is synchronized to `../crates/benchwork-cli/dist/` when `npm run build` runs.
3. Update `benchwork/crates/benchwork-cli/src/daemon/assets.rs`:
   - Change `#[folder = "../../web/dist"]` to `#[folder = "dist"]`.
4. Update `benchwork/crates/benchwork-cli/Cargo.toml` if necessary to explicitly include `dist/**`.

plan.design_markdown:
# GB-100: Add disk space pre-flight check and inter-repo cache hygiene to outfeed release

## Context & Problem Statement
During macro suite releases (`outfeed release --all`), up to 10 member repositories compile, run Tier 4 test suites, install binaries, and run `cargo publish --dry-run` sequentially. All of these compilation steps write artifacts into the shared workspace `target/` directory.

Because debug artifacts, object files (`.rlib`, `.rmeta`), and test binaries accumulate across repositories, `target/` can grow to 15–25+ GB. On storage-constrained machines (such as environments with under 15 GB available), a suite release fails midway with `No space left on device` (OS error 28). This leaves the workspace in a partially-released state where earlier repositories were bumped, tagged, or pushed while subsequent repositories remain unreleased.

## Invariants & Design Decisions

### 1. Pre-flight Disk Space Audit
- Query available filesystem space for `workspace_root` using POSIX `df -P -k <path>` (supported on macOS, Linux, BSD) or safe fallback.
- Enforce minimum headroom requirements:
  - Default for single repo release: **2.5 GB**.
  - Default for suite release (`--all` with inter-repo clean enabled): **4.0 GB**.
  - Default for suite release (`--all` with inter-repo clean disabled): **20.0 GB**.
- If free space is below the required threshold, abort in pre-flight with `OutfeedError::InsufficientDiskSpace` before modifying manifests or tags.
- Support CLI overrides `--min-disk-gb <N>` and `--skip-disk-check`.

### 2. Inter-Repo Cache Hygiene
- In `execute_suite_plan`, after each repository completes its full release lifecycle (`cargo test` -> manifest bump -> commit & tag -> `cargo install` -> `cargo publish`), clean disposable intermediate artifacts.
- Target clean specifically targets:
  - `target/debug`: intermediate object files and test executables.
  - `target/package`: dry-run crate tarballs.
- Preserves installed binaries (`cargo install` copies binaries directly into `~/.cargo/bin`).
- Enabled by default during suite release (`--all`); configurable via `--no-clean-between-repos`.
- Reports reclaimed bytes via `ProgressReporter`.

### 3. File Size Invariant (Law 1: < 250 LOC)
- Implement disk space inspection in a new dedicated module `outfeed-core/src/disk_space.rs` to avoid exceeding the 250-line limit in `clean.rs` or `suite_check.rs`.

## Execution Plan & Verification Steps
1. Create `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/disk_space.rs` with `get_available_disk_space` and `check_disk_space_headroom`.
2. Add `InsufficientDiskSpace` variant to `outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/error.rs`.
3. Add `clean_between_repos`, `min_disk_bytes`, and `skip_disk_check` to `ReleaseOpts` in `outfeed-core` and CLI args in `outfeed-cli`.
4. Integrate disk space check into `check_suite_preflight` in `outfeed-core/src/suite_check.rs`.
5. Integrate inter-repo clean into `execute_suite_plan` in `outfeed-core/src/release.rs`.
6. Run Tier 1 and Tier 2 verifications: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core -p outfeed-cli`.

receipt.summary: Implemented disk space headroom pre-flight audit and inter-repo target/debug and target/package cache hygiene in outfeed release

plan.design_markdown:
# GB-101: Add outfeed publish --all, crates.io registry verification, and release self-healing

## Context & Problem Statement
During release orchestration, `outfeed release` commits manifests and creates git tags in Step 1 of the apply phase. When a subsequent step fails (such as running out of disk space, network interruption, or skipped publication):
- The git tag remains committed locally on `HEAD`.
- On all future runs, `outfeed release` checks `git log <latest_tag>..HEAD`, sees 0 unreleased commits, and marks the repository as `Skip (Clean)`.
- It never queries crates.io to verify if the tagged version actually exists in the registry.
- As a result, `rabbet` remained at `0.0.1-alpha.1` on crates.io despite being tagged `v0.1.0-beta.3` locally, and `outfeed` remained at `0.1.0-beta.1` despite being tagged `v0.1.0-beta.5` locally.
- Furthermore, `outfeed publish` currently only accepts a single repository and lacks an `--all` flag, while `scripts/publish-crates.sh` hardcoded only 7 repositories.

## Invariants & Design Decisions

### 1. Registry Inspection Module (`outfeed-core/src/registry.rs`)
- Query published crate versions from crates.io using `cargo search <crate> --limit 1` or sparse index lookup.
- Provide:
  - `get_published_crate_version(crate_name: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, OutfeedError>`
  - `is_version_published(crate_name: &str, target_version: &str) -> Result<bool, OutfeedError>`
  - `are_repo_crates_published(repo_dir: &Path, target_version: &str) -> Result<bool, OutfeedError>`

### 2. Self-Healing in `plan_suite_releases` & `execute_suite_plan`
- In `plan_suite_releases`, when a repository has 0 new commits since its latest tag, inspect if its member crates at that version are published on crates.io.
- If any member crate is not published on crates.io:
  - Set `action: SuitePlanAction::PublishPending`.
  - Format table displays `Publish (Pending)`.
- In `execute_suite_plan`:
  - When encountering `SuitePlanAction::PublishPending`, automatically invoke `publish_repo` to self-heal and publish the pending release.

### 3. Suite-Wide Publishing (`publish_all` & `outfeed publish --all`)
- Implement `publish_all` and `publish_all_with_progress` in `outfeed-core/src/publish.rs` to publish all suite member crates in topological order.
- Add `pub all: bool` to `PublishArgs` in `outfeed-cli`.
- Update `scripts/publish-crates.sh` to delegate to `outfeed publish --all "$@"`.

### 4. Visibility in `outfeed status`
- In `outfeed status`, if a repository has 0 unreleased commits but its version is unpublished on crates.io, display `⚠️  unpublished (crates.io: <ver>)` instead of `✅ clean`.

### 5. File Size Constraints (Law 1)

plan.summary: Adaptive Disk Space Headroom Guard and cache retention
plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-122 — Implement Adaptive Disk Space Headroom Guard and Cache Retention in outfeed

> **Task Key:** `GB-122`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
`clean_between_repos` currently defaults to `true`, wiping `target/debug` after every released repository. This forces all 10 tools to recompile `syn`, `tokio`, `serde`, and uncached proc-macros from scratch, adding 30–50 minutes of pure CPU churn. If disabled, `outfeed` artificially demanded 20.0 GB of free disk, failing on systems with 12 GB free despite the shared target directory plateauing at only ~5.0 GB.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-core/src/model/options.rs`:
   * Change `ReleaseOpts.clean_between_repos` default to `false`.
2. In `outfeed-core/src/suite_check.rs`:
   * Change required headroom threshold to `DEFAULT_MIN_SUITE_DISK_BYTES` (4.0 GB) regardless of `clean_between_repos`.
3. In `outfeed-core/src/suite_exec.rs`:
   * Add continuous `get_available_disk_space()` monitoring before/after every repository release.
   * If available disk `< 3.5 GB`: trigger adaptive surgical pruning of test binaries in `target/debug/deps` using `prune_workspace()`.
   * If available disk `< 2.0 GB`: trigger emergency target clean.
4. In `.cargo/config.toml`:
   * Add `[env] SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE = "15G"` to prevent LRU cache eviction thrashing.

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Modify default options in `options.rs` and preflight threshold in `suite_check.rs`.
* **Step 2:** Implement continuous adaptive headroom guard in `suite_exec.rs`.
* **Step 3:** Add `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE` configuration to `.cargo/config.toml`.
* **Step 4:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`).

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-123 — Implement Topological DAG Parallel Execution (jobs = num_cpus) in outfeed

> **Task Key:** `GB-123`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
`outfeed release --all` accepts `-j / --jobs`, but `execute_suite_plan()` in `suite_exec.rs` executes a strictly serial loop over `plan.entries`. Member tools that do not depend on each other's unreleased changes are compiled and verified sequentially, causing massive wall-clock latency.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-cli/src/args/release.rs`:
   * Set default `jobs = num_cpus::get()` or `std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(4)`.
2. In `outfeed-core/src/suite_exec.rs`:
   * Partition `plan.entries` into topological dependency waves:
     * Wave 1: `miter`
     * Wave 2: `storypole`, `sawhorse`, `dado`, `rabbet` (concurrent)
     * Wave 3: `chalkline`, `batten` (concurrent)
     * Wave 4: `joiner`
     * Wave 5: `benchwork`, `outfeed` (concurrent)
   * Execute each wave using `tokio::task::JoinSet` with a bounded semaphore sized to `opts.jobs`.
3. In `progress.rs`:
   * Ensure `ProgressReporter` implementations safely handle multi-threaded progress updates with atomic stdout synchronization.

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Default jobs to available CPU parallelism in CLI args.
* **Step 2:** Implement topological wave partitioning and JoinSet execution in `suite_exec.rs`.
* **Step 3:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`).

# Task Plan: GB-124 — Switch Release Verification to cargo-nextest and Make Binary Install Opt-in

> **Task Key:** `GB-124`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core,outfeed-cli`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
`outfeed-core/src/engine.rs` hardcodes `cargo test --workspace` via standard subprocess, completely bypassing the installed `cargo-nextest` runner. Before running tests, it runs a redundant `cargo check --workspace`. Furthermore, `release_repo` forces a full `cargo install --force` in release mode for every single repository, adding 20–30 minutes of binary compilation during releases.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-core/src/engine.rs`:
   * Eliminate the redundant `cargo check --workspace` prior to testing.
   * Detect `cargo-nextest` on PATH:
     * If present: execute `cargo nextest run --workspace` (followed by `cargo test --doc` if doc tests exist).
     * If absent: fallback cleanly to `cargo test --workspace`.
2. In `outfeed-core/src/model/options.rs` & `outfeed-cli/src/args/release.rs`:
   * Invert installation behavior: skip binary compilation into `~/.cargo/bin` by default during `release --all`.
   * Add `--install` flag to explicitly opt in to local binary installations.

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Invert install default and add `--install` argument.
* **Step 2:** Wire `cargo-nextest` execution into `engine.rs` and drop redundant `cargo check`.
* **Step 3:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`).

plan.summary: Port Crates.io 429 rate-limit parser, 30s terminal countdown, and sparse index polling
plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-125 — Port Crates.io 429 Rate-Limit Parser, 30s Terminal Countdown, and Sparse Index Polling

> **Task Key:** `GB-125`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
When publishing member crates, `outfeed` has zero retry or rate-limit handling. A Crates.io `429 Too Many Requests` response immediately hard-crashes the entire release. Furthermore, `outfeed` sleeps a fixed 15 seconds after every crate published, wasting 5–7.5 minutes across the suite.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-core/src/publish.rs`:
   * Implement regex parser for Crates.io 429 responses (matching RFC 2822 dates and integer seconds, ported from `scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh`).
   * When a 429 is received, enter an active cooldown loop with 30s updates through `reporter.on_update()`.
   * Automatically retry publishing up to 3 times upon cooldown expiration.
2. In `publish.rs`:
   * Replace the blind `sleep(15)` with an active HTTP poll against `https://index.crates.io/` every 500ms.
   * Proceed immediately once the new version is returned by the sparse index (typically 2–4s).
3. In `outfeed-core/src/registry.rs`:
   * Replace slow `cargo search` CLI calls with direct HTTP checks (`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{name}`).

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Implement 429 rate-limit parser and retry wrapper in `publish.rs`.
* **Step 2:** Implement async crates.io sparse index polling to replace blind sleep.
* **Step 3:** Replace `cargo search` with direct HTTP registry check in `registry.rs`.
* **Step 4:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`).

steps.title: Implement 429 rate-limit parser and retry wrapper
Implement async sparse index polling
Replace cargo search with direct HTTP registry check
Tier 2 verification

plan.summary: Configure SQLite WAL journal mode and synchronous=NORMAL in storypole-core
plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-132 — Configure SQLite WAL Journal Mode and synchronous=NORMAL in storypole-core

> **Task Key:** `GB-132`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-128`  
> **Scope:** `storypole-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
`storypole-core` currently opens `index.sqlite` without setting SQLite performance PRAGMAs, defaulting to rollback journal deletion and full synchronous disk flushes (`PRAGMA synchronous = FULL`). Every task update, verification, and ledger rebuild incurs blocking `fsync()` system calls.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `storypole-core/src/index/mod.rs` (`open_and_sync_index`):
   * Immediately after `Connection::open(sqlite_path)`, execute:
     ```rust
     conn.execute_batch(
         "PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
          PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;
          PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY;
          PRAGMA cache_size = -64000;
          PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;"
     )?;
     ```
2. Verify WAL mode compatibility with existing tests and multi-process access.

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Add high-performance SQLite PRAGMAs to `open_and_sync_index` in `storypole-core`.
* **Step 2:** Verify all storypole unit and integration tests pass cleanly under WAL mode.
* **Step 3:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p storypole-core`).

# Task Plan: GB-136 — TaskBriefing Omits Parent-Epic and Incoming Edges

> **Task Key:** `GB-136`  
> **Scope:** `storypole-core`  
> **Related:** `GB-97` (benchwork wire contracts), `GB-121`/`GB-128` (epics that render empty)  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement

`build_task_briefing()` summarises only **outgoing** `RelatedTo` / `BlockedBy` edges:

```rust
if matches!(edge.kind, EdgeKind::RelatedTo | EdgeKind::BlockedBy)
```

Two consequences reach the user through both the `storypole show` CLI and the benchwork
inspector (`InspectorEdges.tsx` → `briefing.related_tasks_summary`):

1. **Epics render empty.** `ParentEpic` edges are stored **on the child** (see
   `ops::graph::split_task`), so an epic such as `GB-121` — which owns five children in the ledger —
   reports `Related Tasks & Edges (0)` and the inspector prints "No linked tasks or dependencies."
2. **Linking appears broken.** Choosing "Parent Epic" in the benchwork link modal writes a valid
   `ParentEpic` edge, but because the parent has no outgoing edge, the freshly created link is
   invisible on reload. The write succeeds; the read never shows it.
3. **Dependents are invisible.** A `BlockedBy` edge surfaces on the blocked task only. The blocker
   never learns which tasks it is holding back, and siblings that recorded a mutual `RelatedTo` link
   on their own side are invisible to the other endpoint.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint

1. In `crates/storypole-core/src/dag/briefing.rs` (`build_task_briefing`):
   * Include `EdgeKind::ParentEpic` alongside `RelatedTo`/`BlockedBy` in the outgoing pass so a
     child still lists its parent epic (and keeps inheriting resolved parent decisions).
   * Add a second, **inbound** pass over `all_tasks`: any task whose edge targets this task with one
     of the three summarised kinds is added to `related_tasks_summary`.
   * Deduplicate with a `Vec<Uuid>` of already-linked ids so mutual links collapse to one entry.
2. Wire shape stays `Vec<(String, String, TaskStatus)>` (documented in `CONTRACTS.md`); no schema
   change, so benchwork's TypeScript tuple type remains valid.
3. Regression tests in `crates/storypole-core/tests/briefing_edges_tests.rs`:
   * epic lists its children while each child still lists the epic;
   * `BlockedBy` surfaces on both endpoints;
   * mutual `RelatedTo` links are not duplicated;
   * a child briefing still reaches its ready parent epic.

---

## 3. Execution Steps

* **Step 1:** Extend briefing link summarisation with `ParentEpic` and inbound edges. Gate: `cargo check -p storypole-core`.
* **Step 2:** Add bidirectional regression tests. Gate: `cargo test -p storypole-core --test briefing_edges_tests`.
* **Step 3:** Tier 2 verification. Gate: `cargo nextest run -p storypole-core` + `cargo clippy -p storypole-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
* **Step 4:** Documentation + certification. Gate: `chalkline docs check -d storypole`.

---

## 4. Boundaries

* Task **ordering** semantics (`dag::mod` acyclic rules) are untouched — this is a read-model fix.
* Rendering changes belong to benchwork; `InspectorEdges.tsx` already consumes the tuple list and
  needs no change.
* Any further benchwork contract mismatch (e.g. `TaskStatus` casing) stays with `GB-97`.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-98 — Harmonize miter AGENTS.md, Workspace Metadata, and Clippy Lints

> **Task Key:** `GB-98`  
> **Scope:** `miter-cli` / workspace  
> **Status:** Implemented — Tier 2 gate green

---

## 1. Problem Statement

`miter` is the oldest repository in the suite and never received the metadata and lint harmonization the other nine did:

1. **Wrong canonical remote.** `[workspace.package]` pointed `repository`/`homepage` at
   `https://github.com/colinwolff/miter` instead of `https://github.com/gaugeblock/miter` /
   `https://gaugeblock.dev`, and `authors` carried no email.
2. **Missing publish metadata.** No `readme` key, so `cargo publish` falls back to `README.md` by
   convention rather than by declaration.
3. **No suite lint floor.** The workspace declared only `[workspace.lints.rust]`; the suite standard
   (`unwrap_used`/`expect_used` = deny) was absent, so production paths could silently unwrap.
4. **Stale README badge.** The badge advertised `0.1.0-beta.2` while the workspace is `0.1.0-beta.4`,
   and release links pointed at the personal remote.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint

1. `Cargo.toml`: canonical `repository`/`homepage`, suite `authors`, explicit `readme`, and
   `[workspace.lints.clippy] unwrap_used = "deny"`, `expect_used = "deny"`.
2. Fix every library-path `unwrap()`/`expect()`:
   * `analysis/cycles.rs` — two `lowlink.get_mut(node)` unwraps became `if let Some(..)` guards;
   * `analysis/clones.rs` — `partial_cmp().unwrap()` became `unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)` with an
     `// INVARIANT:` note that similarities are clamped to `0.0..=1.0`.
3. Add `#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]` to test-only modules (43 files: `tests/`
   trees, `*tests.rs`, `tests_*.rs`, `cases.rs` fixture modules and inline `#[cfg(test)]` blocks),
   matching the suite convention that tests may unwrap while library paths may not.
4. README: badge to `0.1.0-beta.4`, release links to the `gaugeblock` org.

---

## 3. Execution Steps

* **Step 1:** Add suite clippy lints and fix library-path unwraps. Gate: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
* **Step 2:** Allow unwrap/expect in test-only modules. Gate: same clippy command.
* **Step 3:** Harmonize workspace metadata and README badge. Gate: `cargo metadata --no-deps`.
* **Step 4:** Tier 2 verification. Gate: `cargo nextest run --workspace` + `chalkline docs check -d miter`.

---

## 4. Boundaries

* `AGENTS.md` already carried the suite directives (250-line ceiling, tiered verification, storypole
  deferral), so no rewrite was needed beyond metadata.
* Dependency upgrades (tree-sitter 0.27, sqlparser 0.63) stay with `GB-20`/`GB-21`.

# Task Plan: GB-125 — Port Crates.io 429 Rate-Limit Parser, 30s Terminal Countdown, and Sparse Index Polling

> **Task Key:** `GB-125`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
When publishing member crates, `outfeed` has zero retry or rate-limit handling. A Crates.io `429 Too Many Requests` response immediately hard-crashes the entire release. Furthermore, `outfeed` sleeps a fixed 15 seconds after every crate published, wasting 5–7.5 minutes across the suite.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-core/src/publish.rs`:
   * Implement regex parser for Crates.io 429 responses (matching RFC 2822 dates and integer seconds, ported from `scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh`).
   * When a 429 is received, enter an active cooldown loop with 30s updates through `reporter.on_update()`.
   * Automatically retry publishing up to 3 times upon cooldown expiration.
2. In `publish.rs`:
   * Replace the blind `sleep(15)` with an active HTTP poll against `https://index.crates.io/` every 500ms.
   * Proceed immediately once the new version is returned by the sparse index (typically 2–4s).
3. In `outfeed-core/src/registry.rs`:
   * Replace slow `cargo search` CLI calls with direct HTTP checks (`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{name}`).

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Implement 429 rate-limit parser and retry wrapper in `publish.rs`.
* **Step 2:** Implement async crates.io sparse index polling to replace blind sleep.
* **Step 3:** Replace `cargo search` with direct HTTP registry check in `registry.rs`.
* **Step 4:** Tier 2 verification (`cargo nextest run -p outfeed-core`).

# Task Plan: GB-125 — Port Crates.io 429 Rate-Limit Parser, 30s Terminal Countdown, and Sparse Index Polling

> **Task Key:** `GB-125`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-121`  
> **Scope:** `outfeed-core`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
When publishing member crates, `outfeed` has zero retry or rate-limit handling. A Crates.io `429 Too Many Requests` response immediately hard-crashes the entire release. Furthermore, `outfeed` sleeps a fixed 15 seconds after every crate published, wasting 5–7.5 minutes across the suite.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `outfeed-core/src/publish.rs`:
   * Implement regex parser for Crates.io 429 responses (matching RFC 2822 dates and integer seconds, ported from `scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh`).
   * When a 429 is received, enter an active cooldown loop with 30s updates through `reporter.on_update()`.
   * Automatically retry publishing up to 3 times upon cooldown expiration.
2. In `publish.rs`:
   * Replace the blind `sleep(15)` with an active HTTP poll against `https://index.crates.io/` every 500ms.
   * Proceed immediately once the new version is returned by the sparse index (typically 2–4s).
3. In `outfeed-core/src/registry.rs`:
   * Replace slow `cargo search` CLI calls with direct HTTP checks (`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{name}`).

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Implement 429 / `Retry-After` parsing and the countdown retry wrapper (`src/rate_limit.rs`).
* **Step 2:** Implement crates.io sparse-index path/version helpers and 500 ms polling (`src/index_poll.rs`).
* **Step 3:** Wire retry + index polling into `publish.rs` and make the registry check sparse-index-first.
* **Step 4:** Tier 2/3 verification (`cargo nextest run --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

---

## 4. Implementation Notes

* **Module split, not `publish.rs` growth.** The parsers live in `rate_limit.rs` and the index logic
  in `index_poll.rs` so `publish.rs` stays well inside the 250-line law and the pure parsing rules
  stay unit-testable without a network.
* **Cooldown semantics.** `Retry-After` accepts integer seconds or an RFC 2822 HTTP-date (parsed with
  `chrono`); when neither is present the resolver falls back to a 30 s default. The retry wrapper
  reports a countdown through `reporter.on_update` and gives up after 3 attempts.
* **Index polling replaces the blind sleep.** `delay_secs` becomes the *timeout budget* for
  `wait_for_index_version`, which polls `https://index.crates.io/<shard>/<name>` every 500 ms and
  returns as soon as the published version appears (typically 2–4 s). A timeout is non-fatal: the
  release proceeds, matching the previous best-effort behaviour.
* **Registry lookup.** `get_published_crate_version` prefers one sparse-index request and falls back
  to the existing `cargo search` parser when the index is unreachable (offline/air-gapped CI).
* **Dependency.** `reqwest` blocking + rustls is added to `outfeed-core`; it is already in the build
  graph through `sawhorse-core`, so no new transitive compilation is introduced.

task.title: parse_cooldown misses crates.io's 'try again after <RFC2822 date>' body form
task.description: Observed during the GB-127 namespace reservation: crates.io returns 429 with the deadline only in the message body ('You have published too many new crates in a short period of time. # Task Plan: GB-127 — Phase 2: Reserve gaugeblock and Sub-Crate Namespaces on Crates.io

> **Task Key:** `GB-127`  
> **Scope:** `workspace`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Objective
Secure all unclaimed root and sub-crate namespaces for `gaugeblock` on Crates.io by publishing initial placeholder versions (`0.1.0-beta.1`) using the automated 429 countdown cooldown harness.

---

## 2. Target Namespaces
* `gaugeblock` (Root facade / meta-harness CLI)
* `gaugeblock-common` (Foundation library)
* `gaugeblock-contracts` (Direct code implementation of CONTRACTS.md)
* `gaugeblock-mcp` (Generic Model Context Protocol stdio engine)
* `gaugeblock-git` (Safe git porcelain and single-round-trip push)
* `gaugeblock-core` (Meta-harness orchestration engine)

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Prepare placeholder Cargo manifests and minimal documentation conforming to Crates.io publishing rules.
* **Step 2:** Execute namespace reservation script with automated 429 cooldown tracking.
* **Step 3:** Verify ownership and package existence on `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{name}`.

---

## 4. Execution Record — 2026-10-28

**Reservation version: `0.1.0-alpha.1`.** Namespace reservations ship at `alpha.1`; the suite only
moves to `0.1.0-beta.1` once a crate is actually built and ready for dogfooding.

All six namespaces are claimed and publicly resolvable:

| Crate | Version | crates.io |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `gaugeblock` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |
| `gaugeblock-common` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |
| `gaugeblock-contracts` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |
| `gaugeblock-mcp` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |
| `gaugeblock-git` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |
| `gaugeblock-core` | `0.1.0-alpha.1` | published |

* Each placeholder is a dependency-free library with `description`, `license`, `repository`
  (`https://github.com/gaugeblock/common` for the sub-crates), `homepage`, `documentation`,
  `readme`, keywords and categories, plus a `pub const PACKAGE` naming the reserved package.
* Published with the freshly built `outfeed publish` (dogfooding `GB-125`): dry-run gate per crate,
  then sequential publication.
* **Live rate-limit exercise:** the sixth crate (`gaugeblock-mcp`) hit crates.io's new-crate limit and
  the new `rate_limit` retry path engaged (`crates.io rate limit: retrying in 30s`). The cooldown in
  crates.io's body form (`try again after <RFC2822 date>`) is not parsed yet, so the three-attempt
  budget expired before the real deadline and the crate was published after the cooldown. The parser
  gap is tracked as `GB-140`.

**Next version:** the first real implementation of any of these crates bumps it to
`0.1.0-beta.1` (dogfood-ready), never re-using `alpha.1`.

decision.question: Where should contract-type behaviour live once members re-export gaugeblock-contracts types?
proposed_options: A: Move behaviour into contracts — relocate constructors (InferenceRequest::new, TypedHole::new), Display for GrammarFormat and task helpers (AgentClaim::is_expired, slug generation) into gaugeblock-contracts so members re-export types+behaviour; contracts stays pure (no I/O).
B: Keep definitions in members — contracts remains a documentation mirror for cross-language consumers only; members keep owning their types, so no orphan-rule problem and no schema churn.
C: Newtype wrappers — members wrap each contract type in a tuple struct that carries their impls; wire shape is preserved via transparent serde, at the cost of double definitions.

D: Hybrid — pure-data types (outfeed, miter) re-export from contracts; behaviour-rich types (storypole, sawhorse, dado, batten) stay local until their extra fields (e.g. DadoPattern::canonical_example_fills) are reconciled into CONTRACTS.md.

Investigated the next four members and found the repoint is NOT mechanical there: sawhorse InferenceRequest has an inherent new(); dado TypedHole has new() and DadoPattern carries an extra canonical_example_fills field absent from CONTRACTS.md; batten implements Display for GrammarFormat; storypole TaskNode/AgentClaim carry lease and slug helpers. Rust rejects inherent impls on re-exported foreign types (E0116), so behaviour placement must be decided first. Raised decision 37ce2855-05e9-403f-bbb3-7e9e62c43f09 with four options (A move behaviour into contracts, B keep local owners, C newtype wrappers, D hybrid).

task.title: A handoff packet clears a pending-decision block and leaves the task Ready
task.description: Observed on GB-143: ask-decision marked the task Blocked, then storypole handoff <KEY> <AGENT> moved it to Ready while the Pending decision was still attached. An agent reading storypole next/ list would see a ready task whose architectural decision is unanswered. Handoff should preserve a Blocked state when a Pending decision exists (or recompute status from the decision set).

rationale: After reconciling CONTRACTS.md with the implementations the schema uncertainty that motivated option D is gone, so the only open question is behaviour placement. The four impls are pure and infallible (InferenceRequest::new, TypedHole::new, Display for GrammarFormat, AgentClaim::is_expired) and inherent impls travel with a re-exported type, so sawhorse_core::InferenceRequest::new keeps compiling with no newtype indirection; the impls live in the crate that owns the type, so the orphan rule is satisfied. Option D would have preserved four duplicate definitions - exactly the drift this ticket just repaired. miter's internal Language/SymbolKind remain internal and are bridged by a From conversion written in miter.
