task.title: Concurrent storypole invocations corrupt the ledger by splicing two JSON events onto one line
task.description: Observed twice on 2026-10-28 while two agent tool calls ran storypole mutations in parallel: the ledger gained a line holding two concatenated JSON objects and every subsequent command failed with 'Corrupt ledger at line N: trailing characters at line 1 column M'. Incidents were at line 747 (claim + three defers) and line 833 (decide + claim). Appends are not atomic against concurrent writers: there is no advisory lock and no guarantee the event is written in a single syscall, so interleaved writers splice objects. Repair requires hand-splitting the affected line and deleting index.sqlite, because the SQLite projection does not notice an externally repaired ledger. Desired: take an advisory lock (flock) or write via a single serialized append per event; add an integrity check that refuses to append to a corrupt tail; and invalidate/rebuild the index when the ledger mtime or size no longer matches the projection.

task.title: dado-core re-implements tree-sitter syntax validation instead of using miter-engine's polyglot parser
task.description: dado-core depends on miter-engine and miter-ast, yet splice/ast_check.rs builds its own tree-sitter parser with tree-sitter, tree-sitter-rust and tree-sitter-typescript (three C-compiled crates) to validate spliced code. miter-engine already exposes the shared parser (polyglot::dispatch::{parse,parse_detected,parse_declarative}); dado's copy covers fewer languages (validate_syntax errors with 'Python grammar not yet enabled in dado' for Language::Python even though miter parses Python). Replacing validate_syntax with the miter-engine parser removes three C dependencies from dado's build graph and closes the Python gap. Note: dado-core/src/polyglot/{rust_gen,ts_gen}.rs is code GENERATION, not extraction, so it is not duplication and should stay with dado.

task.title: Track Cargo.lock in every member repository and remove the silent git-add trap it creates
task.description: Audit 2026-10-28: six repositories ignore their lockfile (storypole:4, sawhorse:4, batten:4, joiner:3, benchwork:4, rabbet:4 - each written as 'Cargo.lock ' with a trailing space, which git trims so the pattern still matches), while five already track it (miter, chalkline, dado, outfeed, common). The harness root .gitignore also lists Cargo.lock even though the root has no Cargo manifest. Two consequences. (1) Reproducibility: every suite member is a binary/tool, where Cargo's own guidance is to commit the lockfile; a fresh clone of the six untracked repos resolves whatever versions exist that day, so a published upstream breaking change silently alters a user's build. (2) Operational trap: 'git add -A <dir> Cargo.lock' aborts with 'paths are ignored' and stages NOTHING, and a following 'git commit -q' then fails with no output - it silently produced no-op merges twice today (batten 33a6286 and storypole 5ffb991 had to be re-committed by hand). Proposed fix: drop the Cargo.lock line from the six member .gitignore files (and the root one), git add + commit the lockfile in each of those six as chore(<repo>): track Cargo.lock, then add scripts/check-lockfiles.sh asserting every repository containing Cargo.toml also tracks Cargo.lock, wire it into the Tier 3 gate, and record in AGENTS.md that 'git add <dir> <ignored-path>' aborts the whole staging operation. Acceptance: git ls-files --error-unmatch Cargo.lock succeeds in all eleven repositories, the check script exits 0, and the Tier 3 gate list names it.

task.title: outfeed release leaves repositories that are clean but ahead of origin unpushed
task.description: Observed while preparing the suite release: chalkline, joiner, benchwork and rabbet each have one commit ahead of origin/main but no unreleased changes since their last tag, so the plan marks them Skip (Clean) and outfeed release --all never pushes them. A repo can legitimately be clean and ahead - its last release was committed and tagged locally but the push never happened - so finishing a release pass leaves the remote behind. Options: have the suite release push any member whose branch is ahead of its upstream even when there is nothing to release, or report those repositories at the end of the run with a pointer to 'outfeed push --all'. Acceptance: after a release pass, no member with an origin remote is left ahead of origin/main without an explicit note or skip flag.

description: Corrected framing after investigation (2026-10-28). Outfeed's release state machine is per repository: plan collects commits between the latest tag and HEAD, and only a repository with at least one such commit is versioned, tagged, pushed and published. Anything after the tag makes a repository 'not clean', so ordinary local work is always swept into the next release - there is no routine case where local changes sit outside a release. Verified in this workspace: for chalkline, joiner, benchwork and rabbet, origin/main equals local HEAD~1 (the last release commit) and the release tags are present on origin; the only pending commit in each is today's chore(<repo>): track Cargo.lock, so the next release --all will patch-bump all four and push them normally. The real gap is failure recovery, not routine operation: because push and publish live inside the per-repository release step, a run that dies after commit+tag but before push (or a run with --skip-push, or a publish that 429s out) leaves a repository whose HEAD is the tagged commit. A later release --all then sees zero commits since the tag, reports Skip (Clean), and never retries the push or the publish - the operator gets a green run while the remote or the registry is behind. Desired: after the release loop, reconcile state for every member (compare HEAD with origin/main and the published registry version) and either finish the missing step or report it loudly, and make a re-run able to heal a half-finished repository. Outfeed sync already audits divergence and is the natural place to share that logic. Acceptance: a release interrupted between tag and push is completed by re-running, and a clean-but-behind repository is never reported as success.

Add the missing push half of release self-healing. Precedent already in the codebase: GB-101 (verified) added registry-side recovery - plan_suite_releases marks a version whose tag exists but is not on crates.io as SuitePlanAction::PublishPending instead of SkipClean, and execute_suite_plan then publishes it, so an interrupted publish heals on the next release --all. There is no analogue for git: SuitePlanAction has only ReleasePatch, ReleaseMinor, ReleaseMajor, PublishPending and SkipClean, and nothing inspects whether a member's commits or tags exist on origin. So a run that dies after commit+tag but before push (or one invoked with --skip-push, or a push that fails on the last repo) leaves HEAD sitting on an already-tagged commit; the next release --all sees zero commits since the tag, reports Skip (Clean), and the remote stays behind indefinitely while the run reports success. Verified in this workspace 2026-10-28 that routine local work is always released (any commit after the tag makes a repo non-clean and origin/main matched local HEAD~1 in every 'clean' member), so this is strictly a recovery/idempotency gap. Proposed fix, mirroring GB-101: add SuitePlanAction::PushPending (or a combined Reconcile action) set when the member's HEAD is tagged but branch or tag is absent from origin, detected with the existing sync_model::calculate_divergence (BranchDivergence::Ahead(n)) rather than new git plumbing, and have execute_suite_plan push it; consider uniting push and publish reconciliation into one end-of-run repair pass so a half-finished repository is healed by re-running instead of being reported as success. Acceptance: a release interrupted between tag and push is completed by re-running release --all, a clean-but-behind member is never reported as success, and the new action is covered by plan/execute tests.

task.title: Make miter clones trustworthy as a suite-wide duplication gate
task.description: Evidence from a live run on outfeed 2026-10-28 (miter clones --path outfeed --min-lines 20): 108 functions analysed, 32 pairs at similarity >= 0.90, of which 30 are test functions and only 2 are production code. The two production pairs are not actionable: mcp_sync.rs:20 (23 lines) vs synthesis.rs:47 (29 lines), and sync.rs:14 (22 lines) vs push.rs:34 (96 lines), both reported at 90.6% - a 22-line and a 96-line function cannot be a structural clone, so the metric is scale-invariant and a size-ratio guard is missing. Additional gaps: JSON emits similarity as a string ("1.0000") plus hamming_distance, which is awkward for typed consumers; there is no exclude/include filter, so tests/ and *_tests.rs dominate every report and bury production duplication; and there is no per-repository summary, making a workspace-wide scan hard to read. Acceptance: a workspace-wide run reports production duplication without test noise, no pair where one side is more than 25% longer than the other, and similarity is a JSON number.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-155 — Cut the Meta-Harness Suite Release

> **Epic Key:** `GB-155`  
> **Scope:** `workspace` + `outfeed`  
> **Status:** Planned — runbook ready, execute after the contracts publish

---

## 1. Objective

Give the meta-harness its own release: a `suite.lock` pinning all eleven repositories, a root changelog
section, and an annotated `suite-v<version>` snapshot tag, behind a certified gate.

Current state (2026-10-28): the root has **no git remote**, **no `suite.lock`**, and one historical tag
`suite-v0.1.0-beta.2`, so the next snapshot derives as **`0.1.0-beta.3`**.

`outfeed release --suite` already implements the mechanics but has never run end to end.

---

## 2. Pre-Release Checklist

1. Every member clean, on `main`, and pushed (`outfeed sync --all --status-only` shows no divergence).
2. Tier 3 matrix green across all eleven repos: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
   `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`,
   `miter contracts`, `outfeed lockfiles`, `chalkline docs check --workspace`
   (expect `12 targets audited, 108 present, 0 missing, 0 drifted`).
3. `gaugeblock-contracts` and `gaugeblock-common` published at `0.1.0-beta.3`-independent version
   `0.1.0-beta.1` **before** any member that depends on them.
4. `suite.lock` generated and committed, pinning all eleven repositories with exact commits.
5. Root `CHANGELOG.md` gains an ecosystem section listing every member version.
6. Annotated tag `suite-v0.1.0-beta.3` on the root.
7. Decision on a root remote: `push_repo` cannot push a repository without one, and the harness
   history is currently single-copy on this machine.
8. Delete `outfeed/PERF_AUDIT_PLAN.md` once the release is out (it is a stray; its content lives in
   the ledger, the tickets, and the commit messages).

---

## 3. Runbook

```bash
# 0. Rebuild the tooling so the installed outfeed has lockfiles/override/waves.
cargo install --path outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli --force

# 1. Publish the foundation first (irreversible; crates.io rate-limits new crates).
outfeed publish common --dry-run      # packages both crates
outfeed publish common                # real upload; expect a 429 cooldown on the 2nd crate

# 2. Confirm the contracts are visible before members reference them.
for c in gaugeblock-contracts gaugeblock-common; do
  curl -s https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c | python3 -c \
    "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['crate']['max_version'])"
done

# 3. Release the members (11 repositories, common first because it is wave 0).
outfeed release --all --no-llm --dry-run   # inspect the plan table first
outfeed release --all --yes --no-llm

# 4. Meta-harness snapshot (writes suite.lock, root changelog, suite-v tag).
outfeed release --suite --suite-version 0.1.0-beta.3 --yes --skip-publish --skip-install

# 5. Push everything, including members that were clean before this pass.
outfeed push --all
```

---

## 4. Gotchas learned the hard way

* **`common` proposes the wrong version.** With no tag baseline the calculator overshoots to
  `0.1.0-beta.2`; use `outfeed release common --override-version 0.1.0-beta.1`. A second pass with the
  same override is a clean no-op (`already released as v0.1.0-beta.1`).
* **`outfeed release --all` must run from the harness root**; from inside a member it sees no members
  and reports "0 repositories".
* **A push failure is invisible on a re-run.** `release --all` self-heals only the registry half
  (`PublishPending`); a repo tagged locally but never pushed reports `Skip (Clean)` next time
  (`GB-153`). Check `git log origin/main..HEAD` per repo before declaring victory.
* **crates.io 429s quote the deadline in the body**, not a `Retry-After` header; `GB-140` handles it,
  but a three-attempt budget cannot outlast a 10-per-hour new-crate limit — space uploads out.
* **Never run two `storypole` mutations in parallel**: appends spliced two JSON events onto one line
  twice today. `GB-147` makes the append atomic, but keep mutations serial until it is trusted.
* **`git add <dir> Cargo.lock` aborts staging entirely in a repo that ignores it**, and
  `git commit -q` then fails silently (`GB-150`). All eleven repos now track a fresh lockfile.

> **Epic Key:** `GB-157`
> **Scope:** `miter` (new crate, two re-export shims), then `dado` and `batten`

## 1. Objective

Move the grammar-level surface — language taxonomy, grammar table, parser construction, syntax
diagnostics — into a `miter-syntax` crate, so a consumer that only needs to *parse* or *name a
format* stops linking the analysis stack.

Evidence (measured, not assumed):

| Consumer | Imports from `miter-engine` | Needs the analysis stack? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `chalkline` | `inspect_workspace`, `WorkspaceInventory`, `PublicTypeInventory` | yes |
| `benchwork` | `inspect_workspace`, `WorkspaceInventory`, `ToolchainInventory` | yes |
| `batten` | `Language` only (3 uses) | **no** |
| `dado` | `polyglot` only (3 lines, the GB-148 adapters) | **no** |
| `joiner` | `Language` + `security::scrub_source_text` | only for the scrubber → `GB-158` |
| `rabbet` | `Language` + `security::{…}` | only for the scrubber → `GB-158` |

`miter-engine` today pulls `miter-ast`, `miter-storage` (redb), `redb`, `rayon`, `sqlparser`, `hcl`,
`dockerfile-parser`, `serde_yaml`, `globset`, `toml`. `batten` and `dado` link all of it to obtain an
enum naming thirteen formats, or to parse one string.

Target: `miter-engine`'s dependents go from six to two, with no functional change anywhere.

---

## 2. Constraints discovered before writing code

1. **`grammar_for` cannot move alone.** It lives at
   `miter-ast/src/extract/grammar.rs:83` and takes `miter_ast::Language`. Moving the table without the
   taxonomy creates a cycle (`miter-ast → miter-syntax → miter-ast`). Both move together.
2. **The `From` impls must move too (orphan rule).** `polyglot/contracts.rs` (50 lines) defines
   `impl From<PolyglotLanguage> for WireLanguage` **and** `impl From<WireLanguage> for PolyglotLanguage`.
   Once `PolyglotLanguage` lives in another crate, neither impl may stay in `miter-engine`. So
   `miter-syntax` depends on `gaugeblock-contracts`, which is correct — contracts is the bottom layer
   and the conversions are what keep the two taxonomies in lockstep.
3. **`polyglot/language.rs` is 246 lines** — four from the hard 250 limit and 46 over the soft target.
   It must not be moved verbatim; split it while moving.
4. **`miter-ast` keeps its semantics.** `FunctionNode`, `Param`, `parse_source`, `signature_of` and the
   indexer visitor stay; only the taxonomy and the grammar table leave. `miter-ast` re-exports both so
   `miter_ast::{Language, grammar_for}` keep resolving.

---

## 3. Slices (each a branch, a gate, and an atomic commit)

### Slice 1 — create the crate and shim the surface (`miter`)
Branch `feat/miter-syntax-crate`.

* `crates/syntax/` → package `miter-syntax`, `version.workspace = true`, `[lints] workspace = true`.
* Move `Language`/`PolyglotLanguage` out of `ast_indexer/src/extract/mod.rs` **split** so no file is near
  the limit: `language/mod.rs` (variants, `name`, `from_extension`, `from_path`, `from_file_name`,
  `is_declarative`) and `language/formats.rs` (the `EXTENSIONS` table, ~90 lines).
* Move `extract/grammar.rs::grammar_for` unchanged; it becomes `miter_syntax::grammar_for`.
* Move `polyglot/contracts.rs` verbatim (the two `From` impls).
* Move `polyglot/syntax.rs` (158 lines) unchanged.
* `miter-ast`: depend on `miter-syntax`; `pub use miter_syntax::{Language, grammar_for};` so
  `miter_ast::{Language, grammar_for}` and the `extract` re-export list keep working.
* `miter-engine`: depend on `miter-syntax`; `polyglot/mod.rs` re-exports the taxonomy, conversions and
  diagnostics at today's paths, so no downstream import changes in this slice.

Gate: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo nextest run --workspace` (baseline 238 tests).

### Slice 2 — repoint `dado`
Branch `feat/dado-miter-syntax`. Replace `miter-engine` with `miter-syntax` in `dado-core`; the
`ast_check` adapter changes one import path. Drop the dead `miter-ast` dependency too (declared today,
never used). Gate: `cargo nextest run -p dado-core` (baseline 14).

### Slice 3 — repoint `batten`
Branch `feat/batten-miter-syntax`. Three `Language` uses. Gate: batten workspace suite.

### Slice 4 — verify
`storypole verify GB-157` with the dependency counts before and after; leave `joiner`/`rabbet` for
`GB-158`.

---

## 4. Risks and how they are handled

* **Re-export drift.** A shim that silently diverges from the real path is how `GB-148` began. Slice 1
  re-exports rather than aliases (`pub use`), so there is exactly one definition.
* **Crate version coupling.** All miter crates share `version.workspace = true` and publish in lockstep,
  so a fourth crate adds a publish target (handled by `outfeed publish`'s topological walk), not a
  version to coordinate. No version changes are made in this ticket; the bump belongs to the next release.
* **Test coverage moves with the code.** The six `syntax_diagnostics_tests` and the language contract
  test move into `miter-syntax`'s own `tests/`, so the new crate is not shipped untested.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-160 — Suite Dependency and Feature Strategy Audit

> **Epic Key:** `GB-160` **Scope:** all eleven repositories + `miter` capability **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Objective

Decide, from evidence, where a shared crate or a Cargo feature is warranted across the suite — and
where the honest answer is "leave it alone".

This exists because one extraction was right and three were guesses. `gaugeblock-contracts` was a
*layering* problem: six members carried copies of the same 42 wire types, ~890 lines came out, and the
repointing was mechanical. `miter-syntax`, `miter-inventory` and `gaugeblock-security` were proposed on
direct-dependency counts; `cargo tree` then showed every consumer already reaches `miter-engine`
transitively through `chalkline-core`, so repointing would have removed **zero crates**. A hunch about
weight is not a measurement.

---

## 2. The framing this audit applies

| Mechanism | Right when | Tonight's example |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Crate extraction** | the *direction* of a dependency must change | `contracts` must sit beneath every member |
| **Cargo feature** | it is the same code in optional *weight* | `tokio` — you select the parts you need |
| **Do nothing** | one consumer, or the heavy dependency is genuinely needed | `chalkline`/`benchwork` need the inventory |

Most "split this out" instincts are the middle row wearing the top row's clothes.

---

## 3. Decision criteria (all three, or the answer is no)

1. **At least two consumers** use it — proved by `miter references`, not by intent or by a symbol's name.
2. **A measured reduction** in at least one consumer: fewer transitive crates *or* less clean build time.
3. **No dependency cycle**, and no heavy dependency pushed *down* onto every consumer.

Corollary: the audit is allowed to recommend deleting a crate, merging two, or adding nothing.

---

## 4. Evidence to collect

* `cargo tree -p <crate> -e normal` per consumer — total transitive size, and `-i <dep>` for the path.
* `cargo build -p <crate> --timings` on the heaviest consumers, before and after any change.
* `miter references/impact` for each candidate module — is it shared, or parochial?
* `miter clones` — duplication that would *justify* extraction.
* `miter skeleton` — the real size of an extracted API surface.
* `miter contracts` — schema drift after any move.

---

## 5. Phases

**P0 — Capability.** `miter` cannot currently answer the central question. `references` and `impact`
work per symbol; nothing aggregates *crate-to-crate* edges with symbol counts, and nothing understands
`#[cfg(feature = ...)]`. Add `miter deps`: per consumer crate, the provider crates it imports from and
how many distinct symbols, plus which items sit behind a feature gate. Without it this audit is
anecdote.

**P1 — Measure.** Run the evidence collection across all eleven repositories. No edits, no branches in
other repos.

**P2 — Report.** One section per repository: current dependency weight, candidates found, and a verdict
of *extract* / *feature* / *leave*, each with the numbers behind it. Publish as
`.gaugeblock/reports/dependency-strategy-audit.md` (or the repo's chosen doc path).

**P3 — Batch.** Group the surviving recommendations into one implementation epic, ordered so that each
step is independently gateable and bisectable.

---

## 6. Exit criteria

* Every repository has a written verdict, including the ones the audit clears.
* Every *extract* verdict cites a consumer count and a measured delta.
* `GB-157`, `GB-158`, `GB-159` are each explicitly closed, rescoped, or promoted with data.
* No production code changed during P0-P2 beyond the new `miter deps` capability.

---

## 7. Known constraints

* Local development resolves cross-repo crates through `.cargo/config.toml` `[patch.crates-io]`, so
  `cargo tree` reflects the working copies — good for honesty, but it means tree sizes are
  workspace-local and must be recorded as such.
* `chalkline-core` is the pivot: its use of `inspect_workspace` is why six repositories carry
  `miter-engine`'s 165-crate subtree. Any verdict that ignores that edge is wrong.
* No pushes, releases, publishes or version bumps are part of this epic.

description: Tier 1 of the miter deps capability that GB-160 depends on, and the only tier needed for the audit to run. task.description: Tier 2 of miter deps: the flags that turn the audit verdicts into measurements. Naming: --what-if is primary with --simulate-extract as a visible alias; --extract was rejected because it reads as mutation, deps is read-only, and miter slice already owns how to extract. (2) --layers [--check] reads ordered layers from workspace.metadata.gaugeblock.layers and fails on upward edges - the architectural fitness function that turns crate strategy into a gate. (3) --budget [--max-crates N] fails when a consumer transitive tree grows, so adding regex to a core crate is caught in review. plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-165 — Live Deterministic Trace Capture

> **Key:** `GB-165` **Scope:** `storypole` (owner), `common` (schema), `joiner` (consumer) **Status:** Slice 1 done

## 1. Decisions (settled, do not relitigate)

**`storypole verify <KEY>` is the single owner of post-task capture.** `outfeed gate` is a
*stateless, repeatable* check run many times mid-branch; emitting there would write duplicate
intermediate traces before a task is finished. `verify` is the one state transition where
`base_commit_sha`, `head_commit_sha`, `commit_shas` and the task context are known and immutable.

**Idempotency key: `(task_key, head_commit_sha)`.** One trace per verified head, even if `verify` is
re-run. A re-run with a new head is a new trace.

**No storypole → joiner Cargo edge.** Trace capture must not create a dependency cycle. The record
type already exists in `joiner-core` (`AnonymizedSynthesisTrace`, `TelemetryTier::{Bronze,Silver,Gold}`,
`assign_telemetry_tier`), so **move those two types into `gaugeblock-contracts`** and have both
storypole and joiner use them. Inventing a second schema on the storypole side is the drift that
`GB-148` was made of.

## 2. Slices

1. **`.gitignore` for derived state — done** (`harness/feat-live-trace-capture`). Six derived paths
   ignored, three canonical paths still tracked, verified with `git check-ignore` both ways.
2. **Schema move** into `gaugeblock-contracts`; `joiner-core` re-exports so its paths keep working.
3. **Spool writer in `storypole-core`**: append one JSONL line to
   `<canonical .gaugeblock>/spool/outbox.jsonl`, creating the directory; scrubbed via the same rules
   joiner applies; returns the record so the caller can log it.
4. **Hook in `verify_task`**: after the receipt is recorded, extract the functions added in
   `base..head` (git diff + miter symbol lookup), emit one Silver trace per function, and degrade to
   a `[skip]` warning when `miter` is absent rather than failing verification.
5. **Dogfood protocol** codified in `AGENTS.md`: `dado contract` for new wire types,
   `dado render` + `batten validate` for batches.

## 3. Acceptance

* Verifying `GB-165` itself writes the first live Silver trace to `.gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl`.
* A second `verify` on the same head writes nothing (idempotency).
* Traces contain no secrets: `CLINE_API_KEY` and friends never appear in a record.

task.title: Give miter an explicit workspace root and wire the gate contracts step to a suite index
task.description: Multi-repo indexing already works - miter index takes any path, so indexing the harness root yields one database covering all eleven members. Two gaps stop outfeed gate from using it. FIRST, staleness: the installed binary is 0.1.0-beta.4 and resolves the default database to <cwd>/.miter/miter.redb, while the source documents <workspace_root>/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb - miter/.miter/ exists on disk as proof the old path was used, and there is no index at the harness root at all, so the contracts step fails from every member with run miter index first. Rebuild before any sweep. SECOND, path semantics: there is no global -d/--dir and no environment override, so the database location is implicitly cwd-relative; running from a member can never see a suite index. Options, in preference order: a global --dir that sets the workspace root for every subcommand, or a MITER_DB environment variable honoured by every command, or explicit --db on the gate contracts step. Recommend the global --dir for symmetry with outfeed and chalkline, plus outfeed gate gaining an --index-db so the contracts step reads the suite index while gating a single repository. Also worth a convenience: miter index --workspace that indexes every member under a root into one database.

task.title: benchwork bulk archive stalls at fifty tasks with no progress or error surfacing
task.description: Bulk archiving verified tasks in benchwork stops after fifty (150 tasks to 101) and re-running does not advance. Investigation so far rules out the backend loop: bulk_archive_tasks_service simply iterates the ids it is given, has no cap, and archive_task is idempotent and has no status guard - it returns Ok immediately when a task is already Archived. That combination explains the stall exactly: re-selecting the same already-archived batch yields zero progress that reports as success. No LIMIT or take() exists in the DAG query or the bulk handler, so the fifty most likely originates in the UI selection or fetch layer - next diagnostic is to log the request body length and compare it with the number of verified tasks the DAG response contains. Two separate defects sit alongside it: BulkArchiveResult already carries an errors vector that nothing surfaces in the UI, and there is no progress indication for a long batch. Proposed fix: archive by filter server-side (archive all Verified) instead of by id list, stream progress counts, surface the errors vector, and guard archive_task to Completed/Verified/Closed so a stray id cannot silently no-op.

title: benchwork bulk archive: writes land in governing ledgers but the unified index never reflects them
description: Evidence gathered after the first investigation, which had the wrong emphasis. Archiving IS writing: counting Archived transitions per ledger gives 35 in .gaugeblock/storypole/ledger.jsonl and 2-4 in every member ledger (batten 2, benchwork 3, chalkline 2, dado 2, joiner 2, miter 3, outfeed 4, rabbet 2, sawhorse 3, storypole 3), because with_governing_store routes each task to its governing store - member ledger when the task is repo scoped, root ledger otherwise. Meanwhile storypole list still reports 116 Verified, which is the unified SQLite index, not the ledgers. So the operation is not failing to archive; the index does not reflect member-ledger archives, and there is no way to ask it to: storypole workspace offers only list, init and distribute, with no sync. Contributing factors to confirm: StorypoleWorkspaceStore::open calls sync_all_members, which swallows unreadable ledgers inside if-let-Ok and therefore under-reports rather than failing, and the replay-ordering defect recorded in GB-79 concatenates root events before member events instead of merging by timestamp - so a member-scoped archive can be overwritten in the index by an older root snapshot. Second defect stands independently: BulkArchiveResult.errors is never surfaced and there is no progress indicator, so a quiet partial result looks like success. Proposed order: fix the index reflect problem (sync command plus GB-79 ordering), then archive-by-filter with streamed progress, then guard archive_task to Completed/Verified/Closed. Diagnostic to keep: compare the per-ledger Archived count against the status histogram from storypole list.

task.title: Add a ledger integrity and index-reconciliation audit to storypole
task.description: There is no integrity check for the distributed ledger set, and GB-177 exposed why that matters. A structural audit of all eleven ledgers today passes cleanly: 1067 events, zero unparsable lines, zero duplicate lines, so nothing is corrupt. But the status views disagree wildly - the unified index reports 116 Verified while a naive per-ledger replay reports 58 Archived, zero Verified and 98 InProgress. Part of that gap is my replay being naive (claim and verification events carry state this script does not model), which is precisely the argument for the tool: you cannot reason about ledger truth without the real replay. Scope: storypole ledger verify (or workspace verify) that (1) parses every line in every ledger and reports the offending file and line, (2) flags exact duplicate events, (3) detects the same task appearing in two ledgers with divergent histories, (4) reconciles index against ledger replay and reports the difference per status, and (5) reports claims whose leases have expired as a separate count. Acceptance: running it on the current suite reproduces the 1067/0/0 structural result and prints the index-versus-ledger delta as its headline. Pairs with GB-177 (index does not reflect member archives) and GB-79 (replay ordering), and should land before any further bulk mutation of task state.

Three tests use a real store: a healthy ledger replays clean and reports the created task as ready; an appended duplicate plus a garbage line are each counted once while the task still replays; discovery covers root plus member files and the formatter renders. Gates: fmt clean, clippy workspace all-targets -D warnings clean, nextest 36/36. SCOPE NOT YET DONE: no CLI subcommand is wired yet, so storypole ledger verify is not runnable from the shell, and index-versus-ledger reconciliation is deliberately not in this module - it needs the unified store, which the audit does not open. Both are the next slice.

title: benchwork bulk archive archived 58 of about 160 verified tasks
description: MEASURED with the new storypole ledger-reconcile, which corrects the earlier theory on this ticket. Ledger replay: 205 tasks, archived 58, verified 102, ready 19, deferred 14, triage 9, blocked 2, in progress 1. Unified index after re-sync: identical for every status except archived, which the index shows as 0 because archived tasks are deliberately hidden from default backlog queries. So the index is NOT stale and NOT over-reporting: it agrees with the ledger exactly. What is real is the shortfall - the bulk archive reached 58 of roughly 160 verified tasks, and nothing surfaced either the shortfall or any error. Two live defects remain: the caller selects only a slice of the verified set (no limit exists in bulk_archive_tasks_service, so the selection is client-side), and BulkArchiveResult.errors plus progress are never shown in the UI. task.title: Model archived as a state orthogonal to status so archived tasks stay viewable and filterable
task.description: Design: archived is a state, not a status. TaskStatus::Archived (contracts task.rs:49) collapses two orthogonal dimensions into one enum, so archiving destroys the status a task actually held. Consequences seen in use: a task archived while Verified cannot be read back as Verified-and-archived; filtering by archived returns nothing because archived is no longer a status anyone filters for; Show Archived in the DagBoard toggles a separate flag rather than a status, so the two views disagree; and archiving from an arbitrary status is a question with no good answer, which is why the proposed status guard on archive_task was wrong and is withdrawn. Intended model: keep status intact and add an orthogonal archived dimension to TaskNode (archived_at: Option<u64>, serde default and skip_serializing_if so existing ledgers and JSON stay valid), replay Archived transitions as setting that field rather than overwriting status, have queries hide archived by default and include them when asked, and let any task in any status be archived. Code trail for the UI symptom: DagBoardPanel sends include_archived=true, DagQuery binds it (model/dag.rs:21), dag_service/query.rs:63 honours it, so the drop is downstream in the view or in how nodes are filtered after the query - worth confirming with a request log before changing the UI. Migration: a replay change plus a contracts field, so it lands with a version bump rather than inline.

description: MEASURED (ledger-reconcile): replay gives 205 tasks - archived 58, verified 102, ready 19, deferred 14, triage 9, blocked 2, in progress 1 - and the unified index agrees on every status except archived, which it hides by design. So the index is not stale; the bulk archive simply covered 58 of roughly 160 verified tasks and reported nothing. Remaining defects: the caller selects only a slice (no server-side cap exists), and BulkArchiveResult.errors plus progress are never surfaced. WITHDRAWN: the proposed status guard on archive_task. GB-179 establishes that archived is a state orthogonal to status and that a task must be archivable from any status, so a guard would encode the wrong model. Test procedure: ledger-reconcile before and after; archived must rise by the verified count and every other status must stay in agreement.

acceptance_criteria: Repair of already-archived tasks verified: every one of the 58 archive events records a from status, distribution 57 verified and 1 ready, so no data was lost and a full restore is possible from the ledger alone

A task archived while Ready is readable as Ready-and-archived, proving the archived dimension is orthogonal rather than a status

Cascade measured before starting: TaskNode has no Default derive and there are 11 literal constructions, of which only 1 uses ..Default::default(), so adding archived_at touches roughly 10 sites across four repositories - contracts 2 (tests), storypole 4 (ops/mutations, ops/graph, two tests), joiner 3 (two tests plus engine_loop), benchwork 2 (integration and archive_service tests). Plan the edits per repo and gate each, rather than one sweeping edit.

plan.summary: Upgrade benchwork/web to native Vite 8 (Rolldown/Oxc) and TypeScript 7/tsgo, plus Rust dev-profile tuning, timing every slice cold and warm against the 29.32s GB-71 baseline
plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-180 — Native Frontend Toolchain + Rust Dev-Profile Tuning

> **Key:** `GB-180` **Scope:** `benchwork/web`, `benchwork/Cargo.toml` **Status:** Planned

## 1. Baseline (measured under GB-71, Law 12)

| Phase | npm | Bun | Toolchain |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| install, cold cache | 27.89 s | 13.21 s | npm 12.0.2 / Bun 1.4.4 |
| install, warm cache | 15.22 s | 1.13 s | same |
| build (`tsc -b` + `vite build`) | 27.58 s | **29.32 s** | TypeScript 5.7, Vite 6 |

Environment: macOS Apple silicon, Node 24.21.0. Timed phases run **sequentially**; parallel runs were
shown to produce noise when `GB-71` was first measured.

## 2. Method (every slice, every time)

1. `rm -rf node_modules` for a cold phase, keep it for the warm phase.
2. Time with `/usr/bin/time -p sh -c '<commands>'` so one number covers the whole phase.
3. Record: platform, tool versions, `bun.lock` state, cold/warm, and the exact commands.
4. Write it in three places - commit message, this ticket, and `benchwork/CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## 3. Slices, each independently measured and committed

| # | Change | Risk |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 3.1 | `incremental`, `skipLibCheck`, `tsBuildInfoFile` in `tsconfig` | low |
| 3.2 | Native typecheck: `typescript@7` if published, else `@typescript/native-preview` (`tsgo`) | medium - peer ranges may pin 5/6 |
| 3.3 | `vite@^8.1` via `rolldown-vite` first if the jump spans Vite 7 | medium |
| 3.4 | Config key migration: `rollupOptions`→`rolldownOptions`, `manualChunks`→`codeSplitting.groups`, `esbuildOptions`→`rolldownOptions`, `esbuild`→`oxc` | medium |
| 3.5 | `build.reportCompressedSize: false`, `server.forwardConsole: true` | low |
| 3.6 | Rust `[profile.dev]`/`[profile.test]`: `incremental = false`, `debug = 1`, `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` | medium |

**Config names in 3.4 are expectations, not verified facts.** Each rename is checked against the
installed Vite 8 documentation before the commit that claims it.

## 4. Acceptance

* One table per slice: cold and warm, before and after, same machine.
* `bun run build` still produces a bundle that loads (`bun run preview` + a Playwright smoke run).
* `outfeed gate -d benchwork` green after every slice - this is a web change, but the gate also covers
  docs and the Rust crates that consume `web/dist`.
* Rust slice reports `outfeed gate` wall time and `target/` size before and after, and says plainly if
  it regresses.

# Task Plan: GB-182 — One spool file, one record shape

> **Key:** `GB-182` **Scope:** `common/crates/gaugeblock-contracts`, `storypole-core`, `storypole-cli`,
> `joiner-core`, `rabbet-core` **Status:** Verified

## 1. Symptom

A single `<canonical .gaugeblock>/spool/outbox.jsonl` held records from two writers, and the same file
could not be read by one parser:

| Writer | Line it appended | Readable by `rabbet`? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `storypole verify` | bare `AnonymizedSynthesisTrace` | no - no envelope, no hash |
| `joiner fill` | `{"trace":…,"content_hash":…,"sync_status":…,"recorded_at_ms":…}` | yes |
| `rabbet` model | its own `SpoolEntry` with `sync_status: String` | accepted any status verbatim |

The live outbox at `GB-179` close-out held exactly this mix: 2 bare traces (GB-165, GB-167) and 2
`joiner` envelopes.

## 2. Decisions

1. **One owner.** `SpoolEntry` and `SyncStatus` move to `gaugeblock-contracts`, beside the trace they
   wrap. Everything else re-exports; no path breaks.
2. **The envelope is the wire type.** A bare trace is not a record: a reader cannot recompute a hash
   the writer never recorded.
3. **One hash implementation.** `SpoolEntry::hash_trace` (SHA-256 over `serde_json` bytes, lowercase
   hex) is what writers record and what the `rabbet` gate recomputes. `joiner`'s `compute_trace_hash`
   and `rabbet`'s `compute_canonical_trace_hash` delegate to it; both keep their signature.
4. **`sync_status` stays a snake_case string.** `pending` | `synced` | `rejected` as an enum keeps
   today's outboxes parseable, so migration is additive rather than a rewrite of every file.
5. **Migration is idempotent and non-destructive.** `storypole spool migrate` rewrites bare-trace
   lines, leaves envelopes byte-for-byte, preserves unparsable lines verbatim, and writes only when
   something changed - a second run reports 0.

## 3. Steps and gates

| # | Step | Gate |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 3.1 | `gaugeblock-contracts`: own `SpoolEntry`/`SyncStatus` + `from_trace`/`hash_trace` | `cargo nextest -p gaugeblock-contracts` |
| 3.2 | `storypole-core`: write envelopes, add `migrate_spool`/`normalize_spool_text` | `cargo nextest -p storypole-core` |
| 3.3 | `storypole-cli`: `spool migrate [--dry-run]`; split `args.rs` under 250 LOC | `storypole spool --help` |
| 3.4 | `joiner-core`: re-export shared types, delegate the hash, drop `sha2` | `cargo nextest -p joiner-core` |
| 3.5 | `rabbet-core`: consume shared types, delegate the gate hash | `cargo nextest -p rabbet-core` |
| 3.6 | Docs: `CONTRACTS.md` §6, `common/SPEC.md`, `storypole/README.md` | `chalkline docs check` 0 drift |

Tier 2 for every repo: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D
warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`, `cargo test --doc --workspace`.

## 4. Evidence (run, not asserted)

* Gate matrix green in `common`, `storypole`, `joiner`, `rabbet` (fmt/clippy/nextest/doc all exit 0).
* `storypole spool migrate --dry-run` -> `2 legacy record(s) would be rewritten`; `migrate` -> `2`
  rewritten; second run -> `no legacy records to migrate (already canonical)`.
* Both `joiner` envelopes kept their hashes across the migration (`e9750e36…`, `b2f96682…`).
* Ingest proof over the live outbox via `POST /api/v1/traces` on `rabbet serve`:
  `{"accepted":5,"duplicates":0,"rejected":0}` - 4 migrated/legacy records plus the GB-182 trace
  `storypole verify` wrote through the new envelope writer.

## 5. Deferred, not fixed here

* `benchwork` owns a third writer path; it now builds against the shared type but has no
  outbox-migration verb of its own.
* Outbox compaction (rewriting `sync_status` in place) is still `joiner mark_synced` only.

# Task Plan: GB-189 — `gaugeblock-workspace`

> **Scope:** `common/crates/gaugeblock-workspace` **Parent epic:** `GB-128` **Status:** Planned

## 1. Why this crate exists

Every tool answers "which repository am I in, and where is `.gaugeblock/`?" differently:

| Tool | Today |
|:--|:--|
| `storypole` | `StorypoleStore::open` walks up from `--dir` for `.storypole`; `telemetry::spool_path` takes `.parent()` of the dot dir and hopes |
| `outfeed` | takes a positional root and guesses members from a hard-coded list |
| `chalkline` | `-d` / `--workspace` heuristics |
| `benchwork` | enumerates repos from its own config |
| `joiner` | `JoinerConfig::default_spool_dir` re-implements the spool rule |

That is five answers to one question, and the worktree case (`.git` is a *file* pointing at the real
common dir) breaks all of them — which is precisely what `GB-169` needs to stop happening.

## 2. Boundary (frozen — see `common/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4)

**Owns:** `GaugeblockPaths` (canonical `.gaugeblock/` resolution), `WorkspaceTopology` (meta-harness
root, 11 member repositories, their `Cargo.toml` members), `SuiteConfig` (`.gaugeblock/config.toml`,
`.env`).

**Does not own:** any `git` subprocess. Worktree detection, `common_dir`, branches and commits are
`gaugeblock-git` (`GB-131`). This crate may call it, never the reverse.

## 3. Data contracts

```rust
pub struct GaugeblockPaths {
    pub repo_root: PathBuf,   // the checkout the caller asked about
    pub common_dir: PathBuf,  // git common dir: shared by every linked worktree
    pub dot_dir: PathBuf,     // <common_dir parent>/.gaugeblock — one per repository, not per worktree
}

impl GaugeblockPaths {
    pub fn resolve(start: &Path) -> Result<Self, WorkspaceError>;
    pub fn storypole_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    pub fn spool_outbox(&self) -> PathBuf;
}

pub struct WorkspaceTopology {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub members: Vec<MemberRepo>, // name, path, Cargo.toml packages
}

pub struct SuiteConfig { /* .gaugeblock/config.toml + .env, typed, no globals */ }
```

Invariants:

1. `dot_dir` is derived from the git common dir, so a linked worktree resolves to the *same*
   `.gaugeblock/` as its main checkout. A test must create a real linked worktree and assert it.
2. `WorkspaceTopology::discover` reads manifests; it never runs `cargo`.
3. `resolve` on a path outside any repository returns a typed error, never a fallback to
   `current_dir` — silent fallbacks are how split-brain state starts.

## 4. Steps

| # | Step | Gate |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `paths` module + linked-worktree fixture | `cargo nextest -p gaugeblock-workspace` |
| 2 | `topology` module: root discovery + 11 members + package names from `Cargo.toml` | fixture tree with two members |
| 3 | `config` module: typed `SuiteConfig` with `toml` + `.env` | fixture config + missing-file default |
| 4 | Re-point `storypole` (store + `spool_path`), `joiner` (`default_spool_dir`), `chalkline --workspace` | `cargo nextest --workspace` per repo |
| 5 | `outfeed` + `benchwork` member enumeration | Tier 3 |

## 5. What this buys `GB-169` and `GB-180`

* `GB-169` — a claimed worktree and the main checkout write one ledger and one spool because
  `GaugeblockPaths` says so; `storypole claim --worktree` becomes a `gaugeblock-git` worktree call plus
  a path value, not new path logic.
* `GB-180` — Panel 1 (multi-repo Docs Studio) needs the member list and per-repo `.gaugeblock/`
  resolution; it consumes `WorkspaceTopology` instead of hard-coding eleven names.

# Task Plan: GB-131 — `gaugeblock-git`

> **Scope:** `common/crates/gaugeblock-git` **Parent epic:** `GB-128` **Status:** Planned

## 1. Why this crate exists

Six places currently spawn `git` with `format!`-built command lines and parse stdout by hand:

| Owner | Duplicated calls |
|:--|:--|
| `storypole-core::git` | current branch, head sha, merge base, `rev-list` between shas |
| `outfeed-core::git` | dirty tree, commit + annotated tag, push, tag verify |
| `benchwork-core` | dirty tree, head sha, scoped commit for Panel 1 |
| `miter` (`deps --since`) | commit ranges |
| `rabbet` (backfill) | commit ranges, head sha |
| `scripts/*.sh` | branch, tags |

`GB-126` already collapsed the worst copy inside `outfeed`. This ticket generalizes the winner and
relocates it, it does not write a seventh wrapper.

## 2. Boundary (frozen — see `common/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4)

**Owns:** repository detection (`common_dir`, worktree vs main checkout), `worktree add/remove/prune/list`,
`rev-list`/`merge_base`/tag ranges, scoped `status`/`add`/`commit`/annotated `tag`, `push`.

**Does not own:** which repository to act on, `.gaugeblock/` resolution, workspace config, and any suite
type (`TaskNode`, `ReleasePlan`). A caller hands it a `Path` and typed arguments; it returns values or a
`thiserror` error carrying stderr. It never depends on `gaugeblock-workspace` — the edge is one-way
(`GB-189` -> `GB-131`).

## 3. Steps

| # | Step | Gate |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `repo` module: `common_dir`, `is_worktree`, `head_sha`, `current_branch`, `is_dirty` | `cargo nextest -p gaugeblock-git` with a temp repo + linked worktree fixture |
| 2 | `worktree` module: `add`, `remove`, `prune`, `list` returning typed `WorktreeInfo` | fixture asserts two worktrees share one `common_dir` |
| 3 | `history` module: `commits_between`, `merge_base`, `describe_range` (replaces `rev-list` string parsing) | fixture with a 3-commit range |
| 4 | `index` module: scoped `stage_paths` + `commit` returning a typed `CommitSummary` | fixture asserts only the named paths are staged (`GB-150` staging rule) |
| 5 | `remote` module: annotated `tag` + single-round-trip `push_branch_and_tag` | dry-run against a local bare remote |
| 6 | Delete `storypole-core::git`, `outfeed-core::git` and the benchwork copy; re-point callers | `cargo nextest --workspace` in each affected repo |
| 7 | `miter contracts` + `chalkline docs check` green | Tier 3 |

## 4. Consumers this unblocks

* `GB-169` — canonical `.gaugeblock` across worktrees needs step 2 and step 1 in that order.
* `GB-170` — benchwork agent pool needs `worktree add/remove/prune/list`.
* `GB-180` — Panel 1 atomic doc commits need step 4 (scoped staging, no `git add .`).
* `outfeed release` — needs step 5 for the single push.

## 5. Explicitly out of scope

* `codegen-units` tuning — moved to `GB-190` because it is a profile decision, not a crate boundary.
* Path/topology/config policy — `GB-189`.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-200 — Staged B crate strategy

> **Kind:** Epic **Status:** Planned **Decision date:** 2026-10-29
> **Phases:** GB-199 → GB-201 → GB-202 → Phase A (GB-131, GB-189, GB-130) → GB-203 → GB-204

## 1. The decision

Three strategies were on the table after the GB-194/GB-198 audit produced facts rather than
impressions:

| | What it buys | Why it was not chosen |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** Foundation only | `gaugeblock-git` + `gaugeblock-workspace`; mesh frozen by a gate | Leaves the six lateral edges and a 15.8k-LOC `miter-engine` in place, so the two largest measured problems stay unfixed |
| **B (chosen)** Foundation, then `miter-engine` split, then de-mesh | Fixes the two concentrated problems in an order where every intermediate state ships | — |
| **C** Consolidate workspaces | One lockfile, trivial cross-crate refactors | **Law 2 holds.** The eleven repositories stay standalone and independently publishable. C is rejected for this program, not deferred |

Because Law 2 holds, no phase may create a hard cross-repo build requirement. Foundation crates ship
from `common/` on their own cadence and consumers declare a minimum version. `.cargo/config.toml`
`[patch.crates-io]` stays a developer convenience, never a product dependency.

## 2. Fact base (measured 2026-10-29, miter 0.1.0-beta.4)

| Measurement | Command | Value |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Files over the 250 ceiling | `miter audit --path . --threshold 250` | **0** |
| Files in the 200-250 band | `miter audit --path . --threshold 200` | **70** - engine 21, benchwork root 9, storypole-core 5, storage 4, mcp 4 |
| Crates / import edges | `miter deps --path .` | **42 / 132** |
| Declared but unreferenced | `miter deps --path .` | **59** over nine repositories |
| `git` wrapper call sites | `grep Command::new("git")` | **66** across 24 files in outfeed, miter, storypole |
| Structural clones >= 0.90 | `miter clones` | 100 pairs, 17 cross-crate, shape-only on spot check (GB-197) |

In-degree tells the story: `gaugeblock-contracts` 17 in / 0 out is a proper foundation leaf;
`storypole-core` 17, `dado-core` 13, `sawhorse-core` 13, `miter-engine` 12 and `chalkline-core` 11 are
all hubs that also depend outward. That is a mesh, and only six of its edges are lateral:

| From | To | Sites |
|:--|:--|--:|
| `batten-core` | `dado-core` | 7 |
| `chalkline-core` | `miter-engine` | 12 |
| `chalkline-core` | `storypole-core` | 6 |
| `dado-core` | `chalkline-core` | 3 |
| `dado-core` | `miter-engine` | 2 |
| `chalkline-core` | `sawhorse-core` | 2 |

Two caveats are part of the fact base, not footnotes: `miter deps` currently counts test-fixture
strings as references (GB-199), and `miter clones` cannot yet separate structure from duplication
(GB-197). Neither number may drive a gate until the first is fixed.

## 3. Phases

### Phase 0 - make the numbers trustworthy (GB-199)
`miter deps` must stop counting raw-string fixtures and `#[cfg(test)]` bodies as proof of use.
**Exit:** two consecutive runs agree, and `miter-engine -> outfeed` / `-> storypole-core` are gone
from the graph.

### Phase 1a - purge the dead declarations (GB-201)
Baseline 59: batten 9, dado 9, rabbet 9, benchwork 7, chalkline 7, joiner 5, outfeed 5, sawhorse 4,
storypole 3. Remove what the scan cannot justify; keep a declaration only with a written reason
(derive-only use, feature enablement, build script).
**Exit:** `miter deps --path . --unused` is zero, with per-repo before/after recorded here and in the
commits.

### Phase 1b - freeze the mesh (GB-202)
`miter deps --layers` classifies every edge as foundation / domain / integrator, and `--check` fails on
a lateral domain edge or on any edge missing from `.gaugeblock/miter/layers-allowlist.toml`. The six
edges above seed that file, each entry carrying its ticket key, so day one is green and every entry is
tracked debt.

**Open decision, recommendation included:** wire `--check` into the Tier 3 gate (`outfeed gate`) rather
than per-repo CI, because the layer map is a suite property that no single repo can evaluate.

### Phase A - the no-regret foundation (GB-131, GB-189, GB-130)
* `gaugeblock-git` - 66 call sites across 24 files. Owns `common_dir`/worktree detection, worktree
  lifecycle, ref ranges, scoped staging and push. Consumers delete their wrappers; they do not
  re-export two copies.
* `gaugeblock-workspace` - `.gaugeblock/` resolution derived from the git common dir, 11-repo topology,
  `SuiteConfig`. Replaces the ~10-site derivation spread across storypole plus chalkline, dado, joiner.
* `gaugeblock-mcp` - evaluate, do not assume (GB-130): seven MCP servers duplicate JSON-RPC stdio
  boilerplate. Measure the duplicated surface first; a thin dispatch shim justifies a crate, tool
  schemas do not.

**Exit:** wrapper families deleted, path resolution has one owner, MCP decision recorded with its
measurement.

### Phase B1 - split `miter-engine` (GB-203)
15,776 LOC, 21 of the 70 band files, 12 dependents, four unrelated jobs:

| Target crate | Contents | Consumer evidence |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `miter-polyglot` | language visitors, grammars, markdown/html/typescript, syntax diagnostics | `miter-ast` already owns grammars; GB-157 wants this seam |
| `miter-inventory` | cargo_parser, clap_extractor, git_extractor, public_types_extractor, toolchain_extractor | used by audit, deps, doc generators |
| `miter-analysis` | audit, clones, contracts, cycles, deps, hygiene, impact, references, skeleton, slice | the heavy half, where GB-159's features belong |
| `miter-engine` | facade re-exporting the three | no consumer path may change |

Constraints: no new crate over roughly 5k LOC, no file over 250 lines, `cargo nextest --workspace`
green at every commit. The 21 band files are swept inside the series, not afterwards.

**Sequencing note:** extract `security` (GB-158) *before* this split. `joiner-core` depends on
`miter-engine` solely for `scrub_source_text`, so it is a rehearsal on a one-function surface and it
drops `miter-engine`'s in-degree from 12 to 11.

### Phase B2 - burn the six edges (GB-204)
Per call site choose exactly one treatment and record it:

* **(a)** move shared data types into `gaugeblock-contracts` / `gaugeblock-workspace`;
* **(b)** depend on the lower-layer `miter-polyglot` instead of the whole analysis stack;
* **(c)** invert control behind a trait or CLI boundary.

An edge leaves the allowlist only when its site count reaches zero, so partial progress never silences
the gate. **Exit:** allowlist empty, layers check green with no exceptions.

## 4. Measurement discipline (law 12)

Every phase writes before/after into its commit, its ticket, and the table in section 2. A phase that
finds no improvement says so. The two numbers to watch: band files (70 today) and lateral edges (6).

## 5. Non-goals

* No repo consolidation, no shared version train, no renames of published crate names.
* No gate on the 200-250 band - that is GB-195, advisory and per-repo.
* No new `common/` crate without a measured call-site count behind it.
* No temporary re-export of a wrapper a foundation crate was meant to replace.

## 6. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|:--|:--|
| Feature unification: optional deps in `miter-engine` resolve for all consumers at once | Physical split first (B1), features second (GB-159) |
| Allowlist rot becomes permanent permission | Every entry carries a ticket; B2 exits only with an empty file |
| Two crates wrap the same thing during migration | Phase A exit requires deletion, not delegation |
| A phase stalls and blocks the rest | Phase 1b freezes growth, so a stall costs progress, not correctness |

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-199 — `miter deps` must not count literals as references

> **Scope:** `miter/crates/engine/src/analysis/deps` **Parent:** `GB-200` **Status:** InProgress

## 1. Symptom

Reading the suite-wide graph after GB-198 showed two edges that cannot exist:

```
miter-engine -> outfeed          1 site
miter-engine -> storypole-core   1 site
```

Both came from `analysis/deps/tests.rs`, where the *fixture strings* contain lines like

```rust
let source = "pub mod outfeed;\nuse storypole_core::model::TaskNode;\n";
```

The scanner read every physical line of every `.rs` file as code, so data became proof of use, and a
fixture that exists to *test* the parser registered a module (`pub mod outfeed;`) as well.

This matters beyond two edges: every number produced by `miter deps` feeds the layer gate that
`GB-202` will introduce, and a gate built on phantom edges is worse than no gate.

## 2. Fix

A line is passed through `strip::code_only` before anything is matched. It removes:

* `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments (state carried across lines),
* ordinary string literals with backslash escapes,
* raw strings `r"..."`, `r#"..."#`, `r##"..."##`, including multi-line ones (state carried).

`declared_modules` uses the same stripper, so a fixture can no longer declare a module either.

Deliberate conservatism: an unterminated raw string or block comment swallows the remainder of the
file rather than guessing a close. Guessing is precisely what produced the false edges, and a missed
reference is cheaper than a fabricated dependency.

## 3. Proof

| Check | Expectation |
|:--|:--|
| `test_import_looking_content_inside_strings_is_not_a_reference` | fixture string, raw string and hashed raw string yield no roots and no modules |
| `test_a_multiline_raw_string_swallows_the_lines_it_covers` | only the `use` after the closing `"#;` is counted |
| `test_comments_hide_imports_but_real_code_after_a_block_comment_still_counts` | a trailing `/* */` does not swallow the statement before it |
| `miter deps --path miter` | `miter-engine -> outfeed` and `-> storypole-core` are gone |
| `miter deps --path .` | cross-repo edge count drops from 132 |

Gates: `cargo nextest run -p miter-engine` (165), `cargo clippy -p miter-engine -p miter-cli
--all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

## 4. Non-goals

* Not changing what counts as *use* otherwise: a dependency used only in `#[cfg(test)]` code still
  counts as used, because the declaration half of that problem belongs to `GB-201`.
* Not touching `miter clones`' similarity semantics (`GB-197`).

task.title: Discover models from the provider catalogue instead of assuming a fixed set
task.description: The owner wants cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 and asked whether model selection must stay static. It does not: the OpenAI-compatible provider already calls GET {base_url}/models in health_check and discards the body, and the live Cline catalogue answers 200 with 439 ids in OpenAI shape. So the path the VS Code extension uses is reachable from sawhorse today. Scope: a list_models method on the provider trait (default empty for embedded providers), a tolerant parser for the catalogue payload, implementation for openai_compat, and a sawhorse models command that prints what each provider advertises, marks the configured model, and flags when the configured id is not in the catalogue - which is exactly the cline-pass alias case, since the catalogue exposes deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 and zero cline-pass/ entries.
acceptance_criteria: sawhorse models lists every advertised id per OpenAI-compatible provider and exits zero
The configured model is marked, and a configured id absent from the catalogue is called out rather than hidden
Payload parsing is unit tested against OpenAI, wrapped and malformed bodies
Embedded providers report an empty list rather than failing

description: The owner wants cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 and asked whether model selection must stay static. It must not, but the first design was wrong in an important way. Discovery: the OpenAI-compatible provider already calls GET {base_url}/models in health_check and discards the body, and the live catalogue answers 200 with 439 ids in OpenAI shape, so the path the VS Code extension uses is reachable today. Constraint the owner corrected: ClinePass is a CURATED SET of fifteen documented ids, not a namespace, so prefixing an arbitrary catalogue id does not make it pass-eligible and a deprecated id (GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6, Kimi K2.7 Code, DeepSeek V4 Flash) stops working even though it may still be documented or cached. Verified against the live endpoint: cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 returns 200 at gateway cost 0 while the catalogue id deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 returns 402 insufficient_credits, so the catalogue describes what exists and says nothing about entitlement. Consequences for the implementation: the command must label ids as pass-eligible from a dated allowlist sourced from https://docs.cline.bot/getting-started/clinepass (refreshed by script, never inferred), must not suggest that prefixing works generally, and should grow an account-level probe that makes a minimal request so eligibility is verified rather than assumed.

acceptance_criteria: unused-deps
The pass set is refreshed by a script that diffs the docs markdown form (docs.cline.bot/getting-started/clinepass.md), not by editing a const by hand
sawhorse models --probe verifies the configured id with one minimal request, so a deprecated or unbillable id is reported as such rather than as a generic error

task.title: benchwork status counts fold archived tasks into their pre-archive status
task.description: benchwork capabilities reports blocked 4, deferred 16, ready 26, triage 11, verified 180 with no archived key, while storypole ledger-reconcile reports archived 59, verified 123, ready 26, deferred 16, triage 9, blocked 4 and says index and ledger agree. Totals match at 237, and the deltas are exactly the archived population: 180 - 123 = 57 and 11 - 9 = 2, which sums to 59. task.title: Hole filling should disable the reasoning trace, not just raise the token budget
task.description: GB-206 raised the fill budget from 1024 to 8192 and its short probe then succeeded, but a longer prompt fails the same way: the live run against cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 with max_tokens 8192 still returned empty response content, and sawhorse diagnostic names the cause again - the thinking trace consumed the budget before any content. Raising a number is a mitigation whose headroom depends on prompt size. The contract already models the real fix: ReasoningEffort::None makes the payload send thinking disabled plus reasoning_effort none, and a deterministic code filler does not need a reasoning trace at all. Set it on the hole-filler request, keep the larger budget as headroom for output, and assert both in the unit test.
acceptance_criteria: The hole-filler request disables the reasoning trace via ReasoningEffort::None
A longer probe that previously failed now fills successfully against the live reasoning model
The budget stays large enough for output, so the two mitigations are independent

receipt.summary: ReasoningEffort::None on the hole-filler request; joiner-core tests, clippy and fmt green; the probe that failed at max_tokens 8192 now fills in one attempt with a correct sliding-window implementation, outbox 20 to 22

task.title: Gold pairs require a syntax failure, so the repair path almost never fires
task.description: Two fill runs now succeed on the first attempt, and the corpus is 22 records with zero rejected_attempt: nothing Gold, therefore no DPO rows and no pattern candidates. That is structural rather than unlucky - the retry in fill_function is triggered by assess_rust, which is a tree-sitter syntax check, so a candidate that parses but is semantically wrong is accepted as Silver and there is no repair to record. Preference pairs for a hole filler need an oracle that can fail: type-check or test failure, which is what joiner oracle.rs and miter verify already provide. Decide whether Gold should be defined by that stronger oracle, and if so route fills through it before spooling.

task.title: Provider returns intermittent 500 empty response and sawhorse blames max_tokens
task.description: Measured, five calls each, same model and key: a structured joiner-style prompt (system message, file context, fenced code) failed 3 of 5 with HTTP 500 empty response content, while a short plain prompt failed 0 of 5. So the failure is intermittent and prompt-shape related, not a token budget problem - but sawhorse appends a diagnostic that asserts reasoning models exhausted max_tokens, which is a guess presented as a cause. That guess cost two wrong fixes before it was tested: GB-206 raised the budget 1024 to 8192, and GB-212 disabled the reasoning trace; neither addressed the flake, though both are defensible on their own terms. Two changes are needed: a bounded retry in the router for an empty-content 500 (transient), and a diagnostic that states what was observed and ranks likely causes instead of naming one. A single-sample bisect of this cost me a wrong conclusion about code fences, which is worth remembering as a measurement discipline point.

receipt.summary: VerifyMode::Crate compiles the candidate via miter verify behind a drop-guard restore, with joiner fill --verify-crate; unit tests cover default mode, crate mode and the apply contract; clippy and fmt green. End-to-end Gold demonstration blocked by GB-214 (provider 500 on 3 of 5 calls for this prompt shape)

task.title: Declare model limits so requests are sized from a known window
task.description: ProviderConfig gains context_window, max_output_tokens and reasoning_effort; ModelLimits::output_budget slides the output budget down as the prompt grows; joiner sizes each fill from them and honours the configured effort. The provider API exposes no limits to discover: /models returns ids only, /models/{id} is 404, and usage reports cost rather than ceiling. Inference timeout raised 60s -> 300s because a medium-effort call with a 32K budget timed out at exactly 60s and reported it as transport failure.
