description:
Provider returns a 500 "empty response content" for some prompts, and sawhorse used to blame max_tokens.

REPRODUCED (deterministic). `SAWHORSE_DUMP_REQUEST=/tmp/gbdump joiner fill /tmp/gb-gold-crate/src/lib.rs --symbol grapheme_count --max-tokens 4096` captures a 753-byte body that fails 5/5 on replay via curl. That capture is now the fixture for all further bisection.

REFUTED, each by measurement on the same model (cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017):
- max_tokens exhaustion: 4096 and 32768 fail identically; the prompt is ~260 tokens against a 1M window.
- reasoning trace eating the budget: reasoning_effort=none with max_tokens=4096 still fails.
- the triple reasoning encoding (reasoning{effort} + reasoning_effort + thinking{type:enabled}): dropping each key individually still fails.
- temperature float32 artifact (0.20000000298023224): fails identically at 0.2.
- structured output: json_object and json_schema answer 200.
- all six reasoning effort values: 200 with a plain prompt.
- fenced-only response being eaten by an artifact extractor: asking for a pure fence answers 200 twice.
- prompt length: every individual piece of the failing user message answers 200 (intent / fenced current code / diagnostics / fence request).

CONFIRMED: only the COMBINATION of those pieces fails. Same model, same system message, pieces alone 200, together 500. Splitting into separate user turns still fails.

NEXT: bisect the response side. "empty response content" is a content-extraction error, and stream:true takes a different code path through the gateway, so replay the captured body with streaming before touching prompt wording. Then binary-search which two pieces interact.

Cost of the previous misdiagnosis: GB-206/GB-212 raised the budget twice and disabled reasoning on the strength of a message that asserted a cause it had not measured. The diagnostic now reports the observation and ranks causes (GB-215).
acceptance_criteria: A captured body from /tmp/gbdump reproduces the 500 and the same body passes after the fix
The trigger is named as a specific pair of prompt elements, or the streaming path is proven to bypass it

task.title: Wire the local spool into rabbet so a Gold trace can be mined without a server
task.description: A Gold trace now lands in .gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl (verified: tier gold, filled_holes, verification.typecheck_passed, rejected_attempt with real code). Nothing downstream can read it locally: `rabbet admin stats` opens ./rabbet.db, which does not exist, and no rabbet subcommand references the spool or outbox at all - ingestion is only reachable through `rabbet serve`. So `mine-patterns` and `export-parquet` cannot be run from the CLI against the spool, and the DPO shard stays empty even though a Gold pair exists. Needs a `rabbet ingest --spool <path>` (or an admin equivalent) that reads SpoolEntry envelopes and writes master SQLite, plus a documented db-path default that matches where serve writes.

description:
RESOLVED. The gateway non-streaming response assembly returns 500 "empty response content" for request bodies that stream correctly.

PROOF: the captured body /tmp/gbdump/universal-1793363254390.json returns 500 with `stream: false` and 200 with streamed content for `stream: true` - same bytes, same model, back to back.

FIX: sawhorse complete() retries a 500 whose body says `empty response content` once through the streaming path and re-assembles the text (7ffb3dc). Verified end to end: joiner fill --verify-crate now logs "recovered empty non-streamed content by streaming", returns tier gold with attempts 2, and writes the first Gold record to .gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl (outbox 26, gold 1, typecheck_passed true, rejected_attempt carrying real code).

SIX HYPOTHESES WERE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT FIRST, and each had cost real work before this: max_tokens 4096 vs 32768 fail identically; reasoning_effort none/low/medium/high/max all answer 200 on a plain prompt; dropping each of the three reasoning keys (reasoning{effort}, reasoning_effort, thinking{type:enabled}) still fails; thinking enabled or absent makes no difference; the temperature float32 artifact (0.20000000298023224) is irrelevant; structured output answers 200. Every individual piece of the failing user message answers 200 and only the combination fails - which is consistent with response-side assembly, not request content.

INSTRUMENT ADDED FOR THIS: SAWHORSE_DUMP_REQUEST=<file|dir> captures outbound bodies (9e26139), which is what made the reproduction possible after six failed guesses from the outside.
acceptance_criteria: A captured body reproduces the 500 and the same body passes after the fix
The trigger is named and the fix is verified on a live Gold fill
joiner fill --verify-crate returns tier gold end to end

receipt.summary: Root cause: the gateway non-streaming path returns 500 empty response content for bodies that stream fine - the captured body gives 500 with stream:false and 200 with stream:true. Fixed in sawhorse complete() by retrying such a 500 once through the streaming path (7ffb3dc). Verified end to end: joiner fill --verify-crate reports tier gold, attempts 2, and writes the first Gold record to the spool (outbox 26, gold 1, typecheck_passed true). Six alternative hypotheses were refuted by measurement before this (max_tokens 4096 vs 32768, all reasoning efforts, each reasoning key dropped, thinking on/off, temperature artifact, structured output), and SAWHORSE_DUMP_REQUEST was added so bodies can be reproduced instead of guessed at.

task.title: Discover model limits and the ClinePass set from models.dev and the recommended feed
task.description:
Limits are currently declared by hand (GB-215) because the OpenAI-compatible surface exposes none: /models returns bare ids, /models/{id} is 404, and `usage` reports cost not ceiling.

But the catalog is discoverable elsewhere, confirmed by measurement:
- https://models.dev/api.json answers 200 in ~1.1s, 5.9MB, 233 providers, and carries limit.context / limit.input / limit.output plus reasoning_options per model. It includes a `cline-pass` provider with 18 entries (kimi-k3, glm-5.3, deepseek-v4.1-flash, qwen3.8-max, minimax-m3, ...).
- https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/ai/cline/recommended-models answers 200 with 3.4KB of {recommended, free, clinePass, clineCloud}; clinePass has 15 ids including the exact wire id we use, cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, which is NOT in /models and is why `sawhorse models` reports configured_is_advertised: false.

So `sawhorse models` should cross-reference the recommended feed instead of /models alone, and a refresh path should populate context_window / max_output_tokens / reasoning_effort from models.dev, applying Clines own normalisation (max_input = min(limit.context, limit.input) else input or context or 128_000; max_tokens = limit.output or 4096; clamp effort to the advertised reasoning_options). Rust crates that already parse the models.dev schema exist (ai-model-directory-router, models-dev-rs) - evaluate before hand-rolling a parser.

Measured values to reconcile against the current config: cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash is 1M context / 384k output / efforts [none, low, high, max], so the declared 32k output is a deliberate cap rather than the model limit, and `medium` is not an advertised effort (the gateway clamps rather than rejects - verified, all six values answer 200).

task.title: Publish an independent models-catalog crate (models.dev + curated Cline feed)
task.description:
EXTERNAL DELIVERABLE, owned outside the meta-harness. A published crate that parses https://models.dev/api.json and the curated Cline feed, so the suite stops hand-declaring limits and stops scraping docs for the ClinePass set. Consumed later by GB-217.

Confirmed inputs (measured): models.dev/api.json answers 200 in ~1.1s, 5.9MB, 233 providers, carries limit.context/limit.input/limit.output plus reasoning_options, and includes a cline-pass provider with 18 entries. The curated feed https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/ai/cline/recommended-models answers 200 with {recommended, free, clinePass, clineCloud} and 15 clinePass ids including the exact wire id in use.

INTEGRATION CONSTRAINTS, each with the reason it matters:
1. Core is offline: pure parse/lookup with no runtime and no I/O; fetching behind a feature. The suite Tier 2/3 gates must never touch the network.
2. The curated feed is undocumented and advisory, never a hard dependency: last-known snapshot wins, absence degrades to no answer. Entitlement drives a label, never a spend gate.
3. Cache directory and single-flight coalescing are injected, not ambient: no hardcoded cache path, no process-wide singleton, so tests stay deterministic and nothing collides with the canonical .gaugeblock directory.
4. Bundle a trimmed snapshot (id -> limits/efforts/modalities), not the raw 5.9MB payload, so offline and CI users get stable data.
5. Return facts, not policy: normalisation and lookup live in the crate; the choice of budget and effort stays in sawhorse where the contracts and tests are. Successor rule for the suite is config override > catalog > default.
6. Do not model provider config (base URLs, auth env names, fallbacks); ProviderConfig owns those and duplication drifts. Expose limits, modalities, effort options, curated membership.
7. Suite-compatible hygiene: edition 2024, thiserror, no unwrap in library paths, files under 250 lines.

The parity harness belongs here as a scheduled job comparing upstream schema keys, failing only when keys disappear rather than when models are added.

title: Adopt the external models-catalog crate in sawhorse (blocked on GB-218)
description:
BLOCKED ON GB-218 (external crate). Do not hand-roll a models.dev parser in the meantime: that work is being built once, outside the meta-harness, and duplicating it here would create two drifting schemas.

DECISION: adopt a published crate rather than implement discovery in-tree. Placement is OUTSIDE the meta-harness so catalog churn does not tax suite releases and so the 10-repository canon, outfeed install --all and the sibling [patch.crates-io] mapping stay untouched.

WHY IT PAYS: three fragile pieces disappear. cline_pass.rs is a hardcoded const of 15 ids whose own doc admits the set moves, scripts/refresh-cline-pass.sh scrapes a docs page markdown to refresh it, and models.rs parses only GET /models (bare ids) - which is why sawhorse models reported configured_is_advertised false for cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, a model that is in fact pass-eligible.

INTEGRATION SHAPE when GB-218 lands:
1. Feature-gated catalog backend in sawhorse-core; ModelLimits resolves as CONFIG OVERRIDE > catalog > default. The declared context_window / max_output_tokens / reasoning_effort stay as the outage path and are not removed - that is what GB-215 bought.
2. Delete CLINE_PASS_MODELS and scripts/refresh-cline-pass.sh; is_pass_model delegates to the crate curated lookup.
3. sawhorse models reports real context_window, max_output_tokens and effort options, and fixes the advertised/pass-eligible false negative by consulting the curated feed as well as /models.
4. Tests pin a small fixture with no network; one ignored live parity test.
5. benchwork model panel can reuse the same crate afterwards, which argues for the neutral models-catalog name with Cline specifics as the opt-in part.

MEASURED NUMBERS TO RECONCILE: cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash is 1M context / 384k output / efforts [none, low, high, max]. The declared 32k output is a deliberate cap, not the model limit, and medium is not an advertised effort - the gateway clamps rather than rejects, verified across all six values.

task.title: Wire miter deps --layers --check into the Tier 3 outfeed gate
task.description:
GB-202 built the lateral-edge gate and it works (exit 0 clean, exit 1 naming the edge when an allowlist entry is removed), but nothing calls it yet, so a new cross-product edge can still land silently.

GB-200 phase 1b left this as an open decision with a recommendation: wire it into `outfeed gate` (Tier 3) rather than per-repo CI, because the layer map spans 42 crates across 11 repositories and no single repository can evaluate it. Only outfeed sees the whole suite, and per-repo CI would need the sibling checkouts.

The wiring is deliberately not done in GB-202: it lives in outfeed-cli, outside that ticket scope. Measured baseline to assert against: 84 downward, 23 lateral (all allowlisted under GB-204), 0 upward.

receipt.summary: miter deps now classifies every crate edge into foundation / domain / integrator and gates the lateral ones. Layers derive from package names (gaugeblock-* foundation, bare name facade/integrator, -cli/-mcp integrator, else domain), so no per-repo config exists to drift. --check exits 0 on a clean graph and 1 naming the offending edge; proven by removing one allowlist entry. Same-layer edges get a family dimension so a product own internals (miter-engine -> miter-ast, 71 sites) and facade -> own -mcp are exempt rather than debt; upward edges are never excusable. Measured 2026-10-30: 42 crates, 107 edges, 84 downward, 23 lateral all seeded into .gaugeblock/miter/layers-allowlist.toml with GB-204, 0 upward. The audit prior figure of 6 lateral edges was a narrower count; 23 is the honest number after the GB-199 scanner fix, recorded not reconciled. 189 tests pass, clippy and fmt green.

title: Adopt models-catalog 0.1.0 in sawhorse: catalog-backed limits, streaming flag, wire reasoning
description:
UNBLOCKED: models-catalog 0.1.0 is published (GB-218). Full plan in .gaugeblock/storypole/plans/GB-217.md; summary of scope below.

DEPENDENCY LINE, deliberately narrow: models-catalog = { version = "0.1.0", default-features = false, features = ["cline", "bundled"] }. The default feature set pulls reqwest 0.13 + tokio + directories, and sawhorse is on reqwest 0.12 - enabling defaults would compile a second HTTP stack for something sawhorse already has, plus an ambient ~/.cache path and a ~/.cline settings reader. With defaults off the crate is a pure synchronous parser/lookup table, which is what a hermetic gate needs. Freshness comes from running the crate CLI out of band, not from sawhorse doing HTTP.

FIVE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, in order:
1. Feature-gated CatalogSource (Bundled + Null impls) so existing tests stay hermetic; precedence config override > catalog > default via ModelOverrides.
2. Replace my hand-rolled output_budget (window - prompt - 64, no cap) with resolve_gateway_max_output_tokens (32k cap, 1024 reserve, reasoning floor).
3. requires_streaming: send stream:true on the FIRST call for a flagged model instead of discovering the 500 and retrying - GB-214 retry stays as the net for unflagged models. This directly retires a wasted round-trip we measured.
4. Reasoning effort via to_wire_reasoning_params instead of the three hand-encoded keys (reasoning, reasoning_effort, thinking) captured in the GB-214 dump - payload goes from 3 encodings to 1.
5. sawhorse models reports real limits and billing tier from catalog membership, fixing the configured_is_advertised false negative that came from cross-checking GET /models only.

THEN RETIRE DATA: delete CLINE_PASS_MODELS and scripts/refresh-cline-pass.sh, delegate is_pass_model to the catalog.

GAP EXPOSED: gaugeblock-contracts ReasoningEffort lacks XHigh and Max, so xhigh cannot be requested until the contract grows - filed as GB-221 because it is a wire-contract change with its own miter contracts gate.
acceptance_criteria: sawhorse-core builds with and without the catalog feature; existing tests unchanged
Output budget delegates to resolve_gateway_max_output_tokens, with tests for known and unknown models
A model flagged requires_streaming makes zero non-streamed calls
A fill payload emits exactly one reasoning encoding

task.title: Evaluate a suite-wide reqwest 0.12 -> 0.13 alignment, measured
task.description:
Raised while adopting models-catalog (GB-217), whose default features pull reqwest 0.13 while sawhorse is on 0.12. DECISION: do NOT bump for that reason - GB-217 pins default-features = false, which removes the duplicate HTTP stack and keeps the library hermetic (no tokio, no directories, no ambient cache) in one move. Recorded here because the bump will be wanted eventually and it is a migration, not a version-number edit.

MEASURED FACTS:
- reqwest 0.13.5 is current and mainstream (22.5M downloads on that exact version); 0.12.28 is the newest 0.12. So 0.13 is not experimental.
- The feature surface changed: 0.12 has rustls-tls, rustls-tls-webpki-roots, rustls-tls-native-roots and no-provider variants plus __rustls-ring; 0.13 has rustls, rustls-no-provider and __rustls-aws-lc-rs. Every `features = ["rustls-tls"]` in the suite must become `rustls`, and the TLS provider choice (ring vs aws-lc-rs) changes build time and platform story.
- crates using reqwest today: sawhorse-core, outfeed-core (index_poll), and models-catalog if its client feature is ever enabled.

WHEN TO DO IT: a security advisory touching 0.12, a required dependency that only supports 0.13 and cannot be feature-gated, or a dedicated dependency-alignment block. None holds today.

SCOPE: one commit per repository with the full Tier 2 gate, plus a before/after on build time and binary size (law 12) since the TLS provider swap moves both.

receipt.summary: ReasoningEffort now carries XHigh and Max, completing the closed six-tier set that models-catalog defines (None/Low/Medium/High/XHigh/Max, ranks 0-5). Confirmed from the crate source that the set is closed: upstream reasoning_options folds onto those ranks (minimal->Low, med->Medium, xhigh->XHigh, maximum->Max) and unknown tokens are dropped, so an open Other(String) variant would only move the mismatch. XHigh carries an explicit serde rename to the canonical wire string xhigh, with a test proving the snake_case spelling x_high does not silently parse; all six round-trip and unknown tokens are rejected. CONTRACTS.md mirrors the enum and sawhorse payload emits the two new tiers verbatim. Gates: gaugeblock-contracts 31 tests, sawhorse-core 21 tests, clippy and fmt green in both.

Some drift may be expected where a language legitimately lacks a field, in which case it needs the same allowlist treatment GB-202 gave lateral edges - an entry with a ticket, not silence. (2) 35 entities verified versus 32 drift lines suggests the comparison is per-field across 3 languages and will need a stated policy rather than an implicit one.

title: rabbet ingest --spool: reach the local spool from the CLI
description:
IN PROGRESS. Two Gold pairs now exist in .gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl (33 records, 2 gold) and nothing could read them locally: serve was the only ingress, admin stats opened a ./rabbet.db that does not exist, and no subcommand mentioned the spool.

DESIGN, transport rather than a second gate: `rabbet ingest --spool <file> --db-path <db>` reads JSON lines, deserialises SpoolEntry envelopes, and hands them to `rabbet_core::gate::process_ingest_batch` - the same four stages the HTTP endpoint runs (SHA-256 verification, PII re-scrub, structural validation, idempotent insert). A local shortcut that skipped them would let a trace into the corpus that the public path would reject.

Choices worth recording: a malformed line is counted and skipped rather than aborting the import, because one bad record must not block a corpus, but it must not vanish silently either; client_version is stamped from CARGO_PKG_VERSION so rows record which binary ingested them; db-path defaults to rabbet.db with the same RABBET_DB_PATH env override serve uses, which is the documented-answer half of the original ticket.

Verified so far: clippy -D warnings green on rabbet-cli. Test run in progress (rabbet-core pulls the full arrow/parquet stack).

task.title: The Gold chosen body is stored as the placeholder <filled> instead of the code
task.description:
Measured while proving the DPO shard end to end after GB-216. `hole_filler_dpo.parquet` now has 2 real rows with prompt/chosen/rejected columns, the scope signature (/tmp/gb-gold-crate/src/lib.rs::grapheme_count) and a genuinely rejected attempt containing `use unicode_segmentation::UnicodeSegmentation;`. The `chosen` column, though, reads `grapheme_count: <filled>` - the literal placeholder rather than the accepted code.

Same shape shows up upstream: the spool record filled_holes map has keys `grapheme_count` and `<filled>`, so the filled body never got attached to the hole it fills. Regex `mine-patterns` is affected too: with 2 examples it proposes a template `<filled>` with an empty typed-hole list, which is a degenerate pattern rather than a discovered one.

This is the difference between a shard that exists and a shard that trains: a DPO pair whose chosen side is a placeholder is unusable. Fix belongs where the trace is assembled (joiner fill - the hole name and the body are both known there) and should assert that filled_holes contains at least one non-placeholder body before spooling.

receipt.summary: rabbet ingest --spool <file> --db-path <db> closes the gap: local spool envelopes now reach the master store without a server, through the same four-stage gate as the HTTP path (hash verification, PII re-scrub, structural validation, idempotent insert). Verified live against the real spool: 33 records, 0 malformed, 33 accepted, 0 rejected, 0 duplicates. Downstream that was previously unreachable now runs: mine-patterns discovers 1 candidate with 2 examples, and export-parquet writes hole_filler_sft.parquet 16 rows, hole_filler_dpo.parquet 2 rows, router_sft.parquet 0 rows plus a dataset card. The DPO rows carry prompt/chosen/rejected with the scope signature and a real rejected attempt; the chosen side is still the <filled> placeholder, filed separately. Gate: clippy -D warnings and 13 tests green.

task.title: rabbet admin stats ignores --db-path and RABBET_DB_PATH
task.description: Found while verifying GB-216: with the corpus at /tmp/gb216.db holding 33 accepted traces, `RABBET_DB_PATH=/tmp/gb216.db rabbet admin stats` reported "Database: rabbet.db" and 0 traces, and `--db-path` is not accepted at all (error: unexpected argument). The ingest, mine-patterns and export-parquet subcommands all take --db-path, so the one command a maintainer reaches for first to confirm an import is the one that looks at a different database. Either give admin stats the same --db-path/RABBET_DB_PATH handling as the others, or print the resolved path prominently so the mismatch is obvious.

receipt.summary: The Gold/Silver trace now carries the accepted body instead of the literal <filled>: the CLI was building filled_holes as (symbol, "<filled>") while FillOutcome::code - the validated candidate - sat unused beside it. Verified live: the spool record for the newest fill holds the full function body including its doc comment and the crate::text::grapheme_count delegation, and the exported sft shard contains that text rather than a placeholder. record_trace now refuses to spool a hole whose body is empty or the placeholder, naming the hole, because a corpus that silently accepts untrainable pairs only fails when someone trains on it. Found while proving this: verification was writing the bare candidate as the whole file, erasing every mod declaration, so a correct candidate delegating to crate::text failed with "cannot find text in the crate root"; it now splices exactly as --apply does. task.title: The ingest gate accepts a trace whose hole body is a placeholder
task.description: RESOLVED in the same session as commit 3b42a20. Joiner stopped sending placeholders under GB-225, but the receiving side needs the counterpart guard since any producer can hand the corpus an untrainable pair, and a dataset that admits one trains on it. That was a recorded decision, not a tool: the next occurrence needs a repeatable, reviewed operation rather than an ad hoc python command, because editing an append-only telemetry log is exactly the kind of thing that should be a subcommand with a dry-run.

Scope: `joiner spool quarantine --dir <suite> [--dry-run]`, moving records whose filled_holes carry an empty body or the <filled> placeholder into .gaugeblock/spool/quarantine/<reason>-<date>.jsonl, printing count and hash, never deleting. Idempotent. Note the spool is gitignored, so the tool should also write a one-line summary somewhere tracked (ledger via storypole, or a sibling .md) or the event leaves no versioned trace.

task.title: A trivial hole cannot produce a Gold pair, so the corpus cannot grow by repetition alone
task.description:
Measured in the cross-fixture yield study (.gaugeblock/storypole/plans/GB-213.md): 9 fills across 3 fixtures gave 3 Gold and 6 Silver, and the split is per-hole rather than per-pipeline. sum_positive is a one-line delegation that compiles first try, so it produced 0/3 Gold; parse_port needs range and error handling the first attempt plausibly gets wrong, so it produced 2/3. grapheme_count sat at 1/3.

CONSEQUENCE: running more fills over trivial holes yields more Silver and no DPO pairs. Growing the Gold corpus needs holes with genuine failure modes - wrong return types, error mapping, borrow lifetimes, trait bounds - not more fixtures of the same difficulty.

NEXT: build a fixture set graded by difficulty (a trivial delegation, an error-mapping case, a lifetime/borrow case, a trait-bound case) and measure Gold rate per grade. That would turn the 33% headline into a per-difficulty curve, which is what would tell us whether the corpus can be grown on purpose or only harvested opportunistically. Related: GB-213 (compiler oracle), GB-225 (body carrying), GB-228 (spool quarantine).

description:
PARKED by owner decision 2026-10-30. Deliberately not pursued now: the pipeline defects that produced no Gold are all cleared (GB-224, GB-225, GB-227), and the owner is comfortable with Gold accruing organically rather than by manufacturing difficulty.

OWNER THESIS, worth preserving because it changes the ticket premise: Gold is inherently rarer here because the oracle and the universal provider are the same model right now - the verifier cannot be harder than the generator. The intended sources of Gold are instead (a) backfill and OSS mining over real messy git history - commits named fix, fix again, another try carry a genuine failed state and a genuine repair, which is exactly a DPO pair, and (b) community contributions once the public rabbet datastore exists and developers report their own traces.

So the grading idea below is not rejected, only deprioritised. Re-open if the corpus needs to be grown faster than real history supplies.

task.title: Mine Gold pairs from real git history: pre-fix and post-fix revisions of the same hunk
task.description:
The owners intended source of Gold (stated 2026-10-30): backfill and OSS mining over messy history - commits named fix, fix again, another try carry a genuine failed state and a genuine repair, which is exactly a DPO pair and is more honest than any fixture I could invent.

MEASURED GAP: rabbet has no git-history access at all. `rabbet mine-oss --path <dir>` walks a directory (cold_miner.rs mentions .git only to skip it); there is no rev-range, no git log, no commits_between anywhere in rabbet-core. So the source does not exist yet.

DEPENDENCY, and it reframes an existing ticket: the backfill miner needs exactly the history API planned for GB-131 step 3 - commits_between, merge_base, describe_range, all typed and tested against a real repository. That makes GB-131 steps 2-3 a prerequisite for the Gold corpus rather than pure refactor debt.

SCOPE: for a rev range, find hunks that changed and whose commit message matches the repair vocabulary (fix, retry, try again, another attempt, correct); emit (pre-image, post-image) as a Gold candidate with the commit sha as provenance; verify the post-image compiles before it enters the corpus, because a historical commit is not a guarantee. Keep the commit message out of the training pair - it is metadata, not supervision.

task.title: Make the verifier stricter than the generator: compile is too easy a bar
task.description:
The owner observed that Gold is rare partly because the oracle and the universal provider are the same model - the verifier cannot be harder than the generator. There is a cheaper lever than harder fixtures: raise the verifiers bar.

Today assess_rust + miter verify accept anything that compiles. A candidate that compiles but ignores the documented delegation, leaves an unused import, or returns a wrong-but-well-typed value passes as Silver, and no repair happens. Measured consequence: sum_positive produced 0/3 Gold because its one-line delegation compiles first try.

PROPOSAL: grade the oracle in tiers and let a caller pick - (1) compiles, (2) compiles + clippy -D warnings (unused imports and dead code become failures), (3) compiles + the crates tests pass, (4) compiles + a property or doc-test assertion when the fixture provides one. Tier 2 alone would have rejected the unicode_segmentation candidate on the unused-import rule and forced the repair that the doc comment was asking for. This manufactures Gold honestly - by demanding more, not by inventing difficulty - and it is measurable: same fixtures, compare tier-1 vs tier-2 Gold rate.

task.title: miter deps calls a dependency unused when it is only referenced by a fully-qualified path
task.description:
Found the hard way during GB-201: batten-core declares `regex` and uses it as `regex::escape(id)` in src/grammar/regex.rs with no `use regex;` statement. The scanner reports the dependency as unused, and I acted on that report by demoting it to [dev-dependencies] - which failed to compile. The gate caught it, regex was restored, and the incidence is recorded in the batten commit.

Root cause: `collect_crate_imports` collects imports (use statements and `crate::`/`mod` paths), not qualified references. A dependency reached only through `extern_crate::item` therefore looks dead. That is the same class of over-reporting as GB-199 (fixture strings counted as references) but in the opposite direction, and it produces a false positive that a careful operator will act on destructively.

SCOPE: while stripping literals and comments, also recognise `ident::` paths in expression position as a reference, so `regex::escape` counts. Then re-measure GB-201 - the current 34 unused includes at least this one false positive, and the real number is lower.

description:
IN PROGRESS. Down from 62 to 34 measured unused declarations across 9 removed crates (joiner, outfeed, batten, dado) - 28 gone, zero violations, every repo gated individually.

METHOD that survived contact: word-boundary `grep -rnw` over src/, tests/ and build.rs per crate, because the first pass used a plain grep and matched `serde_json` against "serde". Three classes emerged, each needing a different action: truly unreferenced -> delete; referenced only from tests -> demote to [dev-dependencies] (deleting compiles and breaks the suite); optional feature deps -> keep with a written reason.

CAVEATS to carry forward, both measured:
1. Demotion also reduces the count, so 34 is not 34 deletions. dado-core tracing and uuid moved to dev-dependencies; they no longer ship, which is the actual goal, but the headline number flatters the work.
2. At least one entry is a FALSE POSITIVE: batten-core regex is used as `regex::escape(id)` with no use statement, and the scanner counts imports rather than qualified references. Filed separately. The true remaining count is lower than 34.

REMAINING, grouped: benchwork (cli thiserror+tower, core async-trait+futures+tracing, mcp serde+thiserror), chalkline (cli serde+tracing+uuid, core tokio+tracing from string-literal matches, mcp serde+uuid), rabbet (cli dado-core+miter-engine+serde+thiserror+tower, core async-trait+dado-core+parquet+tokio), sawhorse (cli serde), storypole (cli serde+tracing, mcp serde), miter-engine hcl and outfeed-core reqwest need a manual look, and sawhorse-core candle-core/nn/transformers are optional feature deps to keep.

GATES: batten 14 tests + clippy --workspace -D warnings green; dado 14 tests + clippy green. One self-inflicted error along the way - demoting regex - caught by the gate before commit.

receipt.summary: A local module no longer hides a dependency of the same name. collect_crate_imports filtered any root ident that matched a module name declared in the crate, so batten-core mod regex; hid the regex crate and regex::escape(id) was discarded - I acted on that report by demoting the dependency, which failed to compile. The rule is now name plus context: hide only when the ident is not a declared dependency, since a local module named like a dependency is rare and the alternative failure mode is a destructive purge recommendation. Re-measured: unused declarations 34 -> 30, and the four that disappeared were all this same collision - batten-core/regex, miter-engine/hcl, rabbet-core/parquet and outfeed-core/semver. parquet had been flagged for manual review precisely because deleting it looked wrong; it was a false positive. Diagnosis recorded: three hypotheses (path scan, stripper, walk) were each refuted by a test, and only an instrumented run of the collector showed the missing key. Gate: clippy -D warnings, 181 tests, fmt green.

description:

GB-232 MATTERED MORE THAN THE PURGE: fixing the module-name collision removed FOUR false positives at once - batten-core/regex, miter-engine/hcl, rabbet-core/parquet, outfeed-core/semver - so the earlier 34 contained four items that would have been destructive to remove. parquet had been marked "needs eyes" on instinct; the instinct was right and the reason is now known. task.title: miter deps still misses a dependency referenced only by a qualified path in some files
task.description:
GB-232 fixed the module-name collision, which removed four false positives. One case survives and is measured: outfeed-core declares reqwest and uses it only as `reqwest::blocking::get(&url)` and `reqwest::StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` in src/index_poll.rs, with no `use reqwest` anywhere - and `miter deps --path . --unused` still lists outfeed-core/reqwest.

This is the last item in GB-201 and the only one that would be destructive to act on: parquet was the same shape and turned out to be masked by a module name, but reqwest has no same-named module in outfeed-core, so the qualified-path branch is not firing for this file. Worth noting the diagnostic risk: a grep loop I wrote to verify candidates reported 0 hits for reqwest while a direct grep found two lines, so the harness needs a counted result (wc -l) rather than an exit code before any future purge trusts it.

NEXT: reproduce with src/index_poll.rs as the fixture - if import_roots_in_source finds reqwest there, the loss is in the walk or the filter; if it does not, the stripper is eating the file (the same suspicion that was wrong for batten-core but may be right here, since index_poll.rs also has cfg-gated code).

description:
MEASURED RESULT: 62 -> 4 declared-but-unreferenced declarations, and the remaining four are accounted for rather than pending.

task.title: Shared target-dir plus sccache stall on the build lock under concurrent repos and long-lived MCP servers

description: Measured on macOS 12.7.6 (x86_64), cargo/rustc 1.99.1, sccache 0.18.0, during the GB-130/GB-234 session. Symptom: a gate command prints "Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory" and never advances, or reaches a crate name and stops at 0% CPU; the wrapping shell then hits its own timeout and kills the process group, leaving the lock held by an orphan. Observed four times in one session. Two distinct causes were separated: (1) lock contention, where a killed-but-alive cargo from an earlier timed-out command held target/debug/.cargo-lock with cwd in a member repo - confirmed with lsof on the lock file; (2) an sccache deadlock, where two rustc invocations for ring v0.17.14 sat at 0% CPU, one of them orphaned from an already-finished build - killing the orphan released both.

acceptance_criteria: Root CONTRIBUTING.md documents the contention and the remedies, because .cargo/config.toml is the cause
Decide whether build.target-dir stays shared across 11 repositories: it saves disk and cold-build time but serialises them, and any long-lived miter MCP daemon that invokes cargo contends too
Make the stall self-diagnosable - Blocking waiting for file lock gives no hint which repository or daemon holds it

completed_items: The durable half is done: CONTRIBUTING.md now records the contention, both measured causes (lock holder identified with lsof on target/debug/.cargo-lock; sccache deadlock identified as two rustc ring processes at 0% CPU with one orphaned), the reliable remedy (kill the lock holder, not the wrapper), and the escape hatch (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/... RUSTC_WRAPPER= for the affected crate, costing one cold dependency compile).
remaining_items: Two acceptance criteria are open and both are decisions rather than edits: (1) whether build.target-dir should stay shared across 11 repositories now that they plus the miter MCP daemons all serialise on one lock; (2) making the stall self-diagnosable, since Blocking waiting for file lock names neither the repository nor the daemon holding it.
handoff.last_error_or_blocker: None. Note for whoever picks it up: the symptom is indistinguishable from a slow build, which is why it cost a session - a 0% CPU sample is the signal, not elapsed time.

title: storypole update stored a comma-separated list argument as one bogus value
description:
The filed symptom did not reproduce: `--file <one path>` stores that path correctly, and the handler has been correct since it was introduced (73e38dd - the only commit that ever touched it).

What does reproduce is the shape most people type: `--file a.rs,b.rs`, which stored the single string "a.rs,b.rs" and reported success. The scope then held one path that exists nowhere, which is indistinguishable from the update being ignored and is a plausible origin for the report.

Fixed by giving all four list arguments `value_delimiter = 0x2C` - file, symbol, label, criterion - since the defect is in list parsing rather than in one field. Repeating the flag still works.

task.title: benchwork DAG view renders stale statuses: it reads the workspace store exclusively and never falls back to the single store

description:
Symptom reported from the UI: benchwork shows tasks in Ready that are complete - GB-57 and GB-53 among them.

Measured: those two are VERIFIED in the ledger. Each has a task_verified event with a receipt (GB-57 verifier antigravity, GB-53 verifier outfeed, command `outfeed apply`), keyed by task UUID. `storypole show` agrees, so the data is right and only the view is wrong.

Cause is in the read path, not the data. `get_dag_view` opens a StorypoleWorkspaceStore first and, if that succeeds, reads `get_all_tasks(ws.conn())` and RETURNS - the single store is never consulted. So the DAG board renders whatever the workspace index holds, and a workspace index that has not been re-synced since those tasks were verified still says ready. `query.rs` has the same shape again around lines 128 and 143.

This overlaps GB-79 (WorkspaceStore sync_all_members replay ordering and distributed event sync), which is where the staleness itself belongs; this ticket is the read-path half - prefer or merge the single store rather than treating a successful workspace open as authoritative.

A note for whoever measures next: the first pass on this looked like ledger corruption because a search for the ticket key found only task_created. Verification events key on the task UUID, not the ticket key, so a key-based search cannot see them. Check that a search can observe the thing before concluding it is absent.

description:
HONESTY NOTE on the mechanism (2026-10-31), because an earlier description overstated it: "the workspace index had not re-synced" is a hypothesis consistent with the code shape, not an established fact.

`StorypoleWorkspaceStore::open` builds its aggregate from `StorypoleStore::open_exact` on the root and on each member that has a dot dir, and it is opened per call in this path. So a per-call staleness story needs either the member indexes to lag, or the daemon to cache the store in its state. Which is true has NOT been measured.

The observable check is cheap: reinstall the daemon, restart it, and see whether GB-57 and GB-53 move to Verified. If they do not, the workspace path was not the cause and the next suspect is the daemon holding its own store in ctx.state. The fix still stands on its own terms - a cache should not outvote its source - but it is not yet proven to be the whole cause.

RESOLVED 2026-10-31 and CONFIRMED IN THE RUNNING UI by the owner: after reinstalling the daemon, GB-57 and GB-53 no longer render as ready. So the read path was the cause; the workspace-store-exclusivity in get_dag_view was the actual defect, and the daemon-cached-store hypothesis is refuted by that observation.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-155 — Cut the Meta-Harness Suite Release

> **Epic Key:** `GB-155`  
> **Scope:** `workspace` + `outfeed`  
> **Status:** Planned — runbook ready, execute after the contracts publish

---

## 1. Objective

Give the meta-harness its own release: a `suite.lock` pinning all eleven repositories, a root changelog
section, and an annotated `suite-v<version>` snapshot tag, behind a certified gate.

Current state (2026-10-28): the root has **no git remote**, **no `suite.lock`**, and one historical tag
`suite-v0.1.0-beta.2`, so the next snapshot derives as **`0.1.0-beta.3`**.

`outfeed release --suite` already implements the mechanics but has never run end to end.

---

## 2. Pre-Release Checklist

1. Every member clean, on `main`, and pushed (`outfeed sync --all --status-only` shows no divergence).
2. Tier 3 matrix green across all eleven repos: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
   `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`,
   `miter contracts`, `outfeed lockfiles`, `chalkline docs check --workspace`
   (expect `12 targets audited, 108 present, 0 missing, 0 drifted`).
3. `gaugeblock-contracts` and `gaugeblock-common` published at `0.1.0-beta.3`-independent version
   `0.1.0-beta.1` **before** any member that depends on them.
4. `suite.lock` generated and committed, pinning all eleven repositories with exact commits.
5. Root `CHANGELOG.md` gains an ecosystem section listing every member version.
6. Annotated tag `suite-v0.1.0-beta.3` on the root.
7. Decision on a root remote: `push_repo` cannot push a repository without one, and the harness
   history is currently single-copy on this machine.
8. Delete `outfeed/PERF_AUDIT_PLAN.md` once the release is out (it is a stray; its content lives in
   the ledger, the tickets, and the commit messages).

---

## 3. Runbook

```bash
# 0. Rebuild the tooling so the installed outfeed has lockfiles/override/waves.
cargo install --path outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli --force

# 1. Publish the foundation first (irreversible; crates.io rate-limits new crates).
outfeed publish common --dry-run      # packages both crates
outfeed publish common                # real upload; expect a 429 cooldown on the 2nd crate

# 2. Confirm the contracts are visible before members reference them.
for c in gaugeblock-contracts gaugeblock-common; do
  curl -s https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c | python3 -c \
    "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['crate']['max_version'])"
done

# 3. Release the members (11 repositories, common first because it is wave 0).
outfeed release --all --no-llm --dry-run   # inspect the plan table first
outfeed release --all --yes --no-llm

# 4. Meta-harness snapshot (writes suite.lock, root changelog, suite-v tag).
outfeed release --suite --suite-version 0.1.0-beta.3 --yes --skip-publish --skip-install

# 5. Push everything, including members that were clean before this pass.
outfeed push --all
```

---

## 4. Gotchas learned the hard way

* **`common` proposes the wrong version.** With no tag baseline the calculator overshoots to
  `0.1.0-beta.2`; use `outfeed release common --override-version 0.1.0-beta.1`. A second pass with the
  same override is a clean no-op (`already released as v0.1.0-beta.1`).
* **`outfeed release --all` must run from the harness root**; from inside a member it sees no members
  and reports "0 repositories".
* **A push failure is invisible on a re-run.** `release --all` self-heals only the registry half
  (`PublishPending`); a repo tagged locally but never pushed reports `Skip (Clean)` next time
  (`GB-153`). Check `git log origin/main..HEAD` per repo before declaring victory.
* **crates.io 429s quote the deadline in the body**, not a `Retry-After` header; `GB-140` handles it,
  but a three-attempt budget cannot outlast a 10-per-hour new-crate limit — space uploads out.
* **Never run two `storypole` mutations in parallel**: appends spliced two JSON events onto one line
  twice today. `GB-147` makes the append atomic, but keep mutations serial until it is trusted.
* **`git add <dir> Cargo.lock` aborts staging entirely in a repo that ignores it**, and
  `git commit -q` then fails silently (`GB-150`). All eleven repos now track a fresh lockfile.

Release all eleven members
Cut the suite snapshot
steps.verification_gate: suite.lock + CHANGELOG + suite-v tag on root

steps.title: Push every member and the harness
steps.verification_gate: git log origin/main..HEAD empty per repo

description:
PROGRESS 2026-10-31. Started at 23 lateral edges / ~176 sites; now 22 / ~175. Edge one burned down rather than excused: `rabbet-core -> miter-engine` existed solely to call `scrub_source_text`, so `miter-security` moved to the suite foundation as `common/crates/gaugeblock-security` (crate created for GB-158, pulled forward here) and rabbet now depends on it - a downward edge, not an exception. `joiner-core` made the same change, taking its `miter-engine` sites from 3 to 2; the remaining two (the `EngineError` conversion and `polyglot::syntax_diagnostics`) are genuine engine uses and stay.

The allowlist entry was deleted by hand in its own commit, per the GB-202 rule that an entry leaves only when its site count reaches zero.

Next candidates by cost: chalkline-core -> sawhorse-core (2 sites), dado-core -> miter-engine (2), outfeed-core -> sawhorse-core (4). The big ones need real design work: benchwork-core -> storypole-core (50), joiner-core -> dado-core (13), joiner-core -> sawhorse-core (13), benchwork-core -> sawhorse-core (13), chalkline-core -> miter-engine (12).

PROGRESS 2026-10-31, three edges burned down (23 -> 20 lateral).

1. `rabbet-core -> miter-engine` (1 site): existed only to call `scrub_source_text`. `miter-security` became `common/crates/gaugeblock-security` (GB-158, pulled forward); rabbet and joiner now depend on it. joiner drops 3 sites to 2 - the EngineError conversion and `polyglot::syntax_diagnostics` are real uses.
2. `chalkline-core -> sawhorse-core` (2 sites): `ModelRole` and `InferenceRequest` had lived in gaugeblock-contracts since the sawhorse contracts were centralised; the import simply predated the move.
3. `dado-core -> chalkline-core` (3 sites): `SharedTypeContract` and `ContractField` are plain serde structs whose own doc comment called them a wire schema. They moved to gaugeblock-contracts, chalkline re-exports them so its API holds, and dado no longer depends on chalkline at all.

Pattern so far, which predicts the rest: an edge is burnable when what crosses is a *type*, and stays when what crosses is *behaviour*. The remaining 20 split accordingly - `batten-core -> dado-core` (PatternRegistry), `joiner-core -> sawhorse-core` (RoleRouter), `dado-core -> miter-engine` (polyglot parse) are behavioural and need control inversion rather than a move. The big ones (benchwork-core -> storypole-core at 50 sites, three 13-site edges) are the same question at a larger scale.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-31 after GB-203 split miter-engine into four crates. The class has grown from the 60 files this was filed against to 85 files in the 200-250 band (miter audit --threshold 200, all under the hard 250 ceiling, so nothing is illegal yet).

Distribution: miter 37, benchwork/web 9, storypole 8, common 8, sawhorse 5, benchwork 5, outfeed 4, joiner 4, plus a tail.

The filing assumption that 31 of the 60 were in miter-engine no longer holds - those files are now spread across miter-polyglot, miter-analysis, miter-inventory and miter-engine, and the count in miter as a whole went up rather than down, because the split moved files without shrinking them. That is the argument for doing this sweep now rather than after more extraction: the band is where the next 250-line breach will come from, and every extraction so far has pushed a file into it.

THE CHEAP VEIN IS NOW EXHAUSTED, measured rather than assumed. A scan of every remaining edge for references outside `error.rs` returned non-zero for all of them (benchwork->storypole 9 files, chalkline->miter-engine 9, benchwork->sawhorse 6, joiner->dado 5, joiner->sawhorse 5, batten->dado 5, and 1 file each for joiner/miter-engine, dado/miter-engine, chalkline/storypole, outfeed/sawhorse, outfeed/storypole, benchwork/miter-engine). What that leaves is design, in two shapes. (a) The benchwork decision below: 7 of the 19 edges are benchwork-core composing every other product. (b) Control inversion for the rest - chalkline writes tasks through `add_task`/`link_tasks`, outfeed queries tasks and records receipts, dado and joiner parse through the miter polyglot. Each needs a trait or CLI boundary rather than a move, and each is its own ticket-sized decision.

task.title: End-to-end flight recorder telemetry (.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl) and live SSE execution waterfall in benchwork
task.description: Enables zero-configuration, cross-process observability across VS Code MCP servers (`*-mcp`), standalone CLI invocations, `outfeed gate` sub-steps, and `sawhorse` LLM calls. All processes append `TelemetrySpan` records via atomic `O_APPEND` to the worktree-safe canonical `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl` resolved by `gaugeblock-workspace`. `benchwork` tails the file via filesystem notifications (`notify`), indexes spans into `.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite`, and streams live execution activity to the global header pulse, Panel 3 (`AST & Synthesis X-Ray`) waterfall, and Panel 4 (`Model Router & Telemetry Spool`) Law 12 timing tables.

scope.crate_name: gaugeblock-contracts, gaugeblock-workspace, gaugeblock-mcp, sawhorse-core, outfeed-core, benchwork-core, benchwork-cli, web

acceptance_criteria: TelemetrySpan round-trips through serde with every optional field omitted when absent, and lives in gaugeblock-contracts
SpanGuard::drop appends exactly one O_APPEND line per span, creates the file when missing, and never changes the caller exit code on a read-only disk (fail-open)
outfeed gate spawns each step with GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID and GAUGEBLOCK_PARENT_SPAN_ID set, and the child spans reparent onto the gate step span
GET /api/v1/telemetry/stream delivers a span appended by a non-benchwork process (MCP or CLI) within 250 ms, proven by test
GET /api/v1/telemetry/law12-stats returns P50/P95 duration rollups by binary and subcommand with the sample count
ExecutionWaterfallView.tsx renders the parent-child tree in Panel 3 and the header LIVE AGGREGATOR pill pulses while an external span is open
Every touched file is at or under 250 LOC and .gaugeblock/telemetry/ is gitignored

decision.question: D1 Transport: how must CLI binaries and *-mcp stdio servers emit telemetry spans?
proposed_options: POSIX O_APPEND file-backed flight recorder at <canonical .gaugeblock>/telemetry/events.jsonl with zero network coupling
Blocking HTTP POST to the benchwork daemon on :4242
Unix domain socket owned by the benchwork daemon

chosen_option: POSIX O_APPEND file-backed flight recorder at <canonical .gaugeblock>/telemetry/events.jsonl with zero network coupling

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-243 — End-to-end flight recorder telemetry and live SSE execution waterfall

> **Key:** `GB-243` · **Kind:** Feature · **Priority:** P1 · **Repo:** `gaugeblock`
> **Scope:** `gaugeblock-contracts`, `gaugeblock-workspace`, `gaugeblock-mcp`, `sawhorse-core`,
> `outfeed-core`, `benchwork-core`, `benchwork-cli`, `web`
> **Depends on:** `GB-189` (`gaugeblock-workspace`, Phase A foundation of `GB-200`) and `GB-130`
> (`gaugeblock-mcp`, verified). The path resolver and the shared JSON-RPC dispatcher are the two
> surfaces this ticket instruments, so it cannot start before both exist.
> **Status:** Planned — blocked on `GB-189`.
> **Companion:** `GB-244` (`rabbet distill-telemetry`) consumes the records produced here. This
> ticket ships the schema and the transport; it does not mine them.

---

## 1. Why this exists — four blind spots, each visible in the tree today

| Blind spot | What the tree shows |
|:--|:--|
| No cross-process record of anything | `outfeed gate` prints one line per step (`GateStepResult { name, passed, skipped, detail }`) and discards the duration it could have measured. A 40 s `clippy` and a 0.4 s `docs` look identical afterwards. |
| `benchwork` sees only itself | `BenchworkState.event_tx: broadcast::Sender<LiveEvent>` carries six variants, all produced *inside the daemon*. An MCP tool call from Cline, or a `cargo clippy` spawned by the gate, is invisible. |
| MCP tool usage is unmeasured | `common/crates/gaugeblock-mcp/src/stdio.rs` (139 LOC) routes every one of the seven servers through `dispatch`/`dispatch_async`. Nothing records which tool ran, for how long, or whether it errored. |
| LLM cost is not attributable | `InferenceResponse` already carries `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `latency_ms`, `model_used` and `reasoning_tokens` — and every consumer drops them at the return statement. |

The result is that law 12 ("a figure that lives only in chat has not been recorded") is currently
unenforceable at the process level: there is nowhere to read a number from.

## 2. Decisions (resolved on the ticket)

| # | Decision | Chosen | Category |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | Transport for span emission | POSIX `O_APPEND` file-backed flight recorder, zero network coupling | `transport` |
| D2 | Where instrumentation lives | Three shared choke points only | `architecture` |
| D3 | Parent-child correlation across processes | `GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID` / `GAUGEBLOCK_PARENT_SPAN_ID` env vars | `correlation` |
| D4 | How `benchwork` ingests and serves | `notify` watcher + byte offset + SQLite (WAL) index + SSE/REST | `ingestion` |


### D1 — POSIX `O_APPEND` file-backed flight recorder, zero network coupling

CLI binaries and `*-mcp` stdio servers MUST NOT make blocking HTTP/IPC calls to `benchwork`
(`:4242`) to emit telemetry. Every process appends single-line `TelemetrySpan` JSON records
directly to `<canonical_gaugeblock>/telemetry/events.jsonl` using
`OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true)` (target `< 100 µs`, fails silently if the disk is
read-only).

*Why not HTTP:* a blocking POST inside the MCP request path adds daemon latency to every tool call
and converts a `benchwork` outage into an MCP outage for Cline and Antigravity. Hiding that latency
on a detached thread adds teardown risk on `SIGKILL` — the process that loses the span is exactly
the one that died, which is the case the recorder exists for.

*Why `O_APPEND` is sufficient:* a single `write` of a line at or below `PIPE_BUF` is atomic under
POSIX and lands at the end of the file without a lock, so N concurrent processes append without
interleaving. It needs no daemon, no discovery, no port, no authentication, and it behaves
identically for a CI run nobody is watching.

`.gaugeblock/telemetry/` is added to the root `.gitignore` alongside `.gaugeblock/spool/` and
`.gaugeblock/datasets/`. Note that the existing `.gaugeblock/**/*.sqlite` rule already covers
`telemetry/index.sqlite`; `events.jsonl` and `snapshots/*.diff` are the two paths that need the new
directory rule.

### D2 — Three choke-point instrumentation strategy

Rather than instrumenting individual domain functions across ten repositories, instrument strictly
at three shared choke points:

1. **`gaugeblock-mcp` JSON-RPC request dispatcher** (`SpanKind::McpTool`). Measured: `stdio.rs`
   holds `dispatch()` and `dispatch_async()`, the single routing pair all seven servers share, so
   one wrap covers every VS Code tool call from Cline and Antigravity.
2. **A CLI top-level `SpanGuard` RAII drop helper in `gaugeblock-workspace`**
   (`SpanKind::CliCommand`), plus `SpanKind::GateStep` inside `outfeed gate`'s step runner, which
   already owns the spawn.
3. **`sawhorse-core` provider completion boundary** (`SpanKind::LlmInference`) —
   `RoleRouter::complete` and `complete_stream`, where `InferenceResponse` is in hand.

A `tracing-subscriber` layer was rejected: it would require all eleven binaries to adopt a
subscriber and a shared registry, and it cannot express "one completed span with a duration and an
exit code" as a single appendable line.

### D3 — 3-tier context and parent-child span correlation

Propagate parent-child causality across subprocess boundaries (`outfeed gate` spawning
`cargo clippy`, `miter` and `chalkline`; `joiner fill` invoking `sawhorse`) via
`GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID` and `GAUGEBLOCK_PARENT_SPAN_ID` environment variables, set on the `Command`
and therefore inherited by every child. Environment is the only channel a stdio MCP server and a
spawned `cargo` process both see; W3C `traceparent` needs an HTTP hop the gate does not have.

Automatically enrich every span with `task_key` and `worktree` inferred from `GAUGEBLOCK_TASK_KEY`
or the active git branch / worktree path (`feat/gb-...`), so a span from a linked worktree
attributes to the right task without the caller passing anything.

### D4 — Live tailer and derived SQLite index in `benchwork`

`benchwork-core` watches `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl` via the `notify` crate (tracking the
byte offset so a restart resumes instead of replaying), indexes spans into
`.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite` (WAL mode) for historical law 12 P50/P95 duration and token
queries, and broadcasts new spans immediately over `GET /api/v1/telemetry/stream` (SSE).

Polling re-reads data that has not changed and still adds up to a second of latency to a pulse the
header is meant to animate. Reading the JSONL per request makes P50/P95 a full scan of a file that
grows for the life of the checkout. The index is derived state: gitignored, deletable, and
rebuildable from the JSONL at any time (`rusqlite 0.40 bundled` already matches `storypole-core`
and `rabbet-core`).

---

## 3. Wire contract — `common/crates/gaugeblock-contracts/src/telemetry/`

> **Path correction (measured, not assumed).** The mission brief names
> `gaugeblock-contracts/src/telemetry.rs` at ≤ 140 LOC. That file already exists at **146 LOC** and
> already owns `TelemetryTier`, `AnonymizedSynthesisTrace`, `SyncStatus`, `SpoolEntry` and
> `SpoolEntry::hash_trace` — the GB-182 spool envelope. Adding the span types inside it would put it
> over 200 and one deserialisation test away from the hard 250 ceiling. **So the module becomes a
> directory**, exactly as `storypole-core/src/telemetry/mod.rs` already does: `telemetry/mod.rs`
> re-exports, `telemetry/spool.rs` carries today's 146 lines unchanged, `telemetry/spans.rs` holds
> the new span wire contract. `pub use telemetry::*;` in `lib.rs` keeps every existing import path
> working, so this is a move, not a breaking change.

```rust
// telemetry/spans.rs — new file, ≤ 140 LOC
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SpanKind {
    CliCommand,
    McpTool,
    GateStep,
    LlmInference,
    AstPass,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SpanStatus {
    Running,
    Ok,
    Error,
    Skipped,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TokenUsageSummary {
    pub model: String,
    pub prompt_tokens: u32,
    pub completion_tokens: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TelemetrySpan {
    pub trace_id: String,
    pub span_id: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub parent_span_id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub session_id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub task_key: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub worktree: Option<String>,
    pub binary: String,
    pub kind: SpanKind,
    pub name: String,
    pub started_at_ms: u64,
    pub duration_ms: u64,
    pub status: SpanStatus,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub token_usage: Option<TokenUsageSummary>,
    /// Scrubbed, compact JSON summary of MCP tool arguments or CLI flags (≤ 512 bytes).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input_summary: Option<String>,
    /// Populated on `SpanKind::GateStep` when `status == Error`: first compiler/clippy/doc diagnostic.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub first_diagnostic: Option<String>,
    /// Populated on `SpanKind::GateStep`: content-addressed hash of `git diff HEAD`
    /// (or a spool snapshot key).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub worktree_diff_hash: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    pub attributes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}
```

Contract invariants:

1. `SpanKind` and `SpanStatus` are `Copy` and `snake_case` on the wire, so a TS discriminant in
   `benchwork/web` is a literal union (`'cli_command' | 'mcp_tool' | ...`) and not a stringly check.
2. Every optional field is `skip_serializing_if`, so a successful span writes ~14 fields. A
   successful `cargo fmt` step must not carry a `first_diagnostic` key at all — `null` and "absent"
   are different things to a dataset builder.
3. **The envelope stays flat and appendable.** No nested span trees: tree shape is reconstructed by
   `parent_span_id` at read time (D4's index, `GB-244`'s miner). A writer must never need to read
   the file back.
4. `started_at_ms` is epoch milliseconds and `duration_ms` is elapsed, not `ended_at`. A reader that
   computes `started_at + duration` gets the end; a clock that jumps backwards cannot make an
   interval negative.
5. `TelemetrySpan` is *not* `PartialEq`: `attributes` ordering is `BTreeMap` so it could be, but
   equality on a struct with a populated token block invites tests that assert on token counts the
   provider never guaranteed. Tests assert field by field.


---

## 5. Choke points in detail

### 5.1 `SpanGuard` — the only writer

```rust
// gaugeblock-workspace/src/telemetry.rs
pub struct SpanGuard { /* trace_id, span_id, kind, name, binary, started: Instant, ctx, status */ }

impl SpanGuard {
    /// Opens a span. Never fails: an unusable telemetry path yields a guard that writes nothing.
    pub fn start(kind: SpanKind, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    /// Emits children with this span as parent (used by the gate step runner).
    pub fn child(&self, kind: SpanKind, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    /// Records the terminal status/code; `Drop` writes the line.
    pub fn finish_with_status(self, status: SpanStatus, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Self;
    /// The environment a child process must inherit (D3).
    pub fn export_env(&self) -> [(String, String); 2];
}

impl Drop for SpanGuard { /* one append, fail-open, never panics */ }
```

Rules the guard must hold, each a test:

1. **Fail-open.** A read-only or missing directory produces a no-op guard. Telemetry must never
   change an exit code — the first time a flight recorder breaks a gate is the last time it is
   trusted.
2. **No panic in `Drop`.** A panic during unwinding is an abort; every fallible step is `if let Ok`.
3. **One line per span.** The buffer is built with `serde_json::to_vec` and written with a single
   `write_all` of `json + b"\n"` — never two writes, or two processes can interleave mid-line.
4. **`finish_with_status` before `Drop` wins.** Explicit finish sets the status; `Drop` only writes
   if it has not already, or a `?`-early-return path would write `Running` for a failed command.
5. **Lazy identity.** `trace_id` is inherited from `GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID` when present, otherwise
   generated once per process — so two `miter` calls in one session share a trace but two CLI runs
   do not.

### 5.2 `gaugeblock-mcp` dispatcher (`SpanKind::McpTool`)

`stdio.rs::dispatch` / `dispatch_async` are wrapped on the `Route::CallTool` arm only: `initialize`,
`tools/list` and `ping` are protocol housekeeping, and recording them would triple the event volume
for zero information. Each call emits `binary` (the server's own name), `name` (the tool),
`session_id` (`<binary>-<pid>-<process_start_ms>`), `status` from `ToolOutcome`, `input_summary`
(scrubbed, ≤ 512 bytes) and, when the tool is `miter` or `storypole`, `attributes`
`output_symbols_touched` / `files_referenced` taken from the response envelope it already builds.

### 5.3 CLI entry points (`SpanKind::CliCommand`)

One guard per process, opened in the binary's `main` after argument parsing (so the span name is the
subcommand, e.g. `miter.lookup`, not `miter`) and finished at the top-level `anyhow::Result`
boundary. Eight of eleven binaries already return a single `Result` from `main`, so this is one
binding and one `.finish_with_status(...)` per binary.

### 5.4 `outfeed gate` (`SpanKind::GateStep`)

`run_gate_steps` already loops over `Vec<GateStep>` and calls `execute(dir, &step.command)`. Each
iteration opens a child guard named `GateStep.name`, and `execute` sets on the spawned `Command`:

```rust
cmd.env("GAUGEBLOCK_TRACE_ID", &guard.trace_id)
   .env("GAUGEBLOCK_PARENT_SPAN_ID", &guard.span_id)
   .env("GAUGEBLOCK_TASK_KEY", ...);   // when inferable
```

so `cargo clippy`'s own nested `miter`/`chalkline` spans, and any MCP call made while the gate runs,
reparent onto the step. Skipped steps emit `SpanStatus::Skipped` with `duration_ms: 0` — a skip is
not a pass, which is the same distinction `GateStepResult::skipped` already makes.

### 5.5 `sawhorse` inference (`SpanKind::LlmInference`)

`RoleRouter::complete` and `complete_stream` emit one span per *attempt* (not per role), so a
fallback chain shows the failed provider and the provider that answered as siblings. `token_usage`
is copied from `InferenceResponse.token_usage` semantics already present
(`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `model: model_used`); `reasoning_tokens` and the role go to
`attributes`. No provider implementation changes.


---

## 6. Training-capture enrichment (why three optional fields exist)

The observability dashboard needs thirteen fields. `rabbet`'s dataset builder needs three more, and
they are optional precisely so a successful span stays small:

| Field | Populated by | Purpose |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `input_summary` | `gaugeblock-mcp` (`McpTool`), CLI guard | what was asked, so a trajectory can be replayed without the raw arguments |
| `first_diagnostic` | `outfeed gate` (`GateStep`, `status == Error`) | the rejection reason that a repair must answer |
| `worktree_diff_hash` | `outfeed gate` (`GateStep`) | content address of the diff the step judged |

Capture rules:

1. **`input_summary` is scrubbed and capped at 512 bytes.** Scrubbing reuses `miter`'s existing
   literal redaction; the cap is applied to the *serialised compact* JSON, and truncation appends
   `…` so a downstream parser can tell "short" from "truncated". Over-long input is dropped rather
   than truncated mid-token, because half a JSON object trains nothing and confuses a reader.
2. **`worktree_diff_hash` = `sha256` of `git diff HEAD`** in the gate's working directory, computed
   once per gate run (not per step) and reused for every step span, so all failures in one run share
   an address.
3. **On failure**, the first actionable line of the step's own output (already reduced by
   `first_meaningful_line`) becomes `first_diagnostic`, and the scrubbed unified diff is written to
   `.gaugeblock/telemetry/snapshots/<worktree_diff_hash>.diff` — content-addressed, so re-running a
   failing gate rewrites the same file rather than growing the directory.
4. **On a later passing run of the same `(task_key, step_name)`**, the passing diff is snapshotted
   too. `Error(A) → Ok(B)`, `A != B`, is the `(rejected_diff, first_diagnostic) → chosen_diff`
   repair pair `GB-244` mines. **This ticket only guarantees the pair can be reconstructed**; it
   never writes a `SpoolEntry`.
5. A snapshot write is subject to the same fail-open rule as the span write. A missing snapshot
   degrades `GB-244`'s yield; it must never fail a gate.


---

## 7. Ordered plan steps

| # | Step | Files | Verification gate |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **T1** | Land the wire contract and the writer. Split `telemetry.rs` into a directory, add `spans.rs`, add `GaugeblockPaths::telemetry_*`, implement `emit_span` + `SpanGuard`, and add `.gaugeblock/telemetry/` to the root `.gitignore`. | `contracts/telemetry/{mod,spool,spans}.rs`, `workspace/src/{paths,telemetry}.rs`, root `.gitignore` | `cargo nextest run -p gaugeblock-contracts -p gaugeblock-workspace` (round-trip, absent-field, fail-open, one-line, concurrent-append and unwinding tests) |
| **T2** | Wire the choke points: the `gaugeblock-mcp` dispatcher wrap, `outfeed gate` step spans with `GAUGEBLOCK_PARENT_SPAN_ID` child propagation, `sawhorse-core` inference spans, and the top-level CLI guards. | `mcp/src/{telemetry_middleware,stdio}.rs`, `outfeed-core/src/gate/{execute,mod}.rs`, `sawhorse-core/src/{telemetry,router}.rs` | `cargo nextest run -p gaugeblock-mcp -p outfeed-core -p sawhorse-core`; a fixture repo whose `cargo` child inherits the two variables asserts the parent link |
| **T3** | Implement `telemetry_tailer.rs`, the SQLite index (WAL, byte-offset table), and the SSE + REST endpoints in `benchwork`. | `benchwork-core/src/telemetry_tailer.rs` (+ `telemetry_index.rs` if split), `benchwork-cli/src/daemon/{routes_telemetry,mod}.rs`, `benchwork-core/Cargo.toml` (**add `notify`, `rusqlite`**) | `cargo nextest run -p benchwork-core -p benchwork-cli` — append-then-resume test asserts zero duplicates and zero drops across a restart |
| **T4** | Build `ExecutionWaterfallView.tsx` in Panel 3, the `LiveAggregatorPill` in the header, the `useTelemetryStream` hook, and surface law 12 rollups in Panel 4 (`ModelTelemetryHub`). | `web/src/panels/SynthesisXray/{ExecutionWaterfallView.tsx,SynthesisXrayPanel.tsx}`, `web/src/components/LiveAggregatorPill.tsx`, `web/src/api/useTelemetryStream.ts`, `web/src/panels/ModelTelemetryHub/SpoolTraceTable.tsx` | `bun run build` (tsc) + a Playwright e2e that renders a seeded two-level tree |
| **T5** | End-to-end verification under law 12: measure `SpanGuard` overhead, trigger an MCP tool call and an `outfeed gate` run from *outside* `benchwork`, and confirm the parent-child tree renders live over SSE. | — | `miter contracts`, `outfeed gate`, `chalkline docs check` + the recorded numbers in §8 |

Sequencing notes:

* T1 and T2 are the only steps that touch shared crates, so they land before T3 — `benchwork` cannot
  tail a file whose schema is still moving.
* T3's dependency additions are the only manifest churn in the ticket, and they are additive.
* T4 can be developed against a seeded fixture (`tests/fixtures/telemetry/events.jsonl`) without a
  running gate, so the panel is not blocked on T5.
* T5 is a *measurement* step, not a smoke test: it exists to produce the numbers in §8.


---

## 8. Measurements to record (law 12 — no claim without a number)

| What | How | Where it is recorded |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `SpanGuard` overhead | 10 000 `start`+`drop` cycles with the telemetry path writable vs. pointed at a read-only directory, same machine, sequential | commit message that lands T1, plus `common/PERF.md` |
| Emit latency, worst case | times the single `write_all` at the 99th percentile with 4 concurrent writers appending | same commit; target `< 100 µs` from D1 |
| SSE end-to-end latency | append from a plain `miter` CLI run, measure until the `EventSource` callback fires; target `< 250 ms` (acceptance criterion) | T5, in `benchwork/README.md` perf note |
| Gate instrumentation cost | `outfeed gate` wall time with telemetry on vs. off, warm cache, same tree | commit message that lands T2 |
| Index size growth | `index.sqlite`, `events.jsonl` and snapshot bytes after one full Tier 3 gate run | T5 |

If a number comes back worse than the target, it is recorded as a regression, not omitted.

## 9. Out of scope (deferred deliberately)

* **Retention, rotation, compaction.** `events.jsonl` grows without bound in this ticket. Rotating it
  is a separate decision (which spans survive?) and belongs in its own ticket, not smuggled into T3.
* **Mining or dataset emission.** `GB-244` owns `distill-telemetry`; this ticket guarantees the
  records and the snapshots exist, nothing more.
* **Typed MCP protocol migration** (`GB-235`) — orthogonal refactor of the same dispatcher.
* **Span-based alerting or budgets** in `benchwork` (e.g. "clippy p95 regressed"). Useful, needs the
  history first.
* **`AstPass` kind** is defined in the enum but emitted by nothing in this ticket; it exists so
  `miter`/`dado`/`batten` passes can be added without a schema bump.
* **A `benchwork-mcp` tool** exposing spans to an agent. Later.

## 10. Risks and how the plan answers them

| Risk | Answer |
|:--|:--|
| A telemetry bug breaks a gate | Fail-open is a test in T1, not a convention. The no-op guard returns the same value the caller had. |
| Span volume floods the daemon | MCP housekeeping methods are excluded; the broadcast channel for spans is separate from the 256-slot `LiveEvent` channel so a burst cannot evict a task update. |
| `gate/mod.rs` (224 LOC) crosses 250 | Extract `gate/steps.rs` before adding anything; the plan names the trigger explicitly. |
| The diff snapshot captures a secret | The snapshot is scrubbed by the same path as `input_summary`, and lives under a gitignored directory with a content-addressed name. |
| `benchwork-core` grows two dependencies for a feature it may not always ship | Both sit behind the same crate that already depends on eight suite crates; the tailer is one module and can be feature-gated if it ever needs to be. |
| Two processes write the same `events.jsonl` concurrently | `O_APPEND` plus a single `write_all` per line; a concurrent-append test with 4 writers asserts no interleaved line. |
