plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-244 — `rabbet distill-telemetry`

> **Key:** `GB-244` · **Kind:** Feature · **Priority:** P2 · **Repo:** `rabbet`
> **Scope:** `rabbet-core`, `rabbet-cli`, `gaugeblock-contracts`
> **Depends on:** `GB-243` (the flight recorder that produces the spans) and `GB-182` (the canonical
> `SpoolEntry` envelope this command must write). Neither is optional: without `GB-243` there is no
> `events.jsonl`, and without `GB-182` the record this command emits is a bare trace the ingest gate
> cannot hash.
> **Status:** Planned — blocked on both.

---

## 1. What it reads, and what it writes

| Input | Where | Provenance |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `TelemetrySpan` lines | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl` | `GB-243` D1 (`O_APPEND`, one line per span) |
| Span queries (P50/P95, joins) | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite` | `GB-243` D4 (derived; rebuildable) |
| Rejected and accepted diffs | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/snapshots/<hash>.diff` | `GB-243` §6 (content-addressed) |
| `VerificationReceipt` | `.gaugeblock/storypole/index.sqlite`, `tasks.raw_json` | `storypole verify` |
| Output envelopes | `.gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl` | `GB-182` `SpoolEntry` |
| Output datasets | `.gaugeblock/datasets/{gate_repair_dpo,agent_trajectory_dpo}.parquet` | this ticket |

Two measured facts about the inputs, because both change the implementation:

1. **`VerificationReceipt` has no `modified_files` field.** Its fields are exactly `verifier`,
   `command`, `exit_code`, `diagnostic_count`, `summary`, `verified_at_epoch_ms`, `git_branch`,
   `base_commit_sha`, `head_commit_sha`, `commit_shas`. So "the files the receipt touched" is
   *derived*: `git show --name-only <sha>` over `commit_shas`, falling back to
   `git diff --name-only base..head` when the list is empty, and skipped with a counted reason when
   both are absent. **The label is the commit, not a field.**
2. **Coverage is good but not total.** Of 200 verified tasks in the current index, 71 of the first 80
   carry `commit_shas` (~89%). The remaining ~11% can still be mined when `base_commit_sha` and
   `head_commit_sha` are present. Every skip is counted by reason and printed — a silent 10% loss is
   how a dataset acquires a bias nobody can see.

## 2. Decisions (resolved on the ticket)

| # | Decision | Chosen | Category |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | Repair-pair identification | `Error(A)` → next `Ok(B)` on the same `(task_key, step_name)`, `A != B`, emitted as a `Gold` `SpoolEntry` | `dataset` |
| D2 | Trajectory pruning | `McpTool`/`CliCommand` spans intersected with the receipt's commits define the minimal sufficient chain | `dataset` |
| D3 | Fail-fast ordering export | `fail_probability / p50_duration_ms` per repository and step, exported, not applied | `telemetry` |

**D1.** Pair any `SpanKind::GateStep` with `status == Error` (`worktree_diff_hash = A`,
`first_diagnostic`) against the next `SpanKind::GateStep` on the same `(task_key, step_name)` with
`status == Ok` (`worktree_diff_hash = B`, `A != B`). Emit a `Gold` DPO record — `context` = task plan
+ `first_diagnostic`, `rejected` = snapshot `A`, `chosen` = snapshot `B` — into
`.gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl` wrapped in the canonical `SpoolEntry`, and export to
`gate_repair_dpo.parquet`.

Keying on the step name is the point: a `clippy` failure later repaired by a formatting-only change
shows up as `fmt Ok`, `clippy` still `Error`, and proximity-only pairing would learn `fmt` as the
fix. Requiring `A != B` rejects the common case of a step simply re-run, which is a rebuild, not a
repair. Records go through the outbox rather than straight to Parquet so the existing ingest gate
(placeholder and secret checks) judges them like any other trace.

**D2.** For every `Verified` task, inspect all `SpanKind::McpTool` and `SpanKind::CliCommand` spans
between `Claimed` and `Verified`. Calls whose queried files or symbols intersect the final receipt's
commits form the **Minimal Sufficient Trajectory** (`chosen`); tasks with high-thrash subsequences
(3+ redundant searches or failed invocations before finding the target) supply the raw trajectory
(`rejected`), training `ModelRole::System1Router` and `Planner` to pick the right `miter`/`storypole`
query on the first turn. The receipt is the label source because it is already a durable, verifiable
fact; a judge model would add inference cost and a second thing that can be wrong. Spans touching
nothing in the receipt are kept — they are what makes the rejected half a real trajectory rather
than a strawman.

**D3.** Compute per-repository, per-step `fail_probability` and P50 duration and export
`fail_probability / p50_duration_ms`, so `outfeed gate --fail-fast-order` can optionally run
high-failure-density, sub-second checks (`docs`, `lockfiles`, `fmt`) before multi-second compiler
passes. This ticket exports the ranking and does not change the default matrix: the canonical order
in `gate_steps()` is part of what Tier 3 means, and flipping it silently would make two gates
disagree about the same word. Parallel execution was rejected — the gate is deliberately sequential
so a lockfile failure is reported before a compile.

---

## 3. Module layout and budget (every file ≤ 250 LOC)

"Today" is `wc -l` on this checkout.

| # | File | Action | Budget | Today | Note |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill_repairs.rs` | new | ≤ 210 | — | scan `Error` → `Ok` transitions on `(task_key, GateStep, name)`, load snapshots, build `Gold` `SpoolEntry` records |
| 2 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill_trajectories.rs` | new | ≤ 220 | — | join `McpTool`/`CliCommand` spans for `Verified` tasks against receipt commits; `Silver` SFT chains and `Gold` pruned-vs-unpruned pairs |
| 3 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill/mod.rs` | new | ≤ 80 | — | shared types: `DistillOptions`, `DistillReport`, `SkipReason`, the `TelemetryReader` trait |
| 4 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill/telemetry_reader.rs` | new | ≤ 170 | — | reads `events.jsonl` (streaming) and/or `index.sqlite`; the JSONL path is authoritative so this works before D4's index exists |
| 5 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/schemas.rs` | update | ≤ 110 | 42 | add `gate_repair_dpo_schema()` and `agent_trajectory_dpo_schema()` |
| 6 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/datasets.rs` | new | ≤ 150 | — | builds the `RecordBatch`es and calls the existing `write_parquet_file` (37 LOC, reused unchanged) |
| 6b | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/exporter.rs` | **unchanged** | 250 | 204 | **46 lines of headroom — the new datasets do not belong in this file**; growing it is the trap |
| 7 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-cli/src/commands/distill_telemetry.rs` | new | ≤ 150 | — | `rabbet distill-telemetry [--since <tag>] [--export-parquet] [--json]` |
| 8 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-cli/src/args.rs` | update | ≤ 220 | 170 | one `Command::DistillTelemetry` variant + a `DistillTelemetryArgs` struct; if it passes 220 the args split into `args/` like `storypole-cli` did in `GB-182` |

**No new dependencies.** `rabbet-core` already declares `arrow 60`, `parquet 60` (`arrow` + `snap`),
`rusqlite 0.40` (`bundled`), `sha2 0.10` and `serde_json` — every piece the miner needs. A command
that adds a dependency to read a text file would be a smell.

**Scrubbing goes through `gaugeblock-security`, not `miter`.** The brief says "scrubs literals via
`miter`"; `rabbet-core` has no `miter` dependency and must not gain one. `miter` and `rabbet` are
different products, so the edge would be lateral, and `miter deps --layers --check` — a Tier 3 gate
step — rejects new lateral edges outside the allowlist (the file currently lists **zero** edges for
`rabbet-core`). The existing path is already correct and already imported:
`gaugeblock_security::scrub_source_text`, used by `rabbet-core/src/gate/scrubber.rs`.

**Reading `storypole`'s index is raw SQL, not a crate dependency.** For the same layering reason,
`rabbet-core` must not depend on `storypole-core`. The receipt is reachable as
`select raw_json from tasks where status = 'verified'` and deserialising the embedded
`verification_receipt`. That keeps `rabbet` behind the *file* contract rather than a Rust type it
would have to version against.

## 4. Dataset shapes

`gate_repair_dpo.parquet` (extends the existing DPO convention in `parquet/schemas.rs`):

| Column | Type | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `task_key` | Utf8, not null | span |
| `step_name` | Utf8, not null | `GateStep.name` (`fmt`/`clippy`/`tests`/`contracts`/`layers`/`lockfiles`/`docs`) |
| `context` | Utf8, not null | task plan excerpt + `first_diagnostic` |
| `rejected` | Utf8, not null | snapshot `A` (scrubbed) |
| `chosen` | Utf8, not null | snapshot `B` (scrubbed) |
| `rejected_hash` / `chosen_hash` | Utf8, not null | the two `worktree_diff_hash` values |
| `quality_tier` | Utf8, not null | literal `gold` |

`agent_trajectory_dpo.parquet`:

| Column | Type | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `task_key` | Utf8, not null | receipt |
| `role` | Utf8, not null | `system1_router` or `planner` |
| `chosen_calls` | Utf8, not null | minimal sufficient call sequence (compact JSON array) |
| `rejected_calls` | Utf8, null | thrashing sequence, when one exists |
| `touched_files` | Utf8, not null | derived from `commit_shas` |
| `quality_tier` | Utf8, not null | `silver` for a chain, `gold` for a pair |

Both shards are written with the existing Snappy `write_parquet_file`, so compression, directory
creation and row counting are not re-implemented.


---

## 5. Command surface

```text
rabbet distill-telemetry [--since <tag>] [--export-parquet] [--json] [--dry-run]
                         [--telemetry <path>] [--storypole <path>] [--datasets <dir>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `--since <tag>` | Only spans whose `started_at_ms` is at or after the commit date of `<tag>`; the default is all recorded history |
| `--export-parquet` | Also writes the two shards into `.gaugeblock/datasets/`; without it only the outbox records are appended |
| `--dry-run` | Counts what would be emitted and writes nothing — the flag that makes the yield figures in §7 reproducible |
| `--json` | Machine-readable report: `{ "repair_pairs": n, "trajectories": n, "skipped": {...by reason...}, "parquet_rows": {...} }` |

Defaults resolve through `gaugeblock-workspace`'s canonical paths, not `current_dir` — the same rule
`GB-189` establishes for every other `.gaugeblock/` consumer. Records appended to the outbox are
idempotent: the `SpoolEntry` content hash of an unchanged pair is identical, so a second run adds
nothing and reports `0 new, N duplicate` rather than appending a second copy of the same pair.

## 6. Ordered plan steps

| # | Step | Files | Verification gate |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **D1** | Implement `distill_repairs.rs` and `distill/mod.rs`: pair failed vs. passing `outfeed gate` snapshots into `Gold` DPO `SpoolEntry` records, with scrubbing through `gaugeblock-security`. Fixtures cover: a real repair (`A != B`), a rebuilt-unchanged step (`A == B`, skipped), a missing snapshot (skipped and counted), and an `Ok` with no preceding `Error` (skipped). | `rabbet-core/src/distill_repairs.rs`, `distill/mod.rs`, `distill/telemetry_reader.rs` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core distill_repairs` |
| **D2** | Implement `distill_trajectories.rs`: correlate `McpTool`/`CliCommand` span sequences with receipt commits (via `git show --name-only`), producing `Silver` SFT minimal chains and `Gold` pruned-vs-unpruned pairs. Fixtures cover a task whose receipt has `commit_shas`, one with only `base`/`head`, and one with neither (skipped and counted). | `rabbet-core/src/distill_trajectories.rs` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core distill_trajectories` |
| **D3** | Wire `rabbet distill-telemetry` (args, dispatch, `--json` report), add the two Arrow schemas and `parquet/datasets.rs`, and verify end-to-end under law 12 on real workspace telemetry spans. | `rabbet-cli/src/{args.rs,commands/distill_telemetry.rs,commands/mod.rs,main.rs}`, `rabbet-core/src/parquet/{schemas.rs,datasets.rs}` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core -p rabbet-cli`, then `rabbet distill-telemetry --dry-run --json` on the live `.gaugeblock/telemetry/`, then `rabbet ingest` over the resulting outbox asserting `0 rejected` |

Tier 2 for every step: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`,
`chalkline docs check -d rabbet`.

## 7. Measurements to record (law 12)

| What | Where it is recorded |
|:--|:--|
| Repair-pair yield: `Error→Ok` transitions found, pairs emitted, and skip reasons with counts | commit message that lands D1, plus `rabbet/README.md` |
| Trajectory yield: verified tasks scanned, tasks with commits, tasks with a thrashing subsequence, chains vs. pairs | commit message that lands D2 |
| Records rejected by the ingest gate and why | D3 verification output, quoted in the commit |
| Row counts per shard and `.parquet` bytes | D3, in the same commit |
| Fail-fast ranking for the suite root: per-step `fail_probability`, P50 ms, sample count | a durable table in `rabbet/README.md` — a ranking with no sample count is an opinion |

Reported plainly if the yield is bad. A corpus of zero repair pairs is a result: it means either the
gate rarely fails or `GB-243`'s snapshots are not being written, and the two are distinguishable by
the skip reasons.

## 8. Out of scope and risks

Out of scope:

* **Changing the default gate order.** D3 exports a ranking; `outfeed gate --fail-fast-order` is a
  later ticket that consumes it.
* **Training.** This produces datasets. Nothing here runs a model.
* **`Diamond`-tier mining** (survival-in-main), which needs release history, not gate history.
* **Cross-repository repair pairs.** A fix in `miter` that repairs a `benchwork` gate is a real
  signal but it has no shared `(task_key, step_name)` key yet.
* **Deduplicating against the existing three shards.** Those carry hole-filling traces; these carry
  behaviour, and the join key would be `task_key`, which the older shards do not have.

| Risk | Answer |
|:--|:--|
| Snapshots are missing because a gate ran before `GB-243` landed | Every pair is conditional on both snapshots existing; the report counts them, so the dataset is honest from day one rather than padded. |
| A diff snapshot contains a credential | Snapshots are scrubbed at write time by `GB-243` and re-scrubbed at read time here through `gaugeblock_security::scrub_source_text`; a high-entropy hit rejects the record, it does not redact-and-keep. |
| `git show` is slow over hundreds of receipts | Commits are resolved once per run into a `HashMap<task_key, Vec<PathBuf>>` and cached for the process; one `git show --name-only` per sha, batched with `--no-walk`. |
| Re-running the command duplicates records | Idempotent by `SpoolEntry` content hash (§5), proven by a test that runs the miner twice and asserts the second run appends nothing. |
| Trajectory labels are wrong because a task touched a file incidentally | The receipt's commits define "touched"; an incidentally-touched file is still touched. Where a task has no commits, it is skipped rather than guessed. |

plan.summary: Join the span log with VerificationReceipt and the diff snapshots to emit gate_repair_dpo and agent_trajectory_dpo datasets
plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-244 — `rabbet distill-telemetry`

> **Key:** `GB-244` · **Kind:** Feature · **Priority:** P2 · **Repo:** `rabbet`
> **Scope:** `rabbet-core`, `rabbet-cli`, `gaugeblock-contracts`
> **Depends on:** `GB-243` (the flight recorder that produces the spans) and `GB-182` (the canonical
> `SpoolEntry` envelope this command must write). Neither is optional: without `GB-243` there is no
> `events.jsonl`, and without `GB-182` the record this command emits is a bare trace the ingest gate
> cannot hash.
> **Status:** Planned — blocked on both.

---

## 1. What it reads, and what it writes

| Input | Where | Provenance |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `TelemetrySpan` lines | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl` | `GB-243` D1 (`O_APPEND`, one line per span) |
| Span queries (P50/P95, joins) | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite` | `GB-243` D4 (derived; rebuildable) |
| Rejected and accepted diffs | `.gaugeblock/telemetry/snapshots/<hash>.diff` | `GB-243` §6 (content-addressed) |
| `VerificationReceipt` | `.gaugeblock/storypole/index.sqlite`, `tasks.raw_json` | `storypole verify` |
| Output envelopes | `.gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl` | `GB-182` `SpoolEntry` |
| Output datasets | `.gaugeblock/datasets/{gate_repair_dpo,agent_trajectory_dpo}.parquet` | this ticket |

Two measured facts about the inputs, because both change the implementation:

1. **`VerificationReceipt` has no `modified_files` field.** Its fields are exactly `verifier`,
   `command`, `exit_code`, `diagnostic_count`, `summary`, `verified_at_epoch_ms`, `git_branch`,
   `base_commit_sha`, `head_commit_sha`, `commit_shas`. So "the files the receipt touched" is
   *derived*: `git show --name-only <sha>` over `commit_shas`, falling back to
   `git diff --name-only base..head` when the list is empty, and skipped with a counted reason when
   both are absent. **The label is the commit, not a field.**
2. **Coverage is good but not total.** Of 200 verified tasks in the current index, 71 of the first 80
   carry `commit_shas` (~89%). The remaining ~11% can still be mined when `base_commit_sha` and
   `head_commit_sha` are present. Every skip is counted by reason and printed — a silent 10% loss is
   how a dataset acquires a bias nobody can see.

## 2. Decisions (resolved on the ticket)

| # | Decision | Chosen | Category |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | Repair-pair identification | `Error(A)` → next `Ok(B)` on the same `(task_key, step_name)`, `A != B`, emitted as a `Gold` `SpoolEntry` | `dataset` |
| D2 | Trajectory pruning | `McpTool`/`CliCommand` spans intersected with the receipt's commits define the minimal sufficient chain | `dataset` |
| D3 | Fail-fast ordering export | `fail_probability / p50_duration_ms` per repository and step, exported, not applied | `telemetry` |

**D1.** Pair any `SpanKind::GateStep` with `status == Error` (`worktree_diff_hash = A`,
`first_diagnostic`) against the next `SpanKind::GateStep` on the same `(task_key, step_name)` with
`status == Ok` (`worktree_diff_hash = B`, `A != B`). Emit a `Gold` DPO record — `context` = task plan
+ `first_diagnostic`, `rejected` = snapshot `A`, `chosen` = snapshot `B` — into
`.gaugeblock/spool/outbox.jsonl` wrapped in the canonical `SpoolEntry`, and export to
`gate_repair_dpo.parquet`.

Keying on the step name is the point: a `clippy` failure later repaired by a formatting-only change
shows up as `fmt Ok`, `clippy` still `Error`, and proximity-only pairing would learn `fmt` as the
fix. Requiring `A != B` rejects the common case of a step simply re-run, which is a rebuild, not a
repair. Records go through the outbox rather than straight to Parquet so the existing ingest gate
(placeholder and secret checks) judges them like any other trace.

**D2.** For every `Verified` task, inspect all `SpanKind::McpTool` and `SpanKind::CliCommand` spans
between `Claimed` and `Verified`. Calls whose queried files or symbols intersect the final receipt's
commits form the **Minimal Sufficient Trajectory** (`chosen`); tasks with high-thrash subsequences
(3+ redundant searches or failed invocations before finding the target) supply the raw trajectory
(`rejected`), training `ModelRole::System1Router` and `Planner` to pick the right `miter`/`storypole`
query on the first turn. The receipt is the label source because it is already a durable, verifiable
fact; a judge model would add inference cost and a second thing that can be wrong. Spans touching
nothing in the receipt are kept — they are what makes the rejected half a real trajectory rather
than a strawman.

**D3.** Compute per-repository, per-step `fail_probability` and P50 duration and export
`fail_probability / p50_duration_ms`, so `outfeed gate --fail-fast-order` can optionally run
high-failure-density, sub-second checks (`docs`, `lockfiles`, `fmt`) before multi-second compiler
passes. This ticket exports the ranking and does not change the default matrix: the canonical order
in `gate_steps()` is part of what Tier 3 means, and flipping it silently would make two gates
disagree about the same word. Parallel execution was rejected — the gate is deliberately sequential
so a lockfile failure is reported before a compile.

---

## 3. Module layout and budget (every file ≤ 250 LOC)

"Today" is `wc -l` on this checkout.

| # | File | Action | Budget | Today | Note |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill_repairs.rs` | new | ≤ 210 | — | scan `Error` → `Ok` transitions on `(task_key, GateStep, name)`, load snapshots, build `Gold` `SpoolEntry` records |
| 2 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill_trajectories.rs` | new | ≤ 220 | — | join `McpTool`/`CliCommand` spans for `Verified` tasks against receipt commits; `Silver` SFT chains and `Gold` pruned-vs-unpruned pairs |
| 3 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill/mod.rs` | new | ≤ 80 | — | shared types: `DistillOptions`, `DistillReport`, `SkipReason`, the `TelemetryReader` trait |
| 4 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/distill/telemetry_reader.rs` | new | ≤ 170 | — | reads `events.jsonl` (streaming) and/or `index.sqlite`; the JSONL path is authoritative so this works before D4's index exists |
| 5 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/schemas.rs` | update | ≤ 110 | 42 | add `gate_repair_dpo_schema()` and `agent_trajectory_dpo_schema()` |
| 6 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/datasets.rs` | new | ≤ 150 | — | builds the `RecordBatch`es and calls the existing `write_parquet_file` (37 LOC, reused unchanged) |
| 6b | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-core/src/parquet/exporter.rs` | **unchanged** | 250 | 204 | **46 lines of headroom — the new datasets do not belong in this file**; growing it is the trap |
| 7 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-cli/src/commands/distill_telemetry.rs` | new | ≤ 150 | — | `rabbet distill-telemetry [--since <tag>] [--export-parquet] [--json]` |
| 8 | `rabbet/crates/rabbet-cli/src/args.rs` | update | ≤ 220 | 170 | one `Command::DistillTelemetry` variant + a `DistillTelemetryArgs` struct; if it passes 220 the args split into `args/` like `storypole-cli` did in `GB-182` |

**No new dependencies.** `rabbet-core` already declares `arrow 60`, `parquet 60` (`arrow` + `snap`),
`rusqlite 0.40` (`bundled`), `sha2 0.10` and `serde_json` — every piece the miner needs. A command
that adds a dependency to read a text file would be a smell.

**Scrubbing goes through `gaugeblock-security`, not `miter`.** The brief says "scrubs literals via
`miter`"; `rabbet-core` has no `miter` dependency and must not gain one. `miter` and `rabbet` are
different products, so the edge would be lateral, and `miter deps --layers --check` — a Tier 3 gate
step — rejects new lateral edges outside the allowlist (the file currently lists **zero** edges for
`rabbet-core`). The existing path is already correct and already imported:
`gaugeblock_security::scrub_source_text`, used by `rabbet-core/src/gate/scrubber.rs`.

**Reading `storypole`'s index is raw SQL, not a crate dependency.** For the same layering reason,
`rabbet-core` must not depend on `storypole-core`. The receipt is reachable as
`select raw_json from tasks where status = 'verified'` and deserialising the embedded
`verification_receipt`. That keeps `rabbet` behind the *file* contract rather than a Rust type it
would have to version against.

## 4. Dataset shapes

`gate_repair_dpo.parquet` (extends the existing DPO convention in `parquet/schemas.rs`):

| Column | Type | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `task_key` | Utf8, not null | span |
| `step_name` | Utf8, not null | `GateStep.name` (`fmt`/`clippy`/`tests`/`contracts`/`layers`/`lockfiles`/`docs`) |
| `context` | Utf8, not null | task plan excerpt + `first_diagnostic` |
| `rejected` | Utf8, not null | snapshot `A` (scrubbed) |
| `chosen` | Utf8, not null | snapshot `B` (scrubbed) |
| `rejected_hash` / `chosen_hash` | Utf8, not null | the two `worktree_diff_hash` values |
| `quality_tier` | Utf8, not null | literal `gold` |

`agent_trajectory_dpo.parquet`:

| Column | Type | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `task_key` | Utf8, not null | receipt |
| `role` | Utf8, not null | `system1_router` or `planner` |
| `chosen_calls` | Utf8, not null | minimal sufficient call sequence (compact JSON array) |
| `rejected_calls` | Utf8, null | thrashing sequence, when one exists |
| `touched_files` | Utf8, not null | derived from `commit_shas` |
| `quality_tier` | Utf8, not null | `silver` for a chain, `gold` for a pair |

Both shards are written with the existing Snappy `write_parquet_file`, so compression, directory
creation and row counting are not re-implemented.


---

## 5. Command surface

```text
rabbet distill-telemetry [--since <tag>] [--export-parquet] [--json] [--dry-run]
                         [--telemetry <path>] [--storypole <path>] [--datasets <dir>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `--since <tag>` | Only spans whose `started_at_ms` is at or after the commit date of `<tag>`; the default is all recorded history |
| `--export-parquet` | Also writes the two shards into `.gaugeblock/datasets/`; without it only the outbox records are appended |
| `--dry-run` | Counts what would be emitted and writes nothing — the flag that makes the yield figures in §7 reproducible |
| `--json` | Machine-readable report: `{ "repair_pairs": n, "trajectories": n, "skipped": {...by reason...}, "parquet_rows": {...} }` |

Defaults resolve through `gaugeblock-workspace`'s canonical paths, not `current_dir` — the same rule
`GB-189` establishes for every other `.gaugeblock/` consumer. Records appended to the outbox are
idempotent: the `SpoolEntry` content hash of an unchanged pair is identical, so a second run adds
nothing and reports `0 new, N duplicate` rather than appending a second copy of the same pair.

## 6. Ordered plan steps

| # | Step | Files | Verification gate |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **D1** | Implement `distill_repairs.rs` and `distill/mod.rs`: pair failed vs. passing `outfeed gate` snapshots into `Gold` DPO `SpoolEntry` records, with scrubbing through `gaugeblock-security`. Fixtures cover: a real repair (`A != B`), a rebuilt-unchanged step (`A == B`, skipped), a missing snapshot (skipped and counted), and an `Ok` with no preceding `Error` (skipped). | `rabbet-core/src/distill_repairs.rs`, `distill/mod.rs`, `distill/telemetry_reader.rs` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core distill_repairs` |
| **D2** | Implement `distill_trajectories.rs`: correlate `McpTool`/`CliCommand` span sequences with receipt commits (via `git show --name-only`), producing `Silver` SFT minimal chains and `Gold` pruned-vs-unpruned pairs. Fixtures cover a task whose receipt has `commit_shas`, one with only `base`/`head`, and one with neither (skipped and counted). | `rabbet-core/src/distill_trajectories.rs` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core distill_trajectories` |
| **D3** | Wire `rabbet distill-telemetry` (args, dispatch, `--json` report), add the two Arrow schemas and `parquet/datasets.rs`, and verify end-to-end under law 12 on real workspace telemetry spans. | `rabbet-cli/src/{args.rs,commands/distill_telemetry.rs,commands/mod.rs,main.rs}`, `rabbet-core/src/parquet/{schemas.rs,datasets.rs}` | `cargo nextest run -p rabbet-core -p rabbet-cli`, then `rabbet distill-telemetry --dry-run --json` on the live `.gaugeblock/telemetry/`, then `rabbet ingest` over the resulting outbox asserting `0 rejected` |

Tier 2 for every step: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`,
`chalkline docs check -d rabbet`.

## 7. Measurements to record (law 12)

| What | Where it is recorded |
|:--|:--|
| Repair-pair yield: `Error→Ok` transitions found, pairs emitted, and skip reasons with counts | commit message that lands D1, plus `rabbet/README.md` |
| Trajectory yield: verified tasks scanned, tasks with commits, tasks with a thrashing subsequence, chains vs. pairs | commit message that lands D2 |
| Records rejected by the ingest gate and why | D3 verification output, quoted in the commit |
| Row counts per shard and `.parquet` bytes | D3, in the same commit |
| Fail-fast ranking for the suite root: per-step `fail_probability`, P50 ms, sample count | a durable table in `rabbet/README.md` — a ranking with no sample count is an opinion |

Reported plainly if the yield is bad. A corpus of zero repair pairs is a result: it means either the
gate rarely fails or `GB-243`'s snapshots are not being written, and the two are distinguishable by
the skip reasons.

## 8. Out of scope and risks

Out of scope:

* **Changing the default gate order.** D3 exports a ranking; `outfeed gate --fail-fast-order` is a
  later ticket that consumes it.
* **Training.** This produces datasets. Nothing here runs a model.
* **`Diamond`-tier mining** (survival-in-main), which needs release history, not gate history.
* **Cross-repository repair pairs.** A fix in `miter` that repairs a `benchwork` gate is a real
  signal but it has no shared `(task_key, step_name)` key yet.
* **Deduplicating against the existing three shards.** Those carry hole-filling traces; these carry
  behaviour, and the join key would be `task_key`, which the older shards do not have.

| Risk | Answer |
|:--|:--|
| Snapshots are missing because a gate ran before `GB-243` landed | Every pair is conditional on both snapshots existing; the report counts them, so the dataset is honest from day one rather than padded. |
| A diff snapshot contains a credential | Snapshots are scrubbed at write time by `GB-243` and re-scrubbed at read time here through `gaugeblock_security::scrub_source_text`; a high-entropy hit rejects the record, it does not redact-and-keep. |
| `git show` is slow over hundreds of receipts | Commits are resolved once per run into a `HashMap<task_key, Vec<PathBuf>>` and cached for the process; one `git show --name-only` per sha, batched with `--no-walk`. |
| Re-running the command duplicates records | Idempotent by `SpoolEntry` content hash (§5), proven by a test that runs the miner twice and asserts the second run appends nothing. |
| Trajectory labels are wrong because a task touched a file incidentally | The receipt's commits define "touched"; an incidentally-touched file is still touched. Where a task has no commits, it is skipped rather than guessed. |

task.description: Reproduced 2026-11-06 while certifying eleven delivered tickets. Running 'storypole verify GB-28 --dir storypole' created storypole/spool/outbox.jsonl (592 bytes, one silver trace) and the same happened in outfeed/, benchwork/ and chalkline/ - four stray spool directories in four repositories, none of them canonical. The root-ledger verifies wrote to .gaugeblock/spool/ as expected, so the defect is only on the --dir path. Likely the spool path is derived from the store root instead of GaugeblockPaths, which is the same class of bug GB-189 exists to remove. Leaked into the working tree as untracked directories that a 'git add -A' would commit.

description: WorkspaceStore sync_all_members event replay ordering and distribute event synchronization.\n\nEVIDENCE 2026-11-06 (measured while closing ten stale tickets): the SAME task id lives in both the root ledger and the owning member ledger - GB-28 is a655439f-8f4d-49d3-b24d-89f01fdfe164 in .gaugeblock/storypole/ledger.jsonl AND in storypole/.storypole/ledger.jsonl, and likewise GB-47/GB-48/GB-55 in outfeed, GB-34/GB-35/GB-37 in benchwork, GB-57 in storypole. 'storypole verify GB-28' at the harness root appended task_verified to the ROOT ledger only; the member replay still read ready, so the unified list, the benchwork DagBoard and every member-scoped view kept reporting the ticket as open while the root copy said verified. The fix that worked was to re-run the same verify with --dir <member> so the event landed in the owning ledger too, which leaves two receipts for one act. Distribution is one-way (task records are copied, later events are not), so any state transition performed through the wrong store silently diverges. Needs: sync_all_members to reconcile per-task event logs in timestamp order, and distribute to carry forward events that postdate the copy.

decision.question: D1 Edge disposition: the 19 remaining lateral edges are three different problems measured separately (135 import sites, 62 files), so one blanket policy cannot be right. A - 7 edges are already-paid moves (types/behaviour already live in gaugeblock-contracts, miter-inventory, miter-polyglot or gaugeblock-workspace): batten->dado 5, chalkline->miter-engine 12, benchwork->miter-engine 4, dado->miter-engine 3, joiner->miter-engine 3, plus the type halves of benchwork->sawhorse (types already in contracts, secret resolution already in gaugeblock-workspace env_credentials) and benchwork->storypole (TaskNode/TaskStatus/TaskScope/EdgeKind/TaskDecision/HandoffPacket already in contracts::storypole). B - 7 edges are orchestrator-by-design (joiner->dado 9, joiner->batten 4, joiner->miter-harness 2, benchwork->chalkline 4, benchwork->joiner 4, benchwork->dado 3, benchwork->batten 2): inverting them would re-invent the crates whose whole purpose is composition. proposed_options: A: classify the 7 orchestrator edges into a declared orchestrator layer, then repoint the 7 already-paid edges, then invert the 5 real ones behind a BacklogPort and a CompletionPort (recommended: each edge gets the treatment its nature demands; burn-down 19->14->12->5->2->0)

B: split benchwork-core into domain and hub halves and pull the composition into benchwork-cli, keeping all 19 edges as real inversions (highest total effort, and it does not address the joiner->dado family at all)
C: invert all 19 edges individually behind traits or CLI boundaries, with no classification change
D: declare the orchestrator layer and stop there, leaving 12 edges in the allowlist

description:
PROGRESS 2026-10-31. Four edges burned, 23 -> 19 lateral; allowlist 23 -> 19; downward edges 123 -> 130.

Burned by kind, which is the useful part:
1. `rabbet-core -> miter-engine` - redaction only; `gaugeblock-security` now lives in common (GB-158).
2. `chalkline-core -> sawhorse-core` - `ModelRole`/`InferenceRequest` were already in gaugeblock-contracts; the import predated the move.
3. `dado-core -> chalkline-core` - `SharedTypeContract`/`ContractField` moved to gaugeblock-contracts; dado no longer depends on chalkline at all.
4. `joiner-core -> chalkline-core` - a DEAD coupling: one unused error variant, no other reference anywhere. Deletion, not refactoring.

THE CHEAP VEIN IS NOW EXHAUSTED, measured rather than assumed. A scan of every remaining edge for references outside `error.rs` returned non-zero for all of them (benchwork->storypole 9 files, chalkline->miter-engine 9, benchwork->sawhorse 6, joiner->dado 5, joiner->sawhorse 5, batten->dado 5, and 1 file each for joiner/miter-engine, dado/miter-engine, chalkline/storypole, outfeed/sawhorse, outfeed/storypole, benchwork/miter-engine). So none of the rest is a misplaced type or a dead error variant; they are genuine behaviour crossings.

What that leaves is design, in two shapes. (a) The benchwork decision below: 7 of the 19 edges are benchwork-core composing every other product. (b) Control inversion for the rest - chalkline writes tasks through `add_task`/`link_tasks`, outfeed queries tasks and records receipts, dado and joiner parse through the miter polyglot. Each needs a trait or CLI boundary rather than a move, and each is its own ticket-sized decision.

MEASURED 2026-11-06 (decision D1 raised, 0fa26f40). The 19 remaining edges are 135 import sites across 62 files, and they are three different problems, not one:

A. Already-paid moves, 7 edges: the symbols they reach for already exist in a foundation or split-out crate, so no inversion is needed, only a repoint. batten->dado 5 (TypedHole is in gaugeblock-contracts/src/dado_batten.rs), chalkline->miter-engine 12 (WorkspaceInventory, PublicTypeInventory and inspect_workspace are in miter-inventory), benchwork->miter-engine 4 (same), dado->miter-engine 3 (polyglot is miter-polyglot), joiner->miter-engine 3 (same, plus EngineError), plus the type halves of benchwork->sawhorse (ExecutionMode/InferenceRequest/ModelRole already in contracts::sawhorse, resolve_secret_from_env_file already gaugeblock_workspace::env_credentials) and benchwork->storypole (TaskNode, TaskStatus, TaskScope, EdgeKind, TaskDecision, DecisionStatus, HandoffPacket already in contracts::storypole).

task.description: Reproduced 2026-11-06 while moving miter-inventory into common as gaugeblock-inventory (GB-204). task.title: miter deps --layers should prune and adopt allowlist entries, and fail on an entry that matches no edge
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06 across GB-204 steps 1-3: the allowlist is hand-edited TOML every time an edge changes, so I edited it with python three times. Two gaps follow. (1) PRUNE/ADOPT: after a repoint the entry's 'to' crate changes name (miter-inventory -> gaugeblock-inventory) and after a mitigation the edge disappears; a --prune that deletes entries matching no current edge, and an --adopt --ticket KEY that adds entries for unallowlisted edges, would make burn-down mechanical instead of error-prone. (2) GATE HOLE: --check fails for unallowlisted lateral and for upward edges, but passes when the allowlist holds an entry for an edge that no longer exists. That is a silent suppression waiting to be re-armed: if the edge returns, it is excused without anyone deciding. --check should report stale entries and fail on them.

task.title: Gates and doc checks should take a --baseline rev so pre-existing drift is not confused with mine
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06: after touching a crate I could not tell whether a fmt failure or a docs drift was mine or already on main. I answered it with a git stash round-trip and a manual re-run, twice (dado fmt drift, common docs drift), and once by checking out HEAD~1 files in place. Both are slow and easy to get wrong. 'chalkline docs check --baseline <rev>' and 'outfeed gate --baseline <rev>' would report which findings are new since that revision, which is the only question an agent or a reviewer actually has. It would also make a red gate on main actionable ('this one is pre-existing, file it') instead of a guess.

task.title: storypole update should append to a description instead of requiring the whole text back
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06: recording progress on GB-204, OF-5 and GB-79 meant reading the full description with 'show --json', concatenating in python, and writing it back with --desc, four times. The description is the ticket's memory and it is now several kilobytes on GB-204, so every append re-sends the whole thing through the model's context - expensive, and one truncation away from destroying the history. A '--append-desc <TEXT>' (or '--desc-from -' reading stdin) would make the normal workflow one cheap call, and makes it impossible to lose the earlier text by accident.

task.title: Make miter verify the documented Tier 1 loop, since cargo check cannot finish inside an agent tool window
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06 across roughly twenty build invocations: every 'cargo check --workspace --all-targets' exceeded the 30s tool window and had to be backgrounded and polled, burning two or three turns per build. Tier 1 in AGENTS.md prescribes cargo check -p <crate>; miter verify already exists for exactly this shape of problem and returns sliced diagnostics with zero build scrollback. Worth doing: measure miter verify cold and warm against cargo check on a real crate, and if it wins, rewrite Tier 1 in AGENTS.md to name it, with cargo as the fallback. It also sidesteps the shared build-lock stall in GB-236 better than polling a log.

task.title: chalkline docs check should say which file and line produced a drift claim
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06 while chasing GB-247: the audit reported 'README missing documentation for CLI command scaffold' for the common repo, which has no binary. The finding was false, but the report gave no provenance, so finding the cause meant grepping the whole tree for 'scaffold' to discover it came from a clap test fixture at gaugeblock-inventory/src/tests.rs:95. A '--explain' (or a file:line column in the existing output) would turn that hunt into one line, and it pays off for true positives too: 'missing spec for boundary type X' should carry the declaration site, not just the name.

task.title: outfeed reserve check should read the crate names from the workspace instead of a hand-typed list
task.description: Observed 2026-11-06 while dogfooding OF-5: checking every name in the suite meant enumerating 51 crates with a shell loop and passing them as arguments, and the same list will be needed before every release. A '--from-workspace' (walk the member repositories' manifests and collect package names) or '--from-file <path>' turns the dogfood into one command, makes 'reserve check' the natural pre-release gate in outfeed's release pipeline, and removes the risk of checking a stale hand-maintained list while a new crate is quietly unpublished.

task.title: Add a standalone-build gate: every member must build with no harness path patches, from published crates only
task.description: Raised by the owner as a standing concern: 'individual tool use vs suite interoperability - both are important'. The layer gate protects interoperability (it forbids hidden coupling). NOTHING currently protects individual tool use, and the suite has already drifted: gaugeblock-workspace and gaugeblock-security are consumed by six member repositories and neither is published, so those members only build because the harness [patch.crates-io] table maps them to local paths. A checkout of sawhorse on its own cannot build. Measured 2026-11-06 against the crates.io API: of 51 package names, 5 are unpublished.\n\nShape: 'outfeed gate --standalone' (or miter) that, per member repository, resolves dependencies with the patch table disabled and fails when any dependency cannot be satisfied from the registry. It would have caught this drift the day the first unpublished dependency was introduced, and it is the guard that makes Law 2 (each repository compiles and is useful on its own) enforceable instead of aspirational. Cheapest implementation may be a cargo metadata pass with --offline and a temporary .cargo/config.toml that omits [patch.crates-io].

task.title: Migration alert should name what would migrate and where the conflict is, and must clear once applied
task.description:
Owner request 2026-11-06: the workbench reports 'migration needed for configs' without saying what or where. Today discover_migration (benchwork-core/src/migration/discovery.rs) only tests whether a legacy artifact EXISTS, so the banner is undismissable and uninformative.

REPRODUCED CONCRETELY: the harness root has .gaugeblock/docs.toml AND .gaugeblock/config.toml already contains the consolidated tables - so the migration has effectively been applied, yet the file was never removed and the alert still fires. Worse, the consolidated shape is nested one level too deep: config.toml carries [docs.docs.readme], [docs.docs.agents], [docs.policies] while the source docs.toml carried [docs.readme], [docs.agents], [policies]. Anything reading [docs.*] finds nothing, so the docs policy in config.toml is currently inert. That is filed separately; this ticket is the alert.

Shape: (1) for each pending item report source path, destination path, and the key-level diff - which tables or files would move and which keys already match; (2) mark an item ALREADY APPLIED when the destination already contains its content, and offer to drop the stale source; (3) surface conflicts explicitly, e.g. a key present in both with different values, naming both values; (4) make the state inspectable from the CLI ('benchwork migrate --dry-run --json') so an operator and an agent see the same thing the UI does.

task.title: Config consolidation wrote docs tables one level too deep, so [docs.docs.*] makes the docs policy in config.toml inert
task.description: Found 2026-11-06 while investigating the permanent migration banner (GB-255). .gaugeblock/config.toml contains [docs.docs.readme], [docs.docs.agents], [docs.docs.contributing], [docs.docs.architecture], [docs.docs.spec], [docs.docs.design], [docs.docs.roadmap], [docs.docs.changelog], [docs.docs.product] and [docs.policies]. The source .gaugeblock/docs.toml it came from contained [docs.readme], [docs.agents], ... and [policies] - one level shallower. So the consolidator nested the whole document under a 'docs' key instead of merging it into the existing [docs] table.\n\nConsequence: anything reading [docs.readme] from config.toml finds nothing and falls back to defaults, silently. The docs audit still passes only because it falls back to the file, and the file is what the migration banner wants removed - so acting on that banner would delete the only copy the readers can see. Verified by inspection of both files; the fix should also assert the round trip (consolidate, then read back the same values the source held) which is the test that would have caught it.

task.title: Claim leases expire but nothing returns the task to the backlog, so the board shows ghost work
task.description:
Reported by the owner 2026-11-06: the workbench showed GB-195 and GB-236 as in progress when nobody was working on them, and no ticket ever appeared to transition while work was happening.

Two distinct causes. (1) MISSING REAPER: AgentClaim carries a TTL and is_expired exists, and claim_task already allows a takeover of an expired lease, but nothing moved an InProgress task back to Ready when its holder stopped heartbeating. GB-195 and GB-236 had been InProgress with leases expired 128 and 131 hours. (2) PROCESS: work was verified without ever being claimed, so tickets went Ready -> Verified with no InProgress in between and the board never showed the work.

Fix for (1): 'storypole reap' plus --dry-run releases the lease (TaskReleased) and returns the task to Ready (StatusChanged with the expiry in the reason). Explicit command rather than a read side effect, because a status change is a ledger event and a read-only checkout must not fail. Verified on this workspace: dry-run named exactly GB-195 and GB-236, the run returned both, and benchwork capabilities then matched storypole ledger-reconcile exactly - archived 61, blocked 4, deferred 26, ready 18, triage 12, verified 164, and no inprogress bucket.

OUTSTANDING: no unit test covers the reaper yet - it was verified against the live ledger only. The next change here should add a temp-store test asserting that an expired claim yields TaskReleased then StatusChanged and a live one yields nothing.

Unit test for the reaper is still outstanding and recorded on the ticket.

Fixed in benchwork 07825e7 and the live config repaired in 057a2e7. consolidate_configs nested the whole docs.toml under the key 'docs' though its root already carried [docs.*] and [policies], producing [docs.docs.readme]; readers of [docs.readme] fell back to defaults silently and the policy in config.toml was inert. It now merges the legacy top-level tables in place with the destination winning, and sawhorse/.storypole keep their namespacing as tool-local documents. Three tests added, including the round trip (depth preserved, existing value wins, tool-local still namespaced). The live .gaugeblock/config.toml was renamed in place from [docs.docs.*] to [docs.*] and [docs.policies] to [policies], verified by parsing before and after; harness docs audit now 9 present, 0 missing, 0 drifted.

task.title: Archive emits a status change to a status that no longer exists, so the ledger's vocabulary contradicts GB-179
task.description:
Reported by the owner 2026-11-06 after archiving tickets from benchwork: the ledger records a status change on archive, but GB-179 decided archived is a STATE, not a status.

DIAGNOSIS - data is intact, the vocabulary is not. Measured on this workspace: 286 tasks, 0 of them with status='archived', and 128 with archived_at set. Archived tasks hold the status they earned (7 ready, 2 triage, 119 verified). So the projection is already doing the right thing: it reads StatusChanged{to: Archived} as 'stamp archived_at, keep the status'. Nothing is corrupted today.

But that is a special case in the replayer standing in for a missing event. Two latent hazards. (1) A consumer reading raw ledger events sees a status transition to a variant the model says is never a status, which is exactly what confused the owner. (2) Any replayer that does not know the special case - a new tool, a rewrite, a backfill - would materialise status='archived' with no archived_at, or fold those rows into status counts, which is the same class of bug as GB-211.

Same shape on the other side: unarchive emits StatusChanged{from: verified, to: verified} when the status never moved, purely to clear the state.

FIX SHAPE: add TaskArchived and TaskUnarchived to LedgerEvent (contracts), carrying the status that was in force; emit them from archive_task/unarchive_task; teach the projection to set and clear archived_at from them; keep reading the legacy StatusChanged{to: archived} shim indefinitely, because 128 historical events already exist and a replay must reproduce today's state exactly. The compiler will name every exhaustive match on LedgerEvent.

ACCEPTANCE: a fresh replay of the existing ledgers yields byte-identical state (0 rows with status='archived', 128 with archived_at); a new archive records TaskArchived and no StatusChanged; and a test asserts the legacy event still replays to the same state.

receipt.summary: Fixed in contracts d1197f5 and storypole 0bcf3b3. Archive emitted StatusChanged{to: Archived} - a transition to a variant GB-179 says is never a status - and unarchive emitted StatusChanged{from: verified, to: verified}, a transition that moved nothing. Both now emit TaskArchived (carrying the status the task keeps) and TaskUnarchived. The legacy StatusChanged{to: Archived} arm stays in the replayer forever, because 128 such events already exist. Verified by deleting the index and rebuilding it from the ledgers through the new code: archived 128/128 delta 0, verified 106, ready 12, deferred 26, triage 11, blocked 4, index and ledger agree, and zero rows with status='archived'. Tier 2 fmt/clippy clean, nextest 51/51. OUTSTANDING: no unit test yet pins the archive/unarchive round trip - verified by full replay only.

description:
SCOPE CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT: the plan says "~10 derivation sites spread across storypole plus chalkline, dado, joiner". Measured on 2026-10-30: 63 real path derivations (join/Path::new/PathBuf::from of ".gaugeblock") across 8 repositories - benchwork 14, storypole 9, miter 2, joiner 2, dado 2, sawhorse 1, outfeed 1, chalkline 1. A further 90 mentions are strings in docs, tests and literals, which are not derivations and must not be counted.

CONSEQUENCE: this is roughly six times the ticket estimate and should be sequenced by repository, not treated as a single pass. Benchwork alone is nearly a quarter of it.

DEPENDS ON GB-131: the whole point of the crate is resolving .gaugeblock from the git common dir rather than from the process working directory, because a worktree has a different working tree and the same common dir. gaugeblock-git steps 1-3 now provide exactly what that needs - Repository::discover, common_dir, is_worktree, and worktrees() - so this is unblocked on the read side.

PROGRESS 2026-11-06 (benchwork a543a78). AC3 - 'SuiteConfig is the only reader of .gaugeblock/config.toml and .env' - had zero adoption when measured today: SuiteConfig was used by nobody, WorkspaceTopology only inside common, and GaugeblockPaths was adopted by six repositories for path resolution only.

First consumer landed: benchwork-core. Its credential module deleted its own dotenv loop in favour of gaugeblock_workspace::env_credentials, and three hand-joined .gaugeblock paths became GaugeblockPaths::at (the .env in resolve_credential, the .env directory in persist_credential, the unified config in both the reader and the writer). Proof that it is behaviour-preserving rather than a rewrite: both parsers skip blanks and '#' comments, split on the same character, trim the key, strip the same quote characters and treat set-but-empty as absent. They agreed by coincidence, which is the duplicate-parser hazard the crate exists to remove.

Eight tests added, where the behaviour previously had none - including the round trip that matters, since persist_credential writes quoted values and the reader must strip them. Benchwork: fmt clean, clippy clean, nextest 43/43 (was 35), docs 9/0/0.

STILL OPEN for AC3: (1) benchwork's own [sawhorse] table interpretation still parses TOML itself via SawhorseConfig::load_from_path - correct by design, since the typed reading stays with the tool, but the *path* is now canonical; (2) outfeed-core and joiner-core each parse a [tool] table out of config.toml themselves, per common/ARCHITECTURE.md, and each has its own fallback ladder, so each is its own commit with its own tests; (3) WorkspaceTopology still has no consumer outside common - storypole's workspace store does its own member discovery, which is the next candidate slice; (4) the residual raw .gaugeblock derivation count needs re-measuring before AC3 can be called done.

SLICE 2 DONE 2026-11-06 (common 004ccb3, storypole 4b14140). WorkspaceTopology had no consumer outside common; storypole carried its own immediate-child scan. The scan now comes from the shared crate.

The interesting part is what did NOT happen: discover() hardcodes .git, and storypole legitimately accepts a member holding .storypole or Cargo.toml without being a checkout. Repointing blindly would have narrowed storypole's standalone behaviour and quietly returned zero members for a workspace of plain directories - the exact regression the owner asked to watch for. So the shared crate gained discover_with(rule) and storypole passes its own rule: the model is shared, the policy stays with the product. Hidden directories are now skipped for every rule.

Verified against the real workspace, not by inspection: 'workspace list' reports the same 11 members, prefixes and task counts before and after the change.

Tests: common 15/15 (was 11, four on the discovery rules), storypole 51/51 (was 49, five on member discovery - the first one pins the standalone guarantee). fmt and clippy clean on both, docs 9/0/0 on both.

task.title: Render a task's own pending decisions in the human briefing
task.description: Repro: from a repo with a decision-blocked task run ask-decision on it, then show it. The human output omits the pending decision entirely, while show --json carries it under task.decisions (status, category, proposed_options). Evidence: format_task_briefing renders inherited_decisions only, and there is no reference to .decisions anywhere in storypole-cli, so a task's own decision is never printed. Observed against AF-17 and AF-18 in the aerofoil backlog on storypole 0.1.0-beta.2 and still present on main at 09557e7.
acceptance_criteria: show KEY renders each own decision with status, category, question and proposed options; a pending decision is distinguishable from a resolved one; list marks a task that is blocked by a decision so the reason is not invisible
